data.title: Faster interpreters in Go: Catching up with C++
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Vitess数据库中的SQL评估引擎的演变和优化过程。最初，该引擎是一个直接对SQL抽象语法树（AST）进行操作的解释器。在过去一年中，团队用一个用Go语言编写的高效虚拟机（VM）替代了它，使其性能接近MySQL的C++评估代码。新的VM不仅更快，而且更易维护。Vitess的查询通过无状态的vtgate实例进行，这些实例负责解析SQL、制定分片感知查询计划并在多个MySQL实例上执行评估。对于无法直接在MySQL上执行的SQL表达式，Vitess评估引擎会在本地进行解释。该引擎支持大多数MySQL的标量表达式，并通过全面的测试和模糊测试确保其准确性和性能。尽管表达式看似简单，但实际工程中存在许多细微差别，因此评估速度必须尽可能快以避免额外开销。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用闭包和复制-修补技术优化解释器和虚拟机的不同方法及其优缺点

不同观点：
• MatthiasPortzel认为，使用Go编译器的闭包进行复制和修补技术可能成为未来创建新解释语言的主流方法，取代AST解释器、基于switch的字节码虚拟机和JIT编译。
• djwatson24指出，使用闭包进行代码生成的概念早在1987年就由Marc Feeley提出，这种方法在支持闭包的语言中效果显著，但速度可能不如基于LuaJIT的尾调用字节码虚拟机或基线JIT编译。
• cosmos0072分享了其在Go解释器中使用闭包优化的经验，如使用`nop`闭包优化执行流程，并提供了具体项目[gomacro]作为例子。
• brianolson提到，使用函数指针数组作为字节码解释器的模式早已有之，并分享了其在Algorand VM和玩具JVM中的实践经验，强调该模式的低开销和高效率。
• returningfory2质疑该技术的 memory usage（内存使用）是否理想，指出传统字节码编译器生成的是缓存友好的二进制数组，而闭包方法可能导致更多的堆分配。
• politician提议Go语言如果支持计算goto，将有助于构建直接线程化的解释器，提升性能。

补充讨论：
• hinkley提到编译查询时需要权衡正确性和速度，强调使用预处理语句的重要性。
• giovannibonetti对比了MySQL和Postgres的类型系统，认为更静态的类型系统可能在性能上更具优势。
• rockwotj引用了Cloudflare使用闭包构建解释器的案例，提供了另一个应用实例。
• medv分享了其在expr-lang.org上的研究，比较了不同VM实现，并提供了相关博客和论文链接。
• Thaxll认为这种VM实现与“基本”模拟器的工作方式非常相似。
• rajandatta对文章表示赞赏，认为展示了高性能解释器的发展趋势。
• kiitos的评论"vitess is not the answer"似乎与主要讨论主题无关。

争议焦点：
• 该技术的创新性及其实际应用效果。一些人认为这是旧概念的新应用，而另一些人则强调其在特定语言和场景下的优势。
• 内存使用和性能之间的权衡，特别是与传统字节码编译器相比的优劣。

Faster interpreters in Go: Catching up with C++
By
Vicent MartÃ­
|
March 20, 2025
The SQL evaluation engine that ships with Vitess,
the open-source database that powers PlanetScale
, was originally implemented as an AST evaluator that used to operate directly on the SQL AST generated by our parser. Over this past year, we've gradually replaced it with a Virtual Machine which, despite being written natively in Go, performs similarly to the original C++ evaluation code in MySQL. Most remarkably, the new Virtual Machine has repeatedly proven itself easier to maintain than the original Go interpreter, even though it's orders of magnitude faster. Let's review the implementation choices we've made to get these surprising results.
What's a SQL evaluation engine?
Vitess has been designed for unlimited horizontal scaling. To accomplish this, all queries to a Vitess cluster must go through a
vtgate
. Since you can deploy as many
vtgate
instances as you want, because theyâre essentially stateless, this allows you to grow the capacity of your cluster linearly.  The job of each gate is the most complex part of the whole distributed system. It parses the SQL of the incoming queries and creates a shard-aware query plan, which we evaluate in one or many of the shards of the cluster. Then, we aggregate the results of these evaluations, and return them to the user.
One of the reasons why Vitess works so well in practice (in both performance and in ease of adoption) is that every shard in a cluster is backed by a real MySQL instance. Even the more complex SQL queries can be decomposed into simpler statements that are evaluated in the underlying MySQL database. Hence, the results of these queries always match what youâd expect from querying MySQL directly.
However, SQL queries in the real world can get
really wild
. We need to support pretty much every kind of query that a normal MySQL instance supports, but we need to evaluate it across several MySQL instances. This means that sometimes, we donât get to fall back to MySQL to evaluate all our SQL expressions.
Think of a rather simple query such as this:
SELECT inventory.item_id, SUM(inventory.count), AVG(inventory.price) AS avg_price
FROM inventory
WHERE inventory.state = 'available' AND inventory.warehouse IN ?
GROUP BY inventory.item_id
HAVING  avg_price > 100;
Assuming this query is executed in a sharded Vitess cluster, the inventoried items can exist in any of the shards. Hence, our query planner will prepare a plan that queries all shards in parallel,
pushing down part of the aggregation to MySQL
, and then we'll perform the aggregations (
SUM
and
AVG
) locally in the
vtgate
. The
state
and
warehouse
checks in the
WHERE
clause can and will be executed directly on the MySQL instance that powers each shard. But the last expression,
avg_price > 100
, applies to the result of the aggregation, which is only available inside Vitess. This is where the Vitess evaluation engine comes in.
Our evaluation engine is an interpreter that supports the majority of the scalar expressions in the SQL dialect used by MySQL. This does not include high level constructs such as performing a
JOIN
,  the grouping of a
GROUP BY
, etc (these are performed directly by the planner, as weâve seen), but the actual sub-expressions that youâd see as the condition of a
WHERE
clause, or a
GROUP BY
clause. Any piece of SQL that cannot be lowered to be executed in MySQL by the planner is evaluated locally in Go by the engine.
Of course, these SQL sub-expressions are not arbitrarily complex. They are not even Turing complete (as they cannot loop!), so you may think that a statement like
avg_price > ?
would be trivial to evaluate, but as in most engineering problems, thereâs a wealth of nuance when doing these things in the real world.
SQL is an incredibly dynamic language full of quirks, and the SQL in MySQL, doubly so. We have spent an inordinate amount of time getting every single corner case of SQL evaluation to match exactly MySQLâs behavior. In fact, our
test
suite
and
fuzzer
are so comprehensive that we routinely find bugs in the original MySQL evaluation engine, which we have to fix upstream (
like this collation bug
,
this issue in the
insert
SQL function
or
this bug when searching substrings
). Nonetheless, being fully accurate is not enough. For most queries, these expressions are evaluated once or even more than once
for every returned row
, so in order to not introduce additional overhead, evaluation needs to be as quick as possible.

data.title: Non-US-based alternatives to popular services
data.author: realty_geek
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由社区策划的非美国隐私保护服务的推荐列表，旨在减少对美国科技巨头和监控网络的依赖。文章指出，使用美国服务可能导致数据被政府获取，且五眼联盟国家可以共享数据。即使是非美国服务，若与美国有业务关联，也可能被迫交出数据。文章强调大数据公司常跟踪、 monetize 和监视用户，因此推荐独立、透明且尊重用户隐私的替代服务。列表涵盖电子邮件、搜索引擎、云存储、消息应用、社交媒体等多个类别，并鼓励社区贡献和审核服务。最终目标是精简列表，只保留真正独立于五眼监控网络的服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕非美国技术服务及其替代方案的可行性和安全性讨论

不同观点：
• remram认为，该网站与之前提交过的"European Alternatives"网站相似，暗示可能存在重复性。
• pjmlp提出，除了非美国的服务，我们可能还需要非美国主导的编程语言和操作系统来支持这些服务。
• amazingamazing对非美国替代方案的具体例子表示疑问，询问了实际的替代网站。
• nixgeek指出，如果担心国家级情报机构的监控，那么任何现有的措施可能都无法完全保护数据，引用James Mickens的演讲来说明即使是复杂的保护也可能无法阻止国家层级的攻击。
• joemazerino质疑是否有人认为欧盟的间谍机构不会进行监控，暗示所有大国都会进行某种形式的监控。
• dangus认为，尽管支持寻找替代方案，但该网站的呈现方式存在缺陷，特别是通过吓人的内容引导用户选择产品不妥。他还指出，某些列出的替代服务本身也有问题，例如GDPR的适用范围以及一些服务在中国有办公室等。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是国家级情报机构的监控普遍性，以及用户是否能通过选择非美国服务来有效保护自己的数据。
• dangus特别提到，GDPR虽然被视为隐私保护的典范，但它适用于所有在欧盟运营的公司，包括美国公司，因此不能作为选择替代服务的唯一标准。
• 某些替代服务如Opera和Deepseek在中国有办公室，可能对一些担心国家监控的人来说并不是一个好的选择。
• 一些列出的替代服务实际上仍有美国服务器或所有权，如Tidal，这与网站声称的非美国选择相矛盾。

Non-U.S. Alternatives List
A collectively curated list of non-US-based alternatives to popular services, because it is time to prioritise our privacy, security, and digital sovereignty.
🚨 Did You Know?
🚩
If you use a US-based service, your private data is NOT yours.
🚩
The US PATRIOT Act
lets the government
access your data WITHOUT your consent
—no warrant needed. Yes, even if you're not American.
🚩
The Five Eyes Alliance (US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand)
means that if
one country gets your data, they ALL get it.
Your info can be passed around intelligence agencies
without you knowing.
🚩
Even if you use a non-US service, you’re NOT safe.
If the company has
servers, offices, or employees in the US,
it can be legally forced to
hand over your data to the US government.
🚩
Big Tech is NOT your friend.
Companies like Google, Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon
comply with these laws
and
give your info to intelligence agencies on request.
🚩
Once your data is in their hands, it NEVER disappears.
Even
deleted files, old emails, and private messages
can be
stored, recovered, and used against you.
📌 Why This List Matters
Big Tech monopolies track, monetize, spy on us and control our digital lives
. Now, it's more important than ever to
seek independent alternatives
that respect user rights.
This list aims to:
✔️
Promote data privacy.
While not every service on this list is entirely free from international surveillance networks (
Five Eyes, Nine Eyes, 14 Eyes, PRISM, FISA, etc.
), our mission is to promote alternatives that reduce dependency on them and enhance user privacy. Over time, we aim to refine this list, keeping only the safest and most secure services.
✔️
Reduce reliance on U.S. Big Tech & surveillance-heavy platforms.
✔️
Promote services that respect user privacy better than their mainstream counterparts.
✔️
Encourage transparency by allowing the community to vet and flag questionable alternatives.
✔️
Encourage global accessibility by promoting platforms available to users worldwide without geopolitical restrictions.
✔️
Break free from corporate monopolies that push anti-competitive policies and exploit user data.
📌 Contributing & Vetting
This list is a
community-driven effort
and we encourage:
✔
Contributions
– If you know of a service that fits, submit it!
✔
Verification
– If a service
claims
to be privacy-friendly but has questionable policies, leave a comment for discussion.
✔
Transparency
– If an entry is
funded by or connected to US interests
, flag it for review.
✔
Continuous Improvement
:
The MAIN GOAL is to refine and shorten this list, prioritizing
‼️
ONLY
‼️
services that are truly independent from Five Eyes & similar surveillance networks.

data.article_summary: 本文解释了为何一些用户在访问Wandering Thoughts博客或CSpace时被阻挡。原因是作者的反爬虫措施自动屏蔽了使用过旧浏览器（尤其是旧版Chrome）的访问者，以应对2025年初大量使用旧浏览器用户代理的高流量爬虫（部分用于LLM训练数据收集）。如果用户确实在使用最新浏览器却仍被阻挡，可以联系作者提供浏览器信息以解决问题。此外，文章特别提到archive.*（如archive.today等）的爬取行为类似恶意爬虫，建议使用更为规范的archive.org进行存档。作者是Chris Siebenmann，2025年2月17日发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SSH配置文件的处理规则及其相关问题，包括配置文件的优先级、安全性、文件命名和排序等技术细节。

不同观点：
• [egberts1] 认为SSH客户端配置应让用户拥有控制权，并介绍了多文件配置的层次结构，包括默认用户、系统范围和特定用户的配置。他还提供了关于SSH和SSHD选项的详细解析和文档链接。
• [0xbadcafebee] 指出不同工具对配置文件的解析方式各异，假设一致可能导致安全漏洞。
• [wruza] 主张直接替换sshd_config文件以避免不同VPS主机模板带来的潜在访问问题，而不是通过打补丁来修复。
• [eadmund] 对"first-wins"规则表示惊讶，认为设计这样的解析器需要额外的工作，并质疑这种设计的原因。
• [drpixie] 提供了一个实用的SSHD选项(-T)来检查实际的配置情况。
• [eapriv] 强调配置文件的顺序很重要，因此文件名中包含数字。
• [samlinnfer] 提到之前曾对文档更新提出过意见，并提供了相关链接。
• [noufalibrahim] 遇到了SSH与keycloak通过PAM脚本认证的问题，并表示两者不易配合使用。
• [jmclnx] 对"/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/"目录的存在表示疑惑，认为这可能是Linux特有的新事物，而在OpenBSD和Slackware上并不存在。
• [czernobog] 对配置文件的"first-wins"规则感到有趣，并询问为何配置文件需要以数字命名。
• [NikkiA] 和 [barotalomey] 解释了*.d目录中使用数字命名是为了排序，这是一种常见的配置方案传统。
• [therein] 对cloudinit持怀疑态度，认为其常带来问题而非解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 配置文件的命名和排序规则（数字命名的原因和传统）。
• 不同操作系统中SSH配置文件处理方式的差异。
• cloudinit工具在实际应用中的问题和争议。
• PAM与SSH在第三方认证集成中的兼容性问题。

43573507.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: QVQ-Max: Think with Evidence
data.author: wertyk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了QVQ-Max，这是一个新发布的视觉推理模型，能够“理解”和分析图像、视频内容，并基于这些信息进行推理和解决问题。模型不仅能处理数学、编程等问题，还能应用于设计、创作等领域。QVQ-Max的核心能力包括细节观察、深度推理和灵活应用，可用于工作、学习和日常生活等场景，如数据分析、解决数学问题、推荐穿搭等。尽管当前版本是初步的，但其潜力显著，未来将通过提高识别准确性、增强多步骤任务处理能力和优化交互方式来进一步改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于新发布的多模态大语言模型（QVQ-Max等）的性能、应用及相关背景的讨论

不同观点：
• [mcbuilder] 认为该模型在编码任务上优于LLaMA 4 Maverick，表示这是旧新闻，但性能更好。
• [torginus] 对模型在周末发布表示疑问，推测AI领域的竞争是否非常激烈。
• [Alifatisk] 分享了之前使用QVQ时遇到的无限推理循环问题，并表示期待尝试QVQ-Max，对模型理解和推理图像的能力感到惊叹。
• [xpe] 指出关于页面没有透露核心团队的组成及收入来源，对此表示疑惑。
• [8ibzjj] 简单表达了对某方面的不解或不满，但没有详细阐述。
• [AbuAssar] 幽默地指出即使是聪明人，命名也是件难事。
• [ttul] 认为该模型似乎是首个使用"思考 tokens"的多模态LLM，表示新颖。
• [unixhero] 关心如何在本地运行该模型，关注实用性。
• [gatienboquet] 质疑模型的图像模式"思考"功能是否与ChatGPT 4o的图像生成类似。
• [drapado] 对该模型没有开放权重表示失望。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到模型的性能比较（如与LLaMA 4 Maverick的对比）、技术细节（如"思考 tokens"和图像理解）、团队和资金透明性、实用性（如何在本地运行）以及对开放权重的期待与失望。
• 争议的焦点包括模型发布时间的巧合、性能的真实优势以及技术实现的独特性。

43570676.article_content:

Introduction
#
Last December, we launched QVQ-72B-Preview as an exploratory model, but it had many issues. Today, we are officially releasing the first version of QVQ-Max, our visual reasoning model. This model can not only “understand” the content in images and videos but also analyze and reason with this information to provide solutions. From math problems to everyday questions, from programming code to artistic creation, QVQ-Max has demonstrated impressive capabilities. Though this is just our first version, its potential is already eye-catching.
MathVision is a benchmark that aggregates various challenging multimodal mathematical problems, and we evaluate a model’s ability to solve complex math problems based on its performance on this benchmark. As shown in the figure, by adjusting the maximum length of the model’s thinking process, we observe a continuous improvement in the model’s accuracy on MathVision, demonstrating the immense potential of the model.
In the following sections, we will discuss the design philosophy behind QVQ-Max, its actual capabilities, and what it can do for you.
Why Do We Need Visual Reasoning?
#
Traditional AI models mostly rely on text input, such as answering questions, writing articles, or generating code. However, in real life, much of the information isn’t expressed through words but rather through images, charts, or even videos. A single image can contain rich details like colors, shapes, spatial relationships, and more. These elements are often more intuitive, but also more complex than text.
For example, if you want to determine whether an architectural blueprint is reasonable, a description alone might not be enough. But if you could see the blueprint and analyze it using professional knowledge, the task becomes much easier. This is the significance of visual reasoning—it allows AI to not just “see,” but also “understand” and “think.”
Our goal in designing QVQ-Max was simple: to create an assistant that is both “sharp-eyed” and “quick-thinking,” capable of solving various practical problems for users.
Core Capabilities: From Observation to Reasoning
#
The capabilities of QVQ-Max can be summarized into three areas: detailed observation, deep reasoning, and flexible application. Let’s break down how it performs in each area.
Detailed Observation: Capturing Every Detail
QVQ-Max excels at parsing images, whether they’re complex charts or casual snapshots taken in daily life. It can quickly identify key elements in an image. For instance, it can tell you what objects are in a photo, what textual labels exist, and even point out small details that you might overlook.
Deep Reasoning: Not Just “Seeing,” But Also “Thinking”
Identifying content in an image is not enough. QVQ-Max can further analyze this information and combine it with background knowledge to draw conclusions. For example, in a geometry problem, it can derive answers based on the accompanying diagram. In a video clip, it can predict what might happen next based on the current scene.
Flexible Application: From Problem-Solving to Creation
Beyond analysis and reasoning, QVQ-Max can also perform interesting tasks like helping you design illustrations, generate short video scripts, or even create role-playing content based on your requirements. If you upload a rough sketch, it might help you refine it into a complete piece. Upload a regular photo, and it can transform into a sharp critic or even a fortune-teller.
Demo Cases
#
QVQ-Max has a wide range of applications, whether in learning, work, or daily life—it can come in handy in many scenarios.
Workplace Tool
: At work, QVQ-Max can assist in completing data analysis, organizing information, and even writing code
Learning Assistant
: For students, QVQ-Max can help solve difficult problems in subjects like math and physics, especially those accompanied by diagrams. It can also explain complex concepts in an intuitive way, making learning easier.
Life Helper
: In daily life, QVQ-Max can offer practical advice. For instance, it can recommend outfit combinations based on photos of your wardrobe, or guide you through cooking a new dish based on recipe images.
Multi-image Recognition

Next Step
#
The current version of QVQ-Max is just the first iteration, and there’s still much room for improvement. Moving forward, we will focus on several key areas:
More Accurate Observations
: Enhance recognition accuracy through grounding techniques, which validate observations made from visual content.
Visual Agent
: Improve the model’s ability to handle multi-step and more complex tasks, such as operating smartphones or computers, and even playing games.
Better Interaction
: Expand beyond text-based interaction

data.title: Show HN: LocalScore – Local LLM Benchmark
data.author: sipjca
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何下载和运行LocalScore工具的两种方法。用户可以选择使用官方模型或自己的.gguf模型。根据操作系统（MacOS/Linux或Windows），用户需在终端或命令行中执行不同命令来运行LocalScore。官方模型根据大小（Tiny、Small、Medium）有不同的内存要求，范围从2GB到10GB。文章还提供了具体操作命令示例，以及解决问题的指南和文档链接。如遇困难，用户可以参考故障排除指南或查看相关视频。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 localscore.ai 项目的功能、可信度、技术细节及未来发展方向的讨论。

不同观点：
• **项目的可信度存疑**：david_draco 对 localscore.ai 是否与 Mozilla 真正相关表示怀疑，因为在 Mozilla Builders 项目页面中找不到该项目，且没有明确的方式验证其关联性。
• **技术改进建议**：zamadatix 指出项目在 Windows 系统上运行时缺少对 Nvidia GPU 或 AMD GPU 的安装提示，且当前的基准测试程序默认使用 CPU 模式，可能导致用户误解性能表现，建议添加警告提示。此外，zamadatix 还提到该项目在 GPU 运行时速度较慢，相较于其他工具表现不佳。
• **隐私与性能需求**：mentalgear 对项目的隐私性表示关注，建议增加匿名联邦评分共享功能，使用户可以在不下载模型的情况下评估其性能。此外，mentalgear 认为需要更多可比较且可信的 AI 基准测试。
• **模型大小与性能优化**：chrismorgan 对项目文件的大小膨胀表示不满，尤其是 llamafile 的大小增长过快。他提出是否可以采用合成模型的方式来减少文件体积，同时对文件大小波动的原因表示好奇。
• **硬件推荐与商业模式**：FloatArtifact 提出基于用户提交的基准数据，网站可以生成符合性能要求的硬件推荐列表，并通过关联链接进行硬件销售获利，类似于 PC 装机推荐网站的模式。
• **用户体验与功能扩展**：omneity 对项目的功能限制表示关注，尤其是对远程无头服务器和多种 LLM 运行方式的支持不足，建议增加 API 连接方式以增强灵活性。
• **许可证选择**：gunalx 对项目中使用 llama 和 qwen 组合模型表示疑问，认为如果仅使用更宽松许可的 qwen 模型可能会更好。

补充讨论：
• **支持与鼓励**：TheFlyingPanda 和 jborichevskiy 对项目发布表示祝贺，并对收集公开数据集的努力表示肯定。jborichevskiy 还提到在没有专用 GPU 的情况下运行 24B 模型的可行性。
• **冷启动与隐私问题**：ftbsqcfjm 关注新用户的冷启动问题以及平台如何处理隐私问题，并建议与本地企业合作以增强数据。
• **边缘设备的适用性**：sharmasachin98 对项目在边缘设备上的表现表示关注，并计划亲自尝试。
• **用户界面改进建议**：alchemist1e9 建议在项目主页上增加更直观的 GPU 可视化展示，类似于 cpubenchmark.net 的做法，以提升用户体验。

争议焦点：
• 项目的可信度与 Mozilla 的关联性是主要争议点，david_draco 对项目是否真正与 Mozilla 相关表示怀疑。
• 技术性能方面，zamadatix 与其他用户对 localscore.ai 在 GPU 上的表现存在争议，认为其速度较慢。
• 文件大小与性能优化的平衡是另一个争议点，chrismorgan 对文件体积膨胀表示不满，并提出合成模型的可行性。

• **项目的可信度存疑**：david_draco 对 localscore.ai 是否与 Mozilla 真正相关表示怀疑，因为在 Mozilla Builders 项目页面中找不到该项目，且没有明确的方式验证其关联性。
• **技术改进建议**：zamadatix 指出项目在 Windows 系统上运行时缺少对 Nvidia GPU 或 AMD GPU 的安装提示，且当前的基准测试程序默认使用 CPU 模式，可能导致用户误解性能表现，建议添加警告提示。此外，zamadatix 还提到该项目在 GPU 运行时速度较慢，相较于其他工具表现不佳。
• **隐私与性能需求**：mentalgear 对项目的隐私性表示关注，建议增加匿名联邦评分共享功能，使用户可以在不下载模型的情况下评估其性能。此外，mentalgear 认为需要更多可比较且可信的 AI 基准测试。
• **模型大小与性能优化**：chrismorgan 对项目文件的大小膨胀表示不满，尤其是 llamafile 的大小增长过快。他提出是否可以采用合成模型的方式来减少文件体积，同时对文件大小波动的原因表示好奇。
• **硬件推荐与商业模式**：FloatArtifact 提出基于用户提交的基准数据，网站可以生成符合性能要求的硬件推荐列表，并通过关联链接进行硬件销售获利，类似于 PC 装机推荐网站的模式。
• **用户体验与功能扩展**：omneity 对项目的功能限制表示关注，尤其是对远程无头服务器和多种 LLM 运行方式的支持不足，建议增加 API 连接方式以增强灵活性。
• **许可证选择**：gunalx 对项目中使用 llama 和 qwen 组合模型表示疑问，认为如果仅使用更宽松许可的 qwen 模型可能会更好。

补充讨论：
• **支持与鼓励**：TheFlyingPanda 和 jborichevskiy 对项目发布表示祝贺，并对收集公开数据集的努力表示肯定。jborichevskiy 还提到在没有专用 GPU 的情况下运行 24B 模型的可行性。
• **冷启动与隐私问题**：ftbsqcfjm 关注新用户的冷启动问题以及平台如何处理隐私问题，并建议与本地企业合作以增强数据。
• **边缘设备的适用性**：sharmasachin98 对项目在边缘设备上的表现表示关注，并计划亲自尝试。
• **用户界面改进建议**：alchemist1e9 建议在项目主页上增加更直观的 GPU 可视化展示，类似于 cpubenchmark.net 的做法，以提升用户体验。

争议焦点：
• 项目的可信度与 Mozilla 的关联性是主要争议点，david_draco 对项目是否真正与 Mozilla 相关表示怀疑。
• 技术性能方面，zamadatix 与其他用户对 localscore.ai 在 GPU 上的表现存在争议，认为其速度较慢。
• 文件大小与性能优化的平衡是另一个争议点，chrismorgan 对文件体积膨胀表示不满，并提出合成模型的可行性。

data.title: Neutron Stars Hint at Another Dimension
data.author: dnetesn
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了19世纪中期以来对额外维度概念的科学探索。起初，这个想法与灵性和超自然现象联系在一起，但像数学家查尔斯·辛顿等人试图通过模型来理解这些维度，例如他的“四维立方体”（tesseract）。随着时间推移，科学与灵性分道扬镳，但对额外维度的研究愈加深入。现代物理学家通过研究重力异常弱的现象，提出了“膜世界”（braneworld）假说，认为我们的宇宙是一个三维的“膜”，嵌在一个拥有额外空间维度的“体”（bulk）中。这种模型试图解释为何重力比其他基本力弱得多，并设想通过研究中子星等天体来探测这些额外维度。文章强调了科学界对探索这些未知领域的好奇心和努力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对引力在多维空间中的表现及其弱性的讨论

不同观点：
• [the__alchemist] 认为引力在多维空间（bulk）中扩展，导致其在三维空间中显得很弱，但提出这种解释可能更适合弱力而非引力。他还指出，反平方定律是三维几何的内在属性，而不是维度的推断依据。
• [amai] 批评了引入额外维度的理论，认为这是在没有物理对称或理由的情况下增加参数空间，可能导致过度拟合数据，而非真正理解自然。
• [whatever1] 提出假设，如果引力在3+ND中作用而在三维世界中观察，我们应该看到更多奇特的现象，而不仅仅是力度的变化。他使用二维物体在一维线上投影的类比来说明这一点。
• [codingdave] 提问是否暗物质可能来自“bulk”的交互作用，暗示了引力和暗物质之间可能的联系。
• [Ygg2] 认为引力的弱性可能只是自然现象，不一定需要解释为异常，尤其是在假设所有力曾经统一的前提下。

补充讨论：
• [p_ing] 分享了一个关于中子星的视频，虽然未直接参与讨论，但提供了额外的学习资源。
• [echelon] 质疑这些关于多维空间的理论是否基于单一研究者或实验室的工作，并询问外行如何判断一个新科学共识的形成。
• [pk-protect-ai] 对文章中模糊的提示和可能的假设持批评态度。
• [deadbabe] 提出是否可以通过高维空间的定位来实现反重力或人工重力，这涉及到了实际应用的问题。
• [johnea] 的评论带有政治色彩，未对科学内容做出实质性贡献。
• [EvgeniyZh] 简短回复反对[johnea]的观点，未展开讨论。

争议焦点：
• 引力在多维空间中的表现及其是否能解释其弱性是主要争议点。
• 引入额外维度的理论是否合理及其对理解自然现象的帮助。
• 判断新科学共识形成的标准及其可靠性。

Explore
I
n the mid 19th century, a strange idea was growing heavy in the ether: There might be dimensions beyond the three we experience. To some—including eminent scientists of the day—these were the realms of spirits and the supernatural, accessed through tabletop seances. To Charles Hinton, a British mathematician and science-fiction writer at the time, it was something that could be puzzled out, modeled in things like his “tesseract” four-dimensional cube.

In the intervening century and a half, spiritualism and mainstream science having parted ways, the serious search for these extra dimensions has only intensified. Lately, physicists have proposed a new way to “see” into a new dimension—by looking deep into the hearts of collapsed, dead stars that have been behaving strangely.
The concerted scientific journey into extra dimensions began with Hermann Minkowski, Einstein’s former teacher, who realized that “space by itself, and time by itself, have vanished into the merest shadows” and that only a unification of them, spacetime, exists. Spacetime means that the universe truly is four-dimensional, just that one of the dimensions is that of time, rather than an additional one of space. One extra dimension discovered.
But might there be more?

Beginning in the middle of the 20th century, scientists began to speculate that there might indeed be more to the universe. And that speculation was born from an unlikely source: the astounding weakness of gravity.
If the “braneworld” hypothesis is true, then we have no idea just how magnificent the universe is.
The force of gravity is weak. And not just a little bit weak. It’s so much weaker than the other three fundamental forces—electromagnetism and the strong and weak nuclear forces—that it’s almost impossible to provide analogies. Gravity could be a trillion trillion times stronger than it is, and it would still be the weakest of the forces by many orders of magnitude.
The origin of the strengths of the fundamental forces of nature remains an outstanding problem in physics. We don’t know why electromagnetism has the strength that it does, why the strong force is so strong, and why the weak force is so weak. But gravity sticks out like a sore thumb. All the other forces may be weaker or stronger than the others, but they’re at least in the same ballpark. Gravity isn’t even on the same planet.

The thinking goes that if we can understand why gravity is so especially weak, we might be able to use that as a way to discern why the other forces are so strong.
And maybe the answer lies in an extra dimension.
In 1999, theoretical physicists Lisa Randall and Raman Sundrum proposed a wild restructuring of the cosmos. In their model, what we call the universe is really a “brane”—a three-dimensional expansion of our usual conceptions of a membrane.
But our brane is not the entire universe. In their model, it’s embedded in something much larger, dubbed the “bulk.” The bulk has an extra spatial dimension, and our brane universe floats along inside of it like a piece of paper caught in the ocean currents. We can’t see the bulk, touch the bulk, experience the bulk, or otherwise interact with the bulk because our entire universe—all the particles and forces of nature—are restricted to life on the brane.
It stretches the mind in a way that’s almost a throwback to the early days of the search for an extra dimension—when, in 1884, Edwin Abbot published his satirical book
Flatland: A Romance of Many Dimensions
, in which geometric figures inhabit a
two-dimensional universe
that is rocked when a sphere, a three-dimensional object, intersects with their world.

The brane-bulk model is a speculative idea for sure, but a fun one. Like the beleaguered citizens of Flatland, if the “braneworld” hypothesis is true, then we have no idea just how magnificent the true extent of the universe is.
And so it’s worth finding ways to investigate whether this literally outside-the-box idea has any merit—to find if we can poke our heads into the fifth dimension. Physicists just need some way to pierce the veil of the brane and peer into the realm of the bulk. To try this, they have enlisted gravity.

data.title: Max severity RCE flaw discovered in widely used Apache Parquet
data.author: andy99
data.article_summary: 研究人员发现Apache Parquet存在一个最高严重级别的远程代码执行（RCE）漏洞（CVE-2025-30065，CVSS v4评分10.0），影响1.15.0及之前所有版本。该漏洞源于反序列化不可信数据，可能让攻击者通过特制的Parquet文件控制目标系统、窃取或修改数据、中断服务或植入勒索软件等恶意 payload。该漏洞已在1.15.1版本中修复。利用此漏洞需要诱导用户导入恶意文件，因此主要威胁来自外部来源的文件。广泛使用Parquet的大数据平台如Hadoop、AWS、Google和Azure，以及Netflix、Uber等公司受影响。建议用户尽快升级至1.15.1版本，并加强监控和验证文件安全性。目前尚未发现实际攻击，但风险极高。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apache Parquet Java库中的高危漏洞及其影响和意义

不同观点：
• **CVSS 10.0评分的意义**：[tptacek]认为CVSS 10.0的评分毫无意义，并指出高分未必代表严重性，举例Heartbleed的CVSS评分仅为7.5。[jtchang]同样质疑10.0的评分，认为除非直接接受Parquet格式文件，否则此漏洞影响不大，相比解析图像、XML、JSON、HTML、CSS的漏洞，Parquet漏洞影响较小。

• **漏洞的实际影响**：[g-mork]认为漏洞报告过于模糊，并将此漏洞描述为序列化bug，提供了一个GitHub对比链接。[3eb7988a1663]建议漏洞标题应更明确区分是解析器漏洞而非文件格式本身，以避免误解。[marginalia_nu]分享了自己迁移到简单柱状格式以避免该漏洞的经历，同时指出Apache Parquet曾给他带来很多问题，可能不适合其使用场景。

• **技术细节和PoC**：[formerly_proven]指出此漏洞是典型的Java反序列化RCE，能够实例化任意类。[ustad]关心Pandas是否受影响，因为其使用Parquet格式进行序列化/反序列化。[nikanj]抱怨CVSS评分的通胀问题，认为"最高严重性RCE"不再等同于"任何角色未经身份验证的RCE"，而是需要导入恶意文件才能利用。

补充讨论：
• **讽刺与幽默**：[lpapez]讽刺地预测Quake PAK文件将因携带恶意软件被宣布为高危漏洞。[rini17]幽默地指出不要自己写反序列化代码。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于CVSS 10.0评分的实际意义和该漏洞的严重性。部分评论者认为此漏洞被过度评分，实际影响有限，尤其是在与其他更常见的文件格式漏洞对比时。

43603091.article_content:
Max severity RCE flaw discovered in widely used Apache Parquet
By
Bill Toulas
April 3, 2025
05:29 PM
0
A maximum severity remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability has been discovered impacting all versions of Apache Parquet up to and including 1.15.0.
The problem stems from the deserialization of untrusted data that could allow attackers with specially crafted Parquet files to gain control of target systems, exfiltrate or modify data, disrupt services, or introduce dangerous payloads such as ransomware.
The vulnerability is tracked under
CVE-2025-30065
and has a CVSS v4 score of 10.0. The flaw was fixed with the release of Apache version 1.15.1.
It should be noted that to exploit this flaw, threat actors must convince someone to import a specially crafted Parquet file.
Severe threat to "big data" environments
Apache Parquet is an open-source, columnar storage format designed for efficient data processing. Unlike row-based formats (like CSV), Parquet stores data by columns, which makes it faster and more space-efficient for analytical workloads.
It is widely adopted across the data engineering and analytics ecosystem, including big data platforms like Hadoop, AWS, Amazon, Google, and Azure cloud services, data lakes, and ETL tools.
Some large companies that use Parquet include Netflix, Uber, Airbnb, and LinkedIn.
The security problem in Parquet was disclosed on April 1, 2025, following a responsible disclosure by its finder, Amazon researcher Keyi Li.
"Schema parsing in the parquet-avro module of Apache Parquet 1.15.0 and previous versions allows bad actors to execute arbitrary code," warned the short
bulletin published on Openwall
.
"Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.15.1, which fixes the issue."
A separate bulletin by Endor Labs highlights the risk of CVE-2025-30065 exploitation more clearly, warning that the flaw can impact any data pipelines and analytics systems that import Parquet files, with the risk being significant for files sourced from external points.
Endor Labs believes the problem was introduced in Parquet version 1.8.0, though older releases might also be impacted. The firm suggests coordinated checks with developers and vendors to determine what Praquet versions are used in production software stacks.
"If an attacker tricks a vulnerable system into reading a specially crafted Parquet file, they could gain remote code execution (RCE) on that system,"
warns Endor Labs
.
However, the security firm avoids over-inflating the risk by including the note, "Despite the frightening potential, it's important to note that the vulnerability can only be exploited if a malicious Parquet file is imported."
That being said, if upgrading to Apache Parquet 1.15.1 immediately is impossible, it is suggested to avoid untrusted Parquet files or carefully validate their safety before processing them. Also, monitoring and logging on systems that handle Parquet processing should be increased.
Although no active exploitation has been discovered yet, the risk is high due to the flaw's severity and the widespread use of Parquet files in big data applications.
Administrators of impacted systems are recommended to upgrade to Parquet version 1.15.1, which addresses CVE-2025-30065, as soon as possible.

• 争议的焦点在于CVSS 10.0评分的实际意义和该漏洞的严重性。部分评论者认为此漏洞被过度评分，实际影响有限，尤其是在与其他更常见的文件格式漏洞对比时。

data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 美国密歇根大学工程师开发了一种改进的电动车电池制造工艺，能够在寒冷天气下实现高效快速充电，解决了许多潜在买家对电动车在低温下充电效率低、续航不足的担忧。该方法通过在电极上增加微米级通道和纳米级玻璃涂层，防止锂离子电池在低温下形成阻碍性能的锂镀层，从而使电池在-10°C下充电速度提高500%。这种技术不仅加快了充电速度，还保持了电池的能量密度，在快速充电100次后仍能保持97%的容量。该方法有望在现有工厂无需大规模改造的情况下被采用，解决了快速充电、低温性能和长续航之间的矛盾。

Charging electric vehicles 5x faster in subfreezing temps
Published On:
April 1, 2025
Contact:
Jim Lynch
Social Media:
Share on:
Share on Twitter
Share on Facebook
Share on LinkedIn
A stabilizing coating on an electrode, combined with microscale channels, helps solve the trade-off between range and charging speed, even in cold temperatures
Engineering student Chloe Acosta plugs in an EV for charging in snowy weather on the University of Michigan’s North Campus. EV charging becomes less efficient in colder weather, but a new strategy for manufacturing battery electrodes could enable charging in 10 minutes in temperatures as cold as -10C. Image credit: Marcin Szczepanski, Michigan Engineering
Study:
Enabling 6C fast charging of Li-ion batteries at sub-zero temperature via interface engineering and 3D architectures
(DOI: 10.1016/j.joule.2025.101881)
A modified manufacturing process for electric vehicle batteries, developed by University of Michigan engineers, could enable high ranges and fast charging in cold weather, solving problems that are turning potential EV buyers away.
“We envision this approach as something that EV battery manufacturers could adopt without major changes to existing factories,” said
Neil Dasgupta
, U-M associate professor of mechanical engineering and materials science and engineering, and corresponding author of the study published in Joule.
Neil Dasgupta
“For the first time, we’ve shown a pathway to simultaneously achieve extreme fast charging at low temperatures, without sacrificing the energy density of the lithium-ion battery.”
Lithium-ion EV batteries made this way can charge 500% faster at temperatures as low as 14 F (-10 C). The structure and coating demonstrated by the team prevented the formation of performance-hindering lithium plating on the battery’s electrodes. As a result, batteries with these modifications keep 97% of their capacity even after being fast-charged 100 times at very cold temperatures.
Current EV batteries store and release power through the movement of lithium ions back and forth between electrodes via a liquid electrolyte. In cold temperatures, this movement of the ions slows, reducing both battery power as well as the charging rate.
To extend range, automakers have increased the thickness of the electrodes they use in battery cells. While that has allowed them to promise longer drives between charges, it makes some of the lithium hard to access, resulting in slower charging and less power for a given battery weight.
Previously, Dasgupta’s team improved battery charging capability by
creating pathways—roughly 40 microns in size—in the anode
, the electrode that receives lithium ions during charging. Drilling through the graphite by blasting it with lasers enabled the lithium ions to find places to lodge faster, even deep within the electrode, ensuring more uniform charging.
This sped up room-temperature charging significantly, but cold charging was still inefficient. The team identified the problem: the chemical layer that forms on the surface of the electrode from reacting with the electrolyte. Dasgupta compares this behavior to butter: you can get a knife through it whether it’s warm or cold, but it’s a lot harder when it’s cold. If you try to fast charge through that layer, lithium metal will build up on the anode like a traffic jam.
“That plating prevents the entire electrode from being charged, once again reducing the battery’s energy capacity,” Manoj Jangid, U-M senior research fellow in mechanical engineering, and co-author of the study.
The team needed to prevent that surface layer from forming. They did this by coating the battery with a glassy material made of lithium borate-carbonate, approximately 20 nanometers thick. The addition of this coating sped up cold charging significantly, and when combined with the channels, the team’s test cells were 500% faster to charge in subfreezing temperatures.
“By the synergy between the 3-D architectures and artificial interface, this work can simultaneously address the trilemma of fast charging at low temperature for long-range driving,” said Tae Cho, a recent Ph.D. graduate in mechanical engineering and first author of the study.
In the past two decades, EVs have become more commonplace on roadways as consumers look for better environmental options, but
AAA survey results
showed that the momentum is hard to maintain. From 2023 to 2024, the number of U.S. adults who would be “likely” or “very likely” to buy a new or used EV dropped from 23% to 18%.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby on Rails（RoR）的演变、编程语言和框架的未来发展、以及AI在编程中的应用

不同观点：
• [thunder-blue-3] 对Ruby库名称的喜爱，尤其是对factory_girl重命名为factory_bot表示遗憾。这一评论更多是个人对RoR生态中工具变化的情感反应。
• [siva7] 对JavaScript框架频繁更新的批评，认为开发者通过过度复杂化自己的工作而使工作变得冗余，既愚蠢又天才。这一观点带有对行业现状的反思和讽刺。
• [999900000999] 提出理想编程语言的三层次结构：LLM "代码"（面向普通用户）、脚本语言（如Python，面向95%的用例）、以及系统编程语言（如Zig、Rust，面向高性能需求）。这一观点展望了编程语言的未来整合方向。
• [bnchrch] 认为基于意图的页面（intent-based pages）可能是下一个技术范式，类似于A/B测试的自然进化。但也指出目前还缺少一些关键要素，尚未完全实现这一未来。
• [Alifatisk] 认为目前已经到达Web开发的顶峰，表达了对行业未来发展的某种“巅峰”感受。
• [Stwerner] 作为文章作者，表示愿意回答问题或讨论背后的想法，更多是一个开放讨论的姿态。
• [blonky] 将讨论内容与已故知名开发者_why the lucky stiff的风格联系起来，表达了对创意编程文化的怀念。
• [dunefox] 对使用不可靠或具有欺骗性名称的框架表示质疑，反映出对框架命名和可靠性的关注。
• [jollyjerry] 将自然语言作为源代码的概念与Cucumber测试框架联系起来，指出了测试工具中已有类似实践。
• [siliconc0w] 分享了使用AI进行CRUD应用开发的实验，指出虽然目前存在速度和可靠性问题，但未来可能成为SaaS应用中聊天界面的补充。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：编程语言和框架的频繁变化是否使开发者工作变得冗余，以及AI在编程中的实际应用效果。
• 不同评论对未来的展望：有人认为已经到达顶峰，有人则认为还有未实现的创新。
• 对工具和框架命名的情感反应和实用性讨论。

data.title: montasaurus/result: A simple Rust-like Result type for Python 3
data.author: networked
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为`result`的Python库，灵感来源于Rust的`Result`类型，用于处理可能成功或失败的操作。该库提供了两种结果类型：`Ok`表示成功并包含返回值，`Err`表示失败并包含错误信息。通过类型注解，开发者可以清晰区分成功和失败的情况。库中包含如`is_ok`、`is_err`等函数来检查结果类型，并可以直接访问成功值（`ok_value`）或错误值（`err_value`）。此外，还支持使用Python 3.10的`match`语句进行模式匹配。该库简化了错误处理，避免使用自定义异常，并提供了自动生成的API文档。注意，该库是实验性的，使用时需自行承担风险。

About this repository
This is the source code of TinyWall as found at its
website
. Upstream development is now largely inactive, but this repository is provided for anyone who would like to submit their own improvements or fork the project.
How to build
Necessary tools
Microsoft Visual Studio 2019 or 2022
Wix v3.14 Toolset
Visual Studio extension for Wix v3 Toolset
To build the application
Open the solution file in Visual Studio and compile the
TinyWall
project. The other projects referenced inside the solution need not be compiled separately as they will be statically compiled into the application.
Done.
To update/build build the database of known applications
Adjust the individual JSON files in the
TinyWall\Database
folder.
Start the application with the
/develtool
flag.
Use the
Database creator
tab to create one combined database file in JSON format. The output file will be called
profiles.json
.
To use the new database in debug builds, copy the output file to the
TinyWall\bin\Debug
folder.
Done.
To build the installer
Copy the compiled application files and all dependencies into the
MsiSetup\Sources\ProgramFiles\TinyWall
folder.
Update the files as necessary inside the
MsiSetup\Sources\CommonAppData\TinyWall
folder. See instructions above about creating the database.
Open the solution file in Visual Studio and compile the
MsiSetup
project.
Done.
Contributing
Please don't open issues for feature requests or bug reports. Any changes you'd like you will need to implement yourself. If you have improvements that you would like to integrate into TinyWall, please fork the repo and create a pull request.
Fork the Project
Create your Feature Branch (
git checkout -b feature/AmazingFeature
)
Commit your Changes (

)

Open a Pull Request
For complex features or large changes, please contact me first if your changes are still within the scope of the application.
If you prefer that, you can also build and distribute your own version of the binaries. In this case though you need to choose a different name other than TinyWall for your application.

data.title: Baby Steps into Genetic Programming
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者使用Common Lisp进行遗传编程（Genetic Programming, GP）的初步探索，目标是通过进化算法找到计算圆面积的公式。文章分为多个部分，从随机代码生成、运行代码、种群进化到适应度评估等。作者首先定义了基本的操作符（+，-，*，/）和随机选择元素的函数`RANDOM-ELT`，接着介绍了生成随机函数表达式的过程，这些表达式由随机操作符和参数构成。随后，文章讨论了如何运行生成的代码、创建种群以及通过交叉和变异进化种群。最后，作者总结了整个过程，并鼓励读者在REPL环境中自行尝试这些代码。文章内容偏重实践，代码示例丰富，理论解释较少，适合对GP或Common Lisp感兴趣的初学者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于遗传编程（Genetic Programming, GP）及其替代方法、应用场景和相关资源的讨论

不同观点：
• abhgh 认为 Bayesian Optimization (Bayesopt) 是一个比遗传编程更具原则性和发展前景的替代方法，特别是在处理不可微目标函数的搜索问题时，比如超参数优化和分子发现。他还提供了相关资源和教程链接。[1][2][4][5]
• mark_l_watson 强调了 John Koza 的经典遗传编程书籍的价值，并指出不应将遗传算法（GA）与遗传编程（GP）混淆。
• hintymad 提出遗传编程适合解决哪些问题，尤其是在深度学习流行的当下，并询问是否有将遗传编程集成到深度学习中的模型。
• arscan 分享了参与 2011 年 "ants" AI 竞赛的个人经历，并提到最终获胜的代码虽然不够优雅但非常有效。
• westurner 提供了关于遗传编程和进化计算的历史背景信息，并提到了与 MOSES 和 Combo 相关的资源和工具。[3]
• ggerules 对帖子表示赞赏。
• nickpsecurity 分享了自己在遗传算法方面的简单演示项目，包括随机选择、轮盘赌选择和锦标赛选择等方法，并计划在学生贷款优化问题上应用遗传算法。
• ribs 认为遗传编程的前景不被看好，但同时指出这在不同情况下可能会有所不同。

补充讨论：
• 关于 ai-contest.com 网站被赌博网站劫持的问题，abhgh 和 artful314w 都提到了这一点。
• 关于遗传编程的具体应用，abhgh 和 nickpsecurity 提供了具体例子，如超参数优化、分子发现和学生贷款优化。
• 关于资源和教程，abhgh 和 westurner 提供了相关书籍和教程链接，帮助进一步了解 Bayesian Optimization 和遗传编程。
• 关于历史背景，westurner 提供了维基百科上的相关信息和与遗传编程相关的工具和项目链接。

争议焦点：
• 遗传编程的实际应用价值和前景。abhgh 和 ribs 对其前景持不同看法，abhgh 更看好 Bayesian Optimization，而 ribs 则认为遗传编程在某些情况下可能仍然有效。

总的来说，讨论围绕遗传编程的替代方法、实际应用和资源分享展开，参与者提供了不同的观点和具体例子。

1
Introduction
While my final ranking in the Google AI Contest was disappointing
(
280th
), it was a very educational experience and was totally offset
by
Gábor Melis' dominating win
using Common Lisp as well.
One of things that piqued my interest during the contest was
a post on the AI Challenge forums
about a bot written using
genetic programming
.
Genetic programming (GP) and
genetic algorithms
have always held my
interest but
seeing the bot in action
really motivated me to dive into
the matter.
Genetic programming is inspired by biological evolution and is a way
of solving problems by setting up an environment (tuned to the problem
at hand!) and allowing computer programs to evolve towards a possible
solution in that environment.
This article shows my initial exploration into GP using Common Lisp
and should be an example of a typical
REPL
session (my session was a
couple of hours divided over two evenings).  The code has been
reviewed, made a more readable and lispier but still looks very much
like what I wrote initially.  From the REPL session useful output has
been cut and pasted into this article.
This is a
really
basic introduction into GP and is meant for people
interested in GP and/or interested in (Common) Lisp.  It is heavy on
code and examples and light on theory.  My intention is for the reader
to play around with the functions on the REPL as they come by in the
article.
The code in this article should be portable Common Lisp.  If you need
to know what a function or macro does please consult the
Common Lisp HyperSpec
.
1.1
Toy Project
I found
A Field Guide to Genetic Programming
on-line and decided to
duplicate
Bill Clementson's toy project
of discovering the formula for
calculating the area of a circle.  Except for educational purposes we
will be starting from scratch.
1.2
Environment
Many Common Lispers use Emacs,
Slime
and usually Unix or OS X as
development environment.  However, do not get the impression this is
the only way to write Lisp.  The
development page on CLiki
lists many
other alternatives in various states of usability.
My recommendation is to use your favorite text editor and
CLISP
since
it comes with command line history and tab completion built in.  Write
or paste the code in your editor and save the file after every
addition as for example "
gp.lisp
".  Then you only need to type:
(load "/path/to/gp.lisp")
once and can use the command line history to reload it.
2
Generating Random Code
As you might have read, the
space.invaders
bot was written in PHP.
Our weapon of choice is Common Lisp and the first matter of business
is generating random code.
2.1
Operators
(
defparameter
*operators*
'(+ - * /))
To keep things simple and already knowing our target function (πr²) we
opt for using four operators: addition, subtraction, multiplication
and division.  In the name of simplicity (again) they will have an
arity of 2, so they will all take two arguments.
*OPERATORS* is the name of the  variable.  The *earmuffs* convention
is used to signify global variables.
2.2
RANDOM-ELT
(
defun
random-elt
(sequence)
(
let
((seq-length (length sequence)))
(
when
(> seq-length 0)
(elt sequence (random seq-length)))))
The function RANDOM-FORM in the next section uses RANDOM-ELT to select
a random element from the list of operators.
2.3
Generating Random
Function Forms
(
defun
random-form
(operators)
(append (list (random-elt operators))
(
loop
repeat 2
;
arity
collect (
let

43605731.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者使用Common Lisp进行遗传编程（Genetic Programming, GP）的初步探索，目标是通过进化算法找到计算圆面积的公式。文章分为多个部分，从随机代码生成、运行代码、种群进化到适应度评估等。作者首先定义了基本的操作符（+，-，*，/）和随机选择元素的函数`RANDOM-ELT`，接着介绍了生成随机函数表达式的过程，这些表达式由随机操作符和参数构成。随后，文章讨论了如何运行生成的代码、创建种群以及通过交叉和变异进化种群。最后，作者总结了整个过程，并鼓励读者在REPL环境中自行尝试这些代码。文章内容偏重实践，代码示例丰富，理论解释较少，适合对GP或Common Lisp感兴趣的初学者。

• abhgh 认为 Bayesian Optimization (Bayesopt) 是一个比遗传编程更具原则性和发展前景的替代方法，特别是在处理不可微目标函数的搜索问题时，比如超参数优化和分子发现。他还提供了相关资源和教程链接。[1][2][4][5]

• hintymad 提出遗传编程适合解决哪些问题，尤其是在深度学习流行的当下，并询问是否有将遗传编程集成到深度学习中的模型。
• arscan 分享了参与 2011 年 "ants" AI 竞赛的个人经历，并提到最终获胜的代码虽然不够优雅但非常有效。
• westurner 提供了关于遗传编程和进化计算的历史背景信息，并提到了与 MOSES 和 Combo 相关的资源和工具。[3]
• ggerules 对帖子表示赞赏。
• nickpsecurity 分享了自己在遗传算法方面的简单演示项目，包括随机选择、轮盘赌选择和锦标赛选择等方法，并计划在学生贷款优化问题上应用遗传算法。
• ribs 认为遗传编程的前景不被看好，但同时指出这在不同情况下可能会有所不同。

• 关于资源和教程，abhgh 和 westurner 提供了相关书籍和教程链接，帮助进一步了解 Bayesian Optimization 和遗传编程。
• 关于历史背景，westurner 提供了维基百科上的相关信息和与遗传编程相关的工具和项目链接。

争议焦点：
• 遗传编程的实际应用价值和前景。abhgh 和 ribs 对其前景持不同看法，abhgh 更看好 Bayesian Optimization，而 ribs 则认为遗传编程在某些情况下可能仍然有效。

总的来说，讨论围绕遗传编程的替代方法、实际应用和资源分享展开，参与者提供了不同的观点和具体例子。

data.title: Glamorous Toolkit
data.author: radeeyate
data.article_summary: Glamorous Toolkit是一个可塑开发环境（Moldable Development Environment），通过上下文微工具使系统问题变得可解释。它免费且开源，适用于Mac、Linux和Windows。该工具允许用户创建数千种针对特定系统问题的微工具，支持API探索、软件分析、数据探索、DevOps调查、系统文档编写和特定系统编辑器等功能。用户可以通过编程利用其潜力，并学习如何在环境中学习。它支持多种语言和技术，如Java、Ruby/Rails、Python、JavaScript和COBOL等，旨在通过上下文工具增强编程能力，使系统内部变得可解释。工具的可塑性是普遍需要的，通过不同视角总结系统，实现压缩通信和新反馈循环。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Glamorous Toolkit（以下简称GT）的可用性、易理解性及其相对于其他工具（如Jupyter Notebook、传统IDE等）的独特性和优势。

不同观点：
• Grumbledour：对GT感到矛盾，一方面认可其目标和潜力，但另一方面觉得界面难以理解，基本功能不直观，需要编程知识。他质疑是否值得投入时间学习，尤其在与Cuis Smalltalk等更简单的系统对比时。
• photonthug：认为GT涉及Smalltalk和Moose等项目，虽然很多人对其中的概念感兴趣，但Smalltalk/Pharo的公共认知度仍然不高。他指出需要新的词汇（如"moldable development"）来描述其独特性，但也认为这可能让大众更难理解。他建议GT应该减少学术化，更多地展示实际应用。
• dude01：赞赏GT的理念，认为它结合了Smalltalk IDE和C.A.S.E.工具，但实际使用中遇到困难，比如无法轻松查看本地Git代码库。
• mindwok：认为GT的网站不清楚其具体用途，让人困惑。
• throwaway743950：觉得GT和Smalltalk的哲学过于陌生，不确定其是否仍然相关，并询问是否可以用Python和Jupyter Notebook实现类似功能。
• jamesrcole：对GT网页上的图像和说明感到困惑，不明白其与"使系统可解释"的关系。
• WillAdams：考虑将GT用于自己的项目，但不确定其额外开销是否值得。希望看到实际项目中使用GT的前后对比案例。
• dhab：首次接触GT，对其潜力感到兴奋，认为它可以统一日常工作中的各种工具和流程，但具体应用场景需要更多说明。
• nathan_compton：定期关注GT，但一直不明白其具体用途。
• gugagore：指出GT与Jupyter Notebook的对比不准确，GT的UI本身是用目标语言实现的。
• 16bytes：对GT的项目介绍和网站设计感到困惑，认为使用了很多抽象和无意义的词汇，建议使用更具体和易懂的语言。
• ilaksh：将GT与Simonyi的Intentional Programming和Projectional Editing对比，询问GT是否是目前最先进的Projectional Editor。
• tylerjnewman：建议将GT与LLM客户端结合，开发能调用工具的代理。
• vivzkestrel：对GT的实际功能感到困惑，认为其网站和名称没有准确传达产品用途。

补充讨论：
• GT的易用性和入门门槛是讨论的焦点，许多用户觉得其基本功能不直观，需要阅读手册或学习编程知识。
• GT的独特概念（如"moldable development"和"contextual micro tools"）被认为既是其优势也是其难以理解的原因。
• 用户对GT的具体应用场景和实际价值感到困惑，希望看到更具体的使用案例和与其他工具的明确对比。
• 网站和介绍材料的改进建议被多次提及，用户希望看到更具体和易懂的描述。

43606027.article_content:
Glamorous Toolkit is the Moldable Development Environment
Make systems explainable through contextual micro tools
Download
Free and open-source for Mac, Linux & Windows
Star us on
GitHub
.
Chat with us on
Discord
.
Contextual micro tools?
Each problem about your system is special. And each problem can be explained through contextual development experiences. Glamorous Toolkit enables you to build such experiences out of micro tools. Thousands of them ... per system. It's called Moldable Development.
Watch Tudor Girba's YOW 2023 talk
(The first two minutes has poor sound quality, but it's still worth it ;))
A single environment. Many use cases
Glamorous Toolkit is the Moldable Development environment made out of visual and interactive operators that can be combined inexpensively in many ways.
API exploration
Discover and browse API data
Software analysis
Explore your code from many perspectives
Data exploration
Unearth patterns in data through visualization
DevOps investigations
Analyze logs and system behavior
System documentation
Make the system tell its stories
System specific editors
Create context-aware editing experiences
An interactive exploration of dependencies between ActiveRecords in a Rails application that also shows the Ruby and SQL sources.
Exploring a REST API through contextual views.
Investigating the logs of a failing Jenkins continuous delivery job.
Exploring the data exported from a Twitter account.
Exploring the book about Glamorous Toolkit written in Glamorous Toolkit.
Editing a AT Protocol lexicon definition at the domain level: highlighting of name strings, completion inside JSON strings, navigation from a reference to its definition.
How to start?
Download and run.
To exploit Glamorous Toolkit, you have to program it. To learn how to program it, first learn how to learn inside the environment.
Then pick a problem you care about and work your way through it.
Get started
Watch Oscar Nierstrasz's GT in 7 minutes series.
Made to work with many languages and technologies
Glamorous Toolkit is implemented in Pharo and Rust but it was designed to be extended for other technologies and languages. It can be used to analyze various sources such as Java, C#, Ruby/Rails, Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, React or COBOL. And it can be used to work with various runtimes like GraphQL, Python, JavaScript or Gemstone.
Editing GraphQL and exploring a server response from a Lepiter page.
Explaining a tokenization algorithm implemented in Python.
A dedicated environment for defining support for other languages.
Exploring COBOL screens, control flows and source code.
So, what exactly is Moldable Development again?
Moldable Development is a way of programming through contextual tools built for each problem.
The premise of Moldable Development is that there is no single perspective on a system that is correct. There are always many, and different parts of the system are best shown differently. These shapes summarize the system from specific perspectives. This then leads to a compressed communication and a new feedback loop.
Glamorous Toolkit itself is an extensive case study of how contextual tools enhance programming abilities. It comes out of the box with thousands of extensions and examples that touch on the whole system.
The goal? To make the inside of systems explainable.
The need for moldability is pervasive. The treemap shows the classes of Glamorous Toolkit organized in packages. Blue denotes classes that contain at least one contextual view; green shows those that have an example.
Watch Simon Wardley and Tudor Girba chat about Moldable Development and thousands of tools per system.

data.author: byry
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对某人在空袭期间进行NFC频谱分析的评论，讨论涉及NFC技术的技术细节、应用场景、隐私问题以及技术限制。

不同观点：
• niemandhier对某人在空袭期间专注于NFC频谱分析表示敬佩，认为这种专注和奉献精神值得学习。
• nubinetwork对NFC的有效传输距离提出质疑，指出NFC的传输范围仅为3厘米，并通过实验（使用Android手机和SDR）无法在6英尺外重现这一情况。
• spongebobstoes对NFC在设备解锁或唤醒时发送传输信号的现象表示惊讶，并寻求解释。
• boznz提到Bluetooth具有广播和UID功能，并猜测NFC可能也有类似的UID，表示对解码NFC数据感兴趣。

补充讨论：
• drag0s表达了对iOS无法像Android那样轻松禁用NFC或定位功能的不满。
• dzhiurgis提问NFC传输是否在锁定模式下也会发生。
• babuloseo提出NFC是否可以用于寻找被困在地震废墟中的人，并随后对相关部门的技术能力表示质疑。
• byry引用了文章中的一段话，赞赏NFC信号在屏幕关闭时发送单次ping的设计。
• yapyap仅表示对该话题感兴趣。
• sparker72678对通过NFC追踪占用模式、关联信号与已知设备、识别睡眠周期等功能不以为然，指出WiFi和GSM早已具备这些功能。
• xyst担心信号泄漏问题，建议使用铅材料阻挡信号，并讽刺地问道何时会出台新的建筑规范。

争议焦点：
• NFC的有效传输距离以及在不同场景下的实际应用效果存在争议。nubinetwork通过实验质疑NFC在较长距离上的传输能力。
• babuloseo对相关部门利用技术（如NFC）进行救援的能力表示怀疑，引发对技术应用实际效果的讨论。

总结：讨论围绕NFC的技术细节、应用潜力、隐私问题以及技术限制展开，参与者对NFC的功能和局限性有不同的理解和期待。

data.title: Microcomputers – The First Wave: Responding to Altair
data.author: cfmcdonald
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了唐·塔贝尔（Don Tarbell）在个人电脑发展初期的贡献。塔贝尔最初通过自制电脑部件和销售集成电路安装板进入个人电脑领域。他在1972年成功组装了一台包含8位处理器、4000字节内存和多种外围设备的电脑。1975年，随着Altair 8800套件的发布，个人电脑爱好者的兴趣激增，塔贝尔也参与成立了南加州电脑协会（SCCS），并担任秘书。他发现Altair套件存在内存不足和无法永久存储数据等问题，于1976年推出了更便宜的塔贝尔卡式接口，通过普通卡式录音机进行数据存储，解决了这一难题。塔贝尔的创新代表了20世纪70年代个人电脑从爱好者的 niche 市场向全国性产业的转变，他也是早期通过提供补充硬件响应市场需求的创业者之一。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于早期计算机（特别是PDP-11）及其历史影响的讨论

here
.]
Don Tarbell: A Life in Personal Computing
In August 1968, Stephen Gray, sole proprietor of the Amateur Computer Society (ACS), published a letter in the society newsletter from an enthusiast in Huntsville, Alabama named Don Tarbell. To help other would-be owners of home-built computers, Tarbell offered a mounting board for integrated circuits for sale for $8 from his own hobby-entrepreneur company, Advanced Digital Design. Tarbell worked for Sperry Rand on projects for NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center, but had gotten hooked on computers through coursework at the University of Alabama at Huntsville, and found the ACS through a contact at IBM.
[1]
Over the ensuing years, integrated circuits became far cheaper and easier to come by, and building a real home computer on one’s own thus far more feasible (though still a daunting challenge, demanding a wide range of hardware and software skills). In June 1972, Tarbell had mastered enough of those skills to report to the
ACS Newsletter
that he (at last) had a working computer system, with an 8-bit processor built from integrated circuits, four-thousand bytes of memory, a text editor and a calculator program, a Teletype for input and output, and an eight-track-tape interface for long-term storage. Not long after this report to ACS, Tarbell decamped from Alabama and moved to the Los Angeles area to work for Hughes Aircraft.
[2]
Don Tarbell with his home-built computer system [
Kilobaud: The Small Computer Magazine
(May 1977), 132].
Three years after that, in 1975, the arrival of the Altair 8800 kit announced that anyone with the skills to assemble electronics could have the power of a minicomputer in their own home, and thousands heeded the call. A group of 150 of these personal computer hobbyists met in the commons of the apartment complex where Tarbell lived. They had come on Father’s Day for the inaugural meeting of the Southern California Computer Society (SCCS). Half of the participants already owned Altairs. Tarbell took on the position of secretary for the new society, and served on the board of directors. Within a few months, SCCS began producing its own magazine with a full editorial staff, a far more sophisticated operation than the old hand-typed
ACS Newsletter
; Tarbell eventually became one of its associate editors.
[3]
But an Altair kit by itself was far from a complete computer system like the one Tarbell had back in 1975. It had a piddling 256 bytes of memory, and no devices for reading or writing data other than lights and switches. Dozens of hobbyists founded their own companies to sell other computer buffs the additional equipment that would answer the deficiencies of their newly-purchased Altairs. Don Tarbell was one of them. Among the major problems was the inability to permanently store or load programs and data. Once you shut off the computer, everything you had entered into it was lost. A standard Teletype terminal came equipped with a paper tape punch and reader, but even a heavily used Teletype could cost $1000.
In February 1976, Tarbell offered a much simpler and cheaper solution, the Tarbell cassette interface, a board that would slot into the Altair case and connect the computer to an ordinary cassette recorder, writing or reading data to or from the magnetic tape. Not only was a cassette machine much cheaper than a teletype, cassettes were more durable than paper, could store more data (up to 2200 bits per inch with Tarbell’s controller), and could be rewritten many times. Tarbell’s board sold for $150 assembled, $100 for a kit. He later branched out into floppy disk controllers and an interpreter for the BASIC computer language, and became a minor celebrity of the growing microcomputer scene.
[4]
Tarbell’s story offers a microcosm of the transition of personal computers, over the course of the 1970s, from an obscure niche hobby to a national industry. Like Hugo Gernsback in radio half a century before, home-computer tinkerers found themselves new roles in a growing hobby business as community-builders, publishers, and small-scale manufacturers. Like Tarbell, the first wave of these entrepreneurs responded directly to the Altair, offering supplemental hardware to offset its weaknesses or offering a more reliable or more capable hobby computer.
The First Wave: Responding to Altair
The Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry Systems (MITS) Altair came with a lot of potential, but it lay mostly unrealized in the basic kit MITS shipped out. This was partly intentional: the Altair sold on the basis of its exceptionally low price (less than $500), and it simply couldn’t remain so cheap if it had all the features of a full-fledged minicomputer system.
Other deficiencies arose by accident, out of the amateurish nature of MITS. The good timing and negotiating skills of Ed Roberts, the company’s owner, had put him at the spearhead of the hobby computer revoluti
43605120.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了唐·塔贝尔（Don Tarbell）在个人电脑发展初期的贡献。塔贝尔最初通过自制电脑部件和销售集成电路安装板进入个人电脑领域。他在1972年成功组装了一台包含8位处理器、4000字节内存和多种外围设备的电脑。1975年，随着Altair 8800套件的发布，个人电脑爱好者的兴趣激增，塔贝尔也参与成立了南加州电脑协会（SCCS），并担任秘书。他发现Altair套件存在内存不足和无法永久存储数据等问题，于1976年推出了更便宜的塔贝尔卡式接口，通过普通卡式录音机进行数据存储，解决了这一难题。塔贝尔的创新代表了20世纪70年代个人电脑从爱好者的 niche 市场向全国性产业的转变，他也是早期通过提供补充硬件响应市场需求的创业者之一。

data.title: Use the Gemini API with OpenAI Fallback in TypeScript
data.author: l5870uoo9y
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何在使用Gemini公共API时，设置一个安全回退机制以应对超出请求限制的情况。作者通过使用OpenAI的TS/JS库和一些辅助函数实现这一功能，特别是在一个图表制作应用中，Gemini模型的请求限制为每分钟20次。

首先，定义要使用的模型类型，包括Gemini和OpenAI的模型。然后，创建一个辅助函数`getCompletion`，该函数接收两个配置对象，分别对应两种模型。在请求第一个模型失败时，自动回退到第二个模型。示例代码展示了如何调用该函数并输出结果。

此外，文章还提供了一个用于生成类型安全结构化输出的辅助函数`getJSONCompletion`，并演示了如何使用Zod库来解析和验证响应格式。通过这种方式，可以灵活地在不同AI模型之间切换，并确保输出的可靠性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对LLM（大语言模型）的抽象和集成工具的比较与讨论

不同观点：
• bearjaws 支持 Vercel AI SDK，认为它能很好地抽象所有LLM，包括本地运行的模型，尤其称赞其对文件附件的处理能力以及使用 zod 进行类型和验证的便捷性。
• DeborahEmeni_ 分享了使用 OpenRouter 和跨供应商的回退链的经验，强调其在应对速率限制和不同有效载荷大小时的实用性，但也指出缺乏关于链式调用（如 Gemini + OpenAI）的延迟数据。
• thesandlord 推荐使用 BAML，指出它支持多种回退和重试策略，并返回强类型的LLM输出。
• calebkaiser 也推荐 OpenRouter，强调其跨模型切换时无需更改实现代码或管理多个API密钥的优势。
• nextworddev 简单直接地推荐 Litellm，没有详细说明原因。
• visarga 对 Gemini 模型的 JSON 模式操作感到失望，认为其表现不如开源的 Qwen 模型，尤其在基本信息提取到JSON任务中。
• _pdp_ 提到提示词无法简单地从一个模型移植到另一个模型，暗示模型之间的差异性。
• ilrwbwrkhv 从视觉和审美角度批评 Typescript，认为其语法不友好，尤其是大写单词让代码扫描变得困难。

补充讨论：
• 关于 Vercel AI SDK 和 OpenRouter 的讨论较多，两者都被认为是有效的模型抽象和集成工具，但在延迟数据和实现细节上存在不同看法。
• visarga 提出的 Gemini 模型问题指出了某些专有模型在特定任务上不如开源模型的现象，这是一个值得注意的争议点。
• ilrwbwrkhv 对 Typescript 的批评虽然不直接相关，但也反映了开发者在使用不同技术栈时的个人偏好和体验差异。

争议焦点：
• 专有模型（如 Gemini）与开源模型（如 Qwen）在特定任务上的表现优劣。
• 不同LLM抽象工具（如 Vercel AI SDK 和 OpenRouter）在实际应用中的优劣比较，特别是延迟数据和实现细节。

data.title: AEgIS turns phone sensors into antimatter camera of unprecedented resolution
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: AEgIS合作团队利用智能手机摄像头传感器开发了一种新型探测器，能够以空前分辨率实时成像反物质湮灭。该探测器由慕尼黑工业大学的研究团队领导，实现了约0.6微米的分辨率，较以往方法提高了35倍。通过集成60个传感器，该设备达到了3840兆像素，是目前成像探测器中像素最高的。这种技术结合了高分辨率、实时诊断和自校准功能，并通过人工分析图像进一步提高了精度。该探测器将用于研究反氢在地球引力场中的自由下落，并为低能反粒子湮灭研究开辟新途径。

• [gaudat] 对相机电路板（PCB）设计表示赞赏，特别提到了设计中的艺术元素和去耦电容的排列方式，显示出对技术和美学细节的关注。

• [sinuhe69] 对文章中缺乏具体技术细节表示不满，认为公司公告往往充斥着空洞的营销词汇，而缺乏实际的技术信息。这里表达了对更多详细技术资料的需求。

AEgIS transforms smartphone sensors into an antimatter camera of unprecedented resolution
The AEgIS collaboration, led by a team from the Technical University of Munich, has repurposed smartphone camera sensors to create a detector capable of imaging antiproton annihilations in real time with unprecedented resolution
2 April, 2025
|
By
Alex Epshtein
Image caption: The new AEgIS detector (left) and a selection of the antiproton annihilations it captured (right). Annihilations appear as star-shaped events with multiple tracks emanating from one primary vertex. Green, cyan and orange arrows point to examples of nuclear fragments. (Image: AEgIS/CERN)
Did you know that the camera sensor in your smartphone could help unlock the secrets of
antimatter
? The
AEgIS
collaboration, led by Professor Christoph Hugenschmidt’s team from the research neutron source FRM II at the Technical University of Munich (TUM), has developed a detector using modified mobile camera sensors to image in real time the points where antimatter annihilates with matter. This new device, described in a paper just published in
Science Advances
, can pinpoint antiproton annihilations with a resolution of about 0.6 micrometres, a 35-fold improvement over previous real-time methods.
AEgIS and other experiments at CERN’s Antimatter Factory, such as
ALPHA
and
GBAR
, are on a mission to measure the free-fall of antihydrogen within Earth’s gravitational field with high precision, each using a different technique. AEgIS’s approach involves producing a horizontal beam of antihydrogen and measuring its vertical displacement using a device called a moiré deflectometer that reveals tiny deviations in motion and a detector that records the antihydrogen annihilation points.
“For AEgIS to work, we need a detector with incredibly high spatial resolution, and mobile camera sensors have pixels smaller than 1 micrometre,” says Francesco Guatieri, the principal investigator on the paper. “We’ve integrated 60 camera sensors into our detector, enabling it to achieve a resolution of 3840 mega pixels – the highest pixel count of any imaging detector to date.”
Previously, photographic plates were the only option, but they lacked real-time capabilities,” added Guatieri. “Our solution, demonstrated for antiprotons and directly applicable to antihydrogen, combines photographic-plate-level resolution, real-time diagnostics, self-calibration and a good particle collection surface, all in one device.”
The researchers used commercial optical image sensors that had previously been
shown
to be capable of imaging low-energy positrons in real time with unprecedented resolution. “We had to strip away the first layers of the sensors, which are made to deal with the advanced integrated electronics of mobile phones,” says Guatieri. “This required high-level electronic design and micro-engineering.”
A key factor in achieving the record resolution was an unexpected element: crowdsourcing. “We found that human intuition currently outperforms automated methods,” says Guatieri. The AEgIS team asked their colleagues to manually determine the position of the antiproton annihilation points in each of the more than 2500 detector images, a procedure that turned out to be far more accurate and precise than any algorithm. The only downside: it took up to 10 hours for each colleague to plough through every annihilation event.
“The extraordinary resolution also enables us to distinguish between different annihilation fragments,” says AEgIS spokesperson Ruggero Caravita. By measuring the width of tracks of different annihilation products, the researchers can investigate whether the tracks are produced by protons or pions.
“The new detector paves the way for new research on low-energy antiparticle annihilation, and is a game-changing technology for the observation of the tiny shifts in antihydrogen caused by gravity,” says Caravita.

43576559.article_summary: AEgIS合作团队利用智能手机摄像头传感器开发了一种新型探测器，能够以空前分辨率实时成像反物质湮灭。该探测器由慕尼黑工业大学的研究团队领导，实现了约0.6微米的分辨率，较以往方法提高了35倍。通过集成60个传感器，该设备达到了3840兆像素，是目前成像探测器中像素最高的。这种技术结合了高分辨率、实时诊断和自校准功能，并通过人工分析图像进一步提高了精度。该探测器将用于研究反氢在地球引力场中的自由下落，并为低能反粒子湮灭研究开辟新途径。

data.title: Knowing where your engineer salary comes from
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了科技公司中工程师常犯的一个误区：他们过于专注于不直接创造利润的工作（如技术债务、无资金项目、重构等），却忽略了公司存在的核心目的是赚钱。文章将这种现象比作投票支持解雇自己的人，指出工程师如果不能将自己的工作与公司利润挂钩，职位就不稳定。科技公司由一小群人运营，目标是盈利，工作价值与其对公司利润的贡献成正比。作者建议工程师要了解公司的商业模式，并确保自己的工作支持该模式，否则可能面临失业风险。简单来说，工程师需要清楚公司如何赚钱，并让自己的工作与之相关联，以保持职位稳定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术工作在公司中的价值以及如何在组织中获得认可和晋升

不同观点：
• PeterStuer：认为大多数管理层对技术工程持忽视态度，将其视为威胁而非资产。管理层倾向于将工程工作商品化，不承认工程师对公司成功的差异化贡献。这种环境下，从工程岗位升至管理岗位变得困难。
• cdavid：指出公司内部“赚钱”的定义是社会构建的，而非客观存在。在大公司中，晋升往往与实际赚钱能力无关，而与办公室政治和社交技巧有关。A/B测试的结果可能会因为管理层的更替而失去意义。
• agentultra：认为文章过于简化，指出某些行业（如航空）的价值不仅仅体现在利润上，还包括安全和客户信任等因素。软件行业也需要注重这些方面，而非单纯追求新功能。
• xivzgrev：个人经历显示，若工作内容不直接产生收入，职业发展会受限。虽然情感上倾向于选择有趣或高风险高回报的项目，但从职业发展角度看，选择高收入产品更为有利。
• tybit：指出在大公司中，即使在盈利丰厚的产品团队工作，也不一定能在晋升中获得“影响”加分，反而是从事平台/基础设施工作的工程师更有可能获得认可。
• 0rzech：同意PeterStuer的观点，认为技术工作价值被低估是普遍现象，而非例外。
• bruce511：强调工程师需要主动向管理层展示其工作的长期价值，而不仅仅是完成技术任务。需将技术贡献转化为可衡量的经济效益。
• cjs_ac：认为在大型组织中，个体难以看到自己的工作如何贡献于公司成功，导致对工作价值的误解。
• sakex：指出AI研究人员是一个例外，他们的工作往往得到高度认可。
• esafak：建议工程师理解并连接工作与收入的关系，以便在组织中获得价值认可。
• tonnydourado：认为文章的观点显而易见，薪酬与工作重要性不成正比，尤其是在非营利性职业中更为明显。
• stego-tech：文章提供了有用的职业建议，但现代科技公司往往不按此逻辑运作，更关注新潮产品而非利润中心。在某些组织中，创造价值但不被认可是一个巨大的红 flag。
• mirawelner：选择在大学和初创公司工作以避开大公司的腐败和自私行为，但经历部门资金被削减后感到失望。
• sanitycheck：认为专注于保持收入来源的工作至关重要，尤其是在资源有限的环境中，否则将面临失业风险。
• shireboy：正在尝试向上级管理层证明“技术债务”的价值，强调需要在业务需求和解决技术债务之间找到平衡。

补充讨论：
• 技术工作在公司中的价值评估存在复杂性，尤其是在大型组织中，社交关系和办公室政治对职业发展的影响不容忽视。
• 不同行业和公司对技术工作的价值认定存在差异，某些情况下，工程师需主动展示其工作对公司的长期经济效益。
• 技术债务的处理和展示是工程师与管理层沟通中的一大挑战，找到业务需求与技术改进的平衡点至关重要。

43603646.article_content:
With the recent flurry of US federal firings, many people are
pointing and laughing
at the Trump-voting federal employees who are just now finding out that they’ve voted for themselves to be let go. How could you have this poor a mental model of
what your job even is
? Well. In my opinion, many software engineers are operating under a mental model that’s just as bad, and are often doing the equivalent of voting for the person promising to fire them.
I won’t quote the tweets, but I regularly see stories like “I convinced my idiot bosses to
finally
let me do only tech debt work, and would you believe they fired me after a few months?” Or “I’ve been busting my ass on this underfunded project and I still got a bad performance review”. Or “it’s so unfair that I haven’t been promoted - look at all this amazing accessibility/standards/open-source work I’ve been doing!” The basic structure goes like this:
A bright-eyed engineer joins a tech company, excited to go and make the world a better place
They throw themselves into various pieces of work that don’t make money (improving FCP performance, better screenreader support, refactoring)
Their managers desperately try to redirect them to work that does make money, causing a long frustrating power struggle
Eventually the bright-eyed engineer gives up and unhappily focuses on Profitable Product X, or
The bright-eyed engineer leaves or is fired, and goes on Twitter to complain about their important work not being valued
The complaint in this story is basically equivalent to “I can’t believe Trump is firing me from the IRS when I voted for the guy”. It represents a fundamental misunderstanding of what tech companies
are
.
What are tech companies?
So what is the right understanding? Let’s start as simple as possible. Tech companies are run by small groups of people with the goal of making money
1
. Successful tech companies make a lot of money, by definition. They hire software engineers in order to continue doing the things that make that money, or to do new things that make more money.
At successful tech companies, engineering work is valued in proportion to how much money it makes the company (directly or indirectly). Patrick McKenzie has an
excellent post
on this:
Profit Centers are the part of an organization that bring in the bacon: partners at law firms, sales at enterprise software companies, “masters of the universe” on Wall Street, etc etc.  Cost Centers are, well, everybody else.  You really want to be attached to Profit Centers because it will bring you higher wages, more respect, and greater opportunities for everything of value to you.  It isn’t hard: a bright high schooler, given a paragraph-long description of a business, can usually identify where the Profit Center is.  If you want to work there, work for that.  If you can’t, either a) work elsewhere or b) engineer your transfer after joining the company.
Companies value work more the closer it is to a profit center. I don’t think you necessarily have to work
in
profit centers (in most tech companies, that would mean abandoning your engineering title and role). But you need to demonstrate your value to the profit center in order for your own work to be valued. I’m not saying you need to do this to keep your job. Companies pay lots of people who don’t deliver value, sometimes for many years. What I’m saying is this:
If your work isn’t clearly connected to company profit, your position is
unstable
In other words, you’re probably depending on a kind-hearted manager (or CEO) who personally values your work. When they leave, you’re in trouble. Or you’re depending on a large company not really caring to check if a small team is bringing in profits. When they look, you’re in trouble. Or you’re depending on a cultural climate where your work has temporary cultural cachet (e.g. biofuels in the early 2000s). When that changes, you’re in trouble. The only way to have a stable position is to be connected to the way the company makes money.
Connecting your work to profit
In order to know if your work is connected to company profits, you have to know two things:
What is your company’s business model? How do they make money?
How does your work support the business model?
Publicly traded companies must publish their business model and finances every year, which means you can either just go read that or read what people are writing about it on business blogs, magazines, and so on. (If you’re working for a well-known company, you can probably just ask a LLM). If you’re working for a private company, that can be harder, but usually it’s not too hard to get the gist. For instance, the broad strokes of where Valve get their money from are pretty clear: it’s Steam, not their first-party games.
Being an engineer at a company will give you much more visibility into the business model. For instance, you can run analytics queries that identify the ten largest customers. Often you won’t have to run these queries directly - they’ll

data.title: Journey to Optimize Cloudflare D1 Database Queries
data.author: rxliuli
data.article_summary:
本文记录了作者在使用Cloudflare Workers和D1数据库过程中，对数据库查询进行优化的经验。作者通过监控D1仪表盘、检查查询语句和行读取/写入数量，发现并解决了几个问题：

1. **使用批量请求**：通过将多个写操作合并为一个批处理请求，减少了数据库的响应时间。
2. **更新操作中排除ID字段**：更新记录时，排除ID字段可以避免不必要的行读取，特别是在有外键引用时。
3. **避免全表扫描计数**：使用基于游标的翻页方式，避免使用OFFSET和COUNT，因为这会扫描整个表。
4. **避免多表左连接**：复杂的左连接查询可能导致大量行读取，应尽量避免。

作者还提到Prisma不支持D1批量操作，因此切换到了Drizzle。这些优化措施有效减少了数据库操作的复杂度和响应时间。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：D1数据库的性能、使用场景、原子性操作的可行性以及与其他存储方案（如Durable Objects和KV）的比较。

不同观点：
• [kpozin] 认为D1的限制在于事务不能跨多个请求，因此无法在数据库选择、执行应用逻辑后以原子方式写入数据库。为了实现类似事务的原子性，需要通过批处理请求并使用SQL技巧（如JSON解析错误）来中止操作。对于更复杂的情况，可能需要将应用逻辑转化为SQL语句。

• [fastball] 对D1的性能持批评态度，指出其全球性能较差，尤其是在非欧洲地区，首字节时间（TTFB）表现不佳。尽管文章对前端开发者有帮助，但不如选择托管的Postgres解决方案，性能和功能更强。

• [your_challenger] 提出了Durable Object与SQL存储性能的比较问题，隐含了对D1性能的质疑，并想知道Durable Object是否同样存在性能问题。

• [piterrro] 认为D1适合小型项目（如页面访问计数、邮件列表等），但对于复杂查询和多表操作，成本高且不划算。分享了自己在logdy.dev项目中使用D1与Cloudflare Workers的成功经验，但也提到过去因不了解定价而产生的高成本问题。

• [taf2] 提出了D1与KV或Durable Objects的性能对比问题，关注不同存储方案之间的性能差异。

补充讨论：
• 对于D1的性能问题，[fastball] 和 [piterrro] 都提到了性能和成本的权衡。前者更倾向于传统托管数据库，而后者认为小型项目中D1表现良好。
• [kpozin] 提出的原子性操作问题显示了D1在处理复杂事务时的局限性，并提供了一种基于SQL技巧的解决方案。
• [your_challenger] 和 [taf2] 更关注D1与其他存储解决方案（如Durable Objects和KV）的对比，特别是性能方面，但未有明确结论。

争议焦点：
• D1的性能问题：[fastball] 认为性能不佳，而 [piterrro] 则认为在小型项目中表现良好，存在使用场景的争议。
• 原子性操作的可行性：[kpozin] 提出的SQL技巧是否是解决复杂事务的最佳实践存在讨论空间。

Journey to Optimize Cloudflare D1 Database Queries
Background
Recently, I've been working on server-side projects using Cloudflare Workers with D1 database. During this process, I encountered several database-related challenges. Since databases are quite unfamiliar territory for frontend developers, I decided to document my experiences.
The image below shows the request records for the past 30 days, revealing dramatic fluctuations in database queries.
Problem Identification
Solving problems begins with identifying them. Here are several methods that helped me spot issues:
Monitoring the D1 dashboard to detect anomalies in database operations
Examining query statements and row read/write counts, with special attention to queries with high counts or rows read/written
Using
c.env.DB.prepare('<sql>').run()).meta
to check the returned metadata, which reveals how many rows were actually read/written for each query
Using Batch Requests
It's important to understand that while Workers and D1 are both Cloudflare services, using them together doesn't make D1 faster. For example, a simple query like this has an average response time exceeding 200ms:
await
db
.
select
(
)
.
from
(
user
)
.
limit
(
1
)
When an endpoint includes multiple database operations, it's best to use D1 batch operations, especially for write operations which are even slower than queries due to lack of read-only replicas. For instance, instead of:
await
db
.
insert
(
user
)
.
values
(
{
...
}
)
await

43572511.article_summary:
本文记录了作者在使用Cloudflare Workers和D1数据库过程中，对数据库查询进行优化的经验。作者通过监控D1仪表盘、检查查询语句和行读取/写入数量，发现并解决了几个问题：

1. **使用批量请求**：通过将多个写操作合并为一个批处理请求，减少了数据库的响应时间。
2. **更新操作中排除ID字段**：更新记录时，排除ID字段可以避免不必要的行读取，特别是在有外键引用时。
3. **避免全表扫描计数**：使用基于游标的翻页方式，避免使用OFFSET和COUNT，因为这会扫描整个表。
4. **避免多表左连接**：复杂的左连接查询可能导致大量行读取，应尽量避免。

作者还提到Prisma不支持D1批量操作，因此切换到了Drizzle。这些优化措施有效减少了数据库操作的复杂度和响应时间。

主要讨论点：用户对某款字谜游戏的反馈，包括技术问题、功能建议和个人体验。

不同观点：
• **技术问题反馈**：
  - [xfp] 指出游戏在Firefox上出现加载后屏幕变黑的问题。
  - [redbell] 进一步确认了Firefox (Windows) 和 Brave (Windows/Android) 上存在问题，但在其他浏览器如Chrome、Edge、Safari上运行正常。指出问题可能与"https://cloud.umami.is/script.js"脚本未加载有关。

• **功能建议**：
  - [redbell] 建议增加音效以增强游戏体验，并提出可以调整单词长度以增加游戏动态性。
  - [BrenBarn] 建议在游戏结束时给出提示，而不是让页面变黑。
  - [zuminator] 建议在游戏失败时，用红色标出错误猜测，用绿色标出正确单词，以满足玩家查看错失单词的心理需求。

• **个人体验分享**：
  - [daredevildave] 提到自己几年前做过类似的字谜游戏，并分享了游戏链接。指出整理单词列表以避免不合适或过于困难的单词是一个重要工作。
  - [anitil] 表示游戏有趣但让人感到压力，放松后表现有所改善。
  - [chakintosh] 提到自己玩到了第11关，但同事干扰了他的游戏体验。
  - [zem] 认为游戏有趣但结束得过于突然，并指出单词列表中出现了不合适的词汇如"cumshots"，需要过滤。

• **其他相关经验**：
  - [benatkin] 提到游戏难度较大，并分享了自己十多年前做的相关项目链接，展示了一个单词变为另一个单词的动画。

补充讨论：
- 游戏在不同浏览器上的兼容性问题是一个争议焦点，尤其是Firefox和Brave。
- 玩家对游戏结束时缺乏提示表示不满，认为影响体验。
- 对单词列表的过滤和单词长度的多样性提出了改进建议，以提升游戏的平衡性和趣味性。
- 有玩家分享了个人相关项目，丰富了讨论内容。

data.title: US tax return filings drop by nearly 1M, extension requests rise
data.author: MilnerRoute
data.article_summary: 截至3月21日，与去年同期相比，美国国税局（IRS）收到的报税表减少了近100万份，下降了1.1%。专家表示，这种下降并非异常，近年此时段常出现类似情况。然而，今年的下降伴随着对税收减少和IRS面临严重人员削减、领导层变动及内部冲突的担忧。可能原因包括：一些人利用IRS内部混乱延迟报税；无证移民因担心被驱逐而推迟报税；自然灾害影响；以及纳税人对报税过程的信心提升，认为可以等到最后一刻。此外，需要缴税的纳税人往往更接近截止日期才报税，这也可能是报税数量下降的原因之一。尽管IRS面临挑战，其客户服务等待时间仍保持在三分钟，显示出一定改进。

• 有人提到，由于越来越多的人需要缴税而不是获得退税，因此他们倾向于晚点报税，以延迟付款。([rdtsc])
• 政治抗议也被认为是部分人拒绝报税的原因，特别是对当前或前任政府政策不满的人。([rdtsc], [silexia])
• 有人提出，消费者经济困难、国税局大规模裁员或其它未知因素可能也是原因之一。([Havoc])
• 飓风导致的报税截止日期延长被认为是南部地区提交量下降的另一个可能原因。([cma])

• 非法移民因担心被驱逐出境而不再报税，这被视为提交量下降的另一个因素。([silexia])
