data.title: The Insanity of Being a Software Engineer
data.author: vmsp
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了软件工程师职业的挑战和不断变化的要求。作者指出，成为软件工程师不仅需要掌握多种编程语言和工具，还需适应公司特定的框架，如Rails、Django或Laravel。随着技术发展，JavaScript、React、TypeScript、Redux等新技术层出不穷，工程师需不断学习。此外，DevOps的兴起使工程师还需掌握Docker、Ansible、AWS及基础设施管理工具如Terraform。即使升职为经理，仍需承担技术工作与管理职责。文章反思了软件开发日益复杂的趋势，质疑为何这一职业要求全能，而不像其他行业有更明确的分工。作者最后表达了对未来通过简单提示构建应用的期望，认为这未必是坏事。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件工程职业的难易程度及其复杂性来源

不同观点：
• **软件工程不难**：[abxyz]认为软件工程是较为容易的职业，因为工程师被过度呵护，误将一些简单任务视为困难。这表明该评论者认为行业对困难的认知有偏差。
• **软件工程变得更复杂**：[travisgriggs]指出软件变得越来越复杂，但并非所有复杂性都有正当理由，认为是行业发展（如大量资金涌入和集体设计）导致了不必要的复杂性。
• **职业压力和多技能要求**：[JKCalhoun]通过自身三十年的职业经历说明软件工程的复杂性不仅在于技术更新（如多种编程语言和工具的演变），还在于工作方式的变化（如敏捷开发、代码审查等）。此外，他提到团队文化和工作压力对个人健康的影响。
• **多技能要求导致不专精**：[maeln]认为软件工程领域要求从业者具备多方面技能，而不是专精某一项工作。这种趋势导致“半桶水”现象普遍存在，因为公司倾向于雇佣能够胜任多种任务的人，而不是多个专家。
• **复杂性源于无谓的创新和职业安全考虑**：[weego]认为当今软件工程的复杂性并非源自实际需要，而是工程师为了个人职业发展（如为了在FAANG公司求职）或工作安全感而故意引入的。

补充讨论：
• **管理岗位的挑战**：[mdaniel]提到技术人员在晋升为管理岗位后需要学习全新的技能，而这些技能与他们之前积累的技术经验并不直接相关，导致管理不善的问题。
• **全栈趋势的问题**：[basfo]指出“全栈开发”趋势导致很多团队成员在不熟悉的领域工作，产生效率低下和技术问题，最终影响项目进展。
• **缺乏标准化**：[bearjaws]和[grahar64]都提到软件行业缺乏像建筑行业那样的标准化，导致每个项目都需要重新发明“材料和标准”，增加了复杂性和学习成本。
• **与其他学科的难度比较**：[chiffre01]认为软件工程的难度相对较低，尤其是与解决现实世界中的复杂问题（如气候变化、疾病治疗等）相比，软件工程更多是数据的重组和处理，而非突破性的科学创新。

争议焦点：
• 软件工程是否真的困难：一部分人认为软件工程并不困难，只是被过度复杂化；另一部分人则认为其复杂性源于技术演变、行业需求和不必要的创新，且工作压力和多技能要求增加了职业难度。
• 行业标准化问题：缺乏标准化被认为是导致软件工程复杂和低效的重要原因，但如何实现标准化以及其可行性在评论中未有一致意见。

43600582.article_content:
The Insanity of Being a Software Engineer
06/04/2025
Is something I think about often because I can’t help but wonder if most other jobs are like this.
Being a software engineer is tough. You need to know a couple of programming languages and tools right from the get-go. But that won’t cut it. Companies expect you to know whatever particular framework they use. That might be Rails or Django or Laravel or something else. You’ll also need CSS. It’ll take you a lifetime to learn — and you still won’t know why the layout’s breaking — but knowing just enough to get by is feasible.
It’s unlikely that you won’t have to deal with JavaScript. Maybe you’re lucky and you just need to sprinkle in the occasional jQuery in the legacy app you’re maintaining. But things change.
At some point, the people at Facebook built React. Turns out that company with tens of thousands of engineers had two specialties all along: front-end and back-end. The programming hive-mind collectively decides that React is now the right way to build software but, at the same time, companies decide they can’t afford more engineers. Lo and behold the full-stack engineer is born and you’re it. Get to learning React and building REST APIs on top of the back-end tech you already know.
It won’t stop there. You know you need types, right? Add TypeScript. Are you really going to be managing state in React like a pleb? Add Redux. Feeling smart because you dodged both of those? Have fun figuring out to how to configure webpack/esbuild/rollup, plus Prettier, plus ESLint.
“Ok”, you say. “But I can keep doing things the way that I’ve been doing them. It worked fine. I don’t need React”. Of course you can. You can absolutely deviate from the way things are done everywhere in your fast-moving, money-burning startup. Just tell your boss that you’re available to teach the new hires — who’ve only ever heard of React — about the joys of server-side rendering.
Oh and, turns out we were just getting started.
Back when dinosaurs roamed the earth there was a type of professional called a System Administrator. Their whole job was to make sure that your backend was working nicely. They handled infrastructure changes, upgrading the database, system upgrades, keeping the daemon running, restarts, everything. Then came DevOps. Some cash-strapped company somewhere decided that now all of this would be handled by the engineers and everyone agreed. Now you need to learn Docker. Oh, your whole app is just a single statically linked binary and you don’t need Docker? Learn Ansible and I hope you have fun figuring out the options you need to pass to SystemD.
And you’re not even halfway there. Now you gotta learn AWS. You won’t be using the GUI to configure your infrastructure like a peasant so you better learn Terraform or Pulumi or whatever.
You do a good job. You’re promoted to manager. You need to learn a whole other job. But that’s ok because it’s the end-game. Bliss. Here’s some of the stuff you’ll need to do:
Guesstimate deadlines
Assign tasks to teammates
Spec tasks
Participate in annual reviews
Provide valuable feedback during product meetings
You better hope your company has quadrupled in number of employees by this point or you’ll be doing management plus all of the above.
And it can always get worse. A recruiter reached out to me a couple of days ago about an engineering position for a secret company. They decided that they required senior level skills in Rails, Hotwire and, incredibly, native mobile development. Why not add kernel and compiler development in there as well for good measure?
Software gets more complicated. All of this complexity is there for a reason. But what happened to specializing? When a house is being built, tons of people are involved: architects, civil engineers, plumbers, electricians, bricklayers, interior designers, roofers, surveyors, pavers, you name it. You don’t expect a single person, or even a whole single company, to be able to do all of those.
Maybe a future where we can build a whole app with a couple of prompts isn’t so bad.

data.title: Are FreeBSD Jails a Containers?
data.author: vermaden
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了FreeBSD Jails是否可以被称为容器（Containers）的问题。作者认为，FreeBSD Jails本质上就是容器技术，早在2000年FreeBSD就引入了Jails，这比Linux的容器技术早得多。Allan Jude在访谈中明确将Jails称为容器，并指出其他操作系统如Solaris和HP-UX也有类似的容器技术。文章还提到，尽管Linux的Docker和Podman等工具使“容器”一词流行起来，但这并不意味着只有这些工具定义的才是容器。作者反对将容器技术的定义局限于Linux的实现，认为这是一种对历史的误读。文章最后通过类比汽车类型，强调不应因为新技术的流行而改变历史上的定义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FreeBSD Jails与Linux容器技术的比较及其定位

不同观点：
• sshine认为，过去为了强调FreeBSD Jails相对于普通容器的优势，特别是安全性，刻意区分了两者。但随着容器技术在全球基础设施中变得流行，并且人们开始寻找云平台之外的解决方案，FreeBSD可能需要重新强调其拥有容器技术，以吸引非云用户的注意。

• tombert认为，Jails可以被视为容器，并且与Docker类似，都属于轻量级虚拟化技术。他指出，Jails和Docker都共享主机内核，相比于QEMU或bhyve等技术有更低的系统开销。虽然Docker更具声明性，但本质上还是基于cgroups等底层技术。他还提到自己曾经是BSD Now节目的听众，并对其中的主持人的观点表示认同。

• dpe82认为，这个讨论像是为了争论术语而争论，感觉像是在纠缠于语义问题。

• jmclnx表示，曾经使用过Jails，并坚信Jails比Linux的容器技术更安全。

• TZubiri提到，自己在Hacker News和Reddit上曾与人就此问题发生过争论。他曾主张容器是一种虚拟化技术，但遭到反对。他表示没有精力去翻找过去的讨论记录，但如果有人愿意可以去查找。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对Jails和容器技术在不同场景下的安全性、技术实现及使用体验的比较。
• 争议的焦点在于Jails是否应该被称为容器，以及其与Linux容器技术和Docker的异同。
• 一些人认为这是语义上的争论，而另一些人则基于实际使用经验和安全性来支持自己的立场。

43617559.article_content:
I believe its not the first time – that when I post some article and it contains
FreeBSD Jails
and
Containers
in one sentence – it sparks vigorous discussions about it.
They were these at least:
Minecraft Server in FreeBSD Jails Container
Secure Containerized Browser
FreeBSD Jails Containers
RabbitMQ Cluster on FreeBSD Containers
Some people agree with me – that
FreeBSD Jails
are
Containers
– and some really do not.
Today I will try to find the last and only answer to that case.
Arguments For
IMHO the term
Containers
is not reserved to
Linux
Podman
/
Docker
solutions. The term
Containers
was in the
BSD/UNIX
land long before
Docker
or
Podman
saw any light of day – and yet – now the new kids on the block are to decide what to call a
Container
or not?
The
FreeBSD Jails
were introduced in year 2000 as a
Container
technology – some called it improved
chroot(8)
on steroids also.
Well known to everybody not only in the
FreeBSD
world
Allan Jude
recently told in the
Changelog Interviews – 574 – Lets Talk FreeBSD
episode the following things.
“FreeBSD pioneered the practical implementation of
containers
in the year 2000, whereas we only saw
containers
and
namespaces
on
Linux
come much, much later. Now, it’s gotten maybe a lot more built on top of it since then, but the concept came originally from
BSD
.”
… and later in the same interview …
“FreeBSD’s
container
concept is called
Jails
. They basically are a
chroot(8)
that contains a different install of the OS, that can have other packages, and so on. And they have a restriction on which IP addresses it can use, and you can lock it down. It’s since grown a bunch of features, like the network
namespaces
, kind of like on
Linux
, where you can have this basically be almost like a lightweight VM. It has its own network stack, its own files, everything… and that’s how I run Plex on my
FreeBSD
ZFS machine, is I just have a
Jail
, and then inside that
Jail
I install the Plex package from
FreeBSD
‘s package system.”
… and more …
“And that concept has continued to grow, and Sun saw that concept and built their concept of
Zones
based on top of that… and that’s why ZFS has specific support for delegating datasets to a
container
. Because
Solaris
had its own concept that they borrowed the idea from
FreeBSD
. And then full circle, eventually ZFS comes back to
FreeBSD
and
Linux
, and support for those has landed.”
… and later …
“But it also has a concept called
VNET
, where you can have a completely isolated separate copy of the
FreeBSD
network stack. So in those
containers
, they can have their own complete network stack; that means they can have their own firewall. So each
container
can have its own complete separate firewall, with its own firewall rules. They can even have conflicting IP addresses. So you have two
containers
that have the same IP addresses, and as long as you don’t link them together, they won’t see each other and won’t have a conflict.”
In other words –
Allan Jude
referred to the
FreeBSD Jails
as
Containers
all the time.
In 2004 Sun introduced
Solaris Containers
(also known as
Solaris Zones
) – they were introduced 4 years after
FreeBSD Jails
happened and they both do exactly the same
OS Level Virtualization
.
HP with its
HP-UX
system – which last
11i v3
(B.11.31) official release was in 2007 (there were some patches after that) has
HP-UX Virtual Partitions

43617559.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了FreeBSD Jails是否可以被称为容器（Containers）的问题。作者认为，FreeBSD Jails本质上就是容器技术，早在2000年FreeBSD就引入了Jails，这比Linux的容器技术早得多。Allan Jude在访谈中明确将Jails称为容器，并指出其他操作系统如Solaris和HP-UX也有类似的容器技术。文章还提到，尽管Linux的Docker和Podman等工具使“容器”一词流行起来，但这并不意味着只有这些工具定义的才是容器。作者反对将容器技术的定义局限于Linux的实现，认为这是一种对历史的误读。文章最后通过类比汽车类型，强调不应因为新技术的流行而改变历史上的定义。
43617559.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FreeBSD Jails与Linux容器技术的比较及其定位

不同观点：
• sshine认为，过去为了强调FreeBSD Jails相对于普通容器的优势，特别是安全性，刻意区分了两者。但随着容器技术在全球基础设施中变得流行，并且人们开始寻找云平台之外的解决方案，FreeBSD可能需要重新强调其拥有容器技术，以吸引非云用户的注意。

• tombert认为，Jails可以被视为容器，并且与Docker类似，都属于轻量级虚拟化技术。他指出，Jails和Docker都共享主机内核，相比于QEMU或bhyve等技术有更低的系统开销。虽然Docker更具声明性，但本质上还是基于cgroups等底层技术。他还提到自己曾经是BSD Now节目的听众，并对其中的主持人的观点表示认同。

• dpe82认为，这个讨论像是为了争论术语而争论，感觉像是在纠缠于语义问题。

• jmclnx表示，曾经使用过Jails，并坚信Jails比Linux的容器技术更安全。

• TZubiri提到，自己在Hacker News和Reddit上曾与人就此问题发生过争论。他曾主张容器是一种虚拟化技术，但遭到反对。他表示没有精力去翻找过去的讨论记录，但如果有人愿意可以去查找。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对Jails和容器技术在不同场景下的安全性、技术实现及使用体验的比较。
• 争议的焦点在于Jails是否应该被称为容器，以及其与Linux容器技术和Docker的异同。
• 一些人认为这是语义上的争论，而另一些人则基于实际使用经验和安全性来支持自己的立场。

主要讨论点：对某政权处决腐败官员的看法

不同观点：
• Suraci认为该政权的行为是野蛮的，直接将其定性为野蛮政权，并指出该政权处决腐败官员的做法不符合法治原则。Suraci还提到，这些"共产主义者"应该向西方学习法治。
• 潜在反对观点（可以从语气中推测）：可能有人认为该政权处决腐败官员是为了维护正义和法律，这种做法在某些立场下可能被视为严厉但有效的反腐措施，而非单纯违反法治。

补充讨论：
• Suraci的观点带有明显的意识形态对立，将"共产主义者"与西方对立起来，认为西方的法治体系更优越。
• 争议的焦点在于对腐败官员的严厉惩罚是否符合法治精神。一方认为这是野蛮的行为，缺乏法治原则中的公正审判和适当惩罚；另一方可能认为这是对腐败的有效威慑，符合某种形式的法律执行。
• 该评论还隐含了对西方政治制度的推崇，可能引发关于东西方法治和政治制度优劣的更广泛讨论。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：与跳蛛相关的视频内容引发的讨论，包括对跳蛛行为的科学分析、对视频制作质量的评价以及对观众互动的讨论。

不同观点：
• 一些评论者对跳蛛的行为表现出极大的兴趣和赞赏，认为这些蜘蛛表现出类似人类的情感和反应。例如，有评论指出跳蛛会表现出好奇心和探索行为，这让人感到它们有某种程度的“人性”。

• 另一部分评论者则对这种拟人化的看法持怀疑态度，认为将人类情感投射到动物身上是不科学的。他们强调跳蛛的行为是由本能驱动，而不是出于情感或意识。

• 部分观众对视频的制作质量和拍摄技巧表示赞赏，认为视频制作者成功地捕捉到了跳蛛的细微行为，并以一种引人入胜的方式呈现出来。

• 也有观众指出视频中的一些科学 inaccuracies（不准确之处），并对其中某些结论提出质疑。他们认为视频制作者在解释跳蛛行为时存在过度简化或误导性的信息。

• 还有评论讨论了观众对这类内容的反应，认为跳蛛视频的流行反映了公众对自然和科学内容的需求，但也可能导致错误信息的传播，因为许多人可能缺乏足够的科学背景知识去判断内容的真伪。

补充讨论：
• 有评论提到视频平台的算法推荐可能影响观众的观看体验，使得类似内容更容易被推送给已经对跳蛛感兴趣的观众，从而形成某种“信息茧房”。

• 对于跳蛛是否真的具有某种程度的认知能力，评论中存在一定争议。一些评论者引用科学研究来支持跳蛛具有复杂行为能力的观点，而另一些评论者则认为现有证据不足以支持这种结论。

• 最后，有评论讨论了科学传播的难度，指出科学家和视频制作者在向公众传达准确且易于理解的信息时面临的挑战。这一讨论强调了科学素养和批判性思维的重要性。

data.title: Lessons from open source in the Mexican government
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 本文总结了Federico González Waite在SCALE 22x会议上分享的墨西哥政府采用开源软件的经验。他指出，尽管开源软件能降低成本并提升国家的“IT主权”，但政府在采用过程中遇到了诸多阻力。墨西哥希望通过开源软件减少对专有软件和供应商的依赖，实现IT自主，并培养本地技术人才，从技术消费国转变为技术生产国。然而，政府内部的腐败和缺乏技术知识导致了一些项目失败。González Waite曾领导多个开源项目，包括电子护照系统，但在不同政府角色中推动变革并不容易。他目前致力于帮助他人向开源转型，并关注未来的技术趋势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源软件（OSS）与专有软件在政府及企业中的使用及相关问题

不同观点：
• [huijzer] 和 [firejake308] 提到专有软件公司（如Microsoft和Oracle）利用各种手段（如免费顾问服务、威胁恐吓）来维持客户锁定。这些公司通过影响政府决策来打压开源软件的应用，并在客户尝试转向开源时进行许可证审计以制造障碍。

• [looofooo0] 引用经济网络理论解释专有软件公司的商业模式，强调软件公司的价值与客户切换成本密切相关。公司通过锁定客户来维持增长，特别是在成熟市场中。

• [bruce511] 指出在IT决策中，许可证成本只是其中一个因素，其他成本（如培训和支持）同样重要。虽然开源软件在某些情况下是合适的选择（如PostgreSQL替代Oracle），但在其他情况下，专有软件由于用户熟悉度和支持服务可能更具优势。

• [pritambarhate] 主张政府应资助开源基金会，以培养和保留优秀的编程人才，确保重要开源软件的长期维护，从而更好地服务于政府部门和公民。

• [wjholden] 认为开源软件在传统企业中逐渐增长，但由于云计算和人工智能的兴起，未来企业对数据库和模型的控制力减弱，可能使开源迁移变得更加困难。

• [grg0] 批评美国科技公司为牟利不择手段，憎恨免费软件，因为开源软件威胁到他们的商业模式。

• [ptsd_dalmatian] 质疑政府在微软产品上的巨额花费，建议将这些资金用于教育和医疗等公共服务，并指出政府透明度不足，难以了解实际支出。

补充讨论：
• [specialist] 提出利用FOSS（自由及开源软件）实现“公民拥有的软件”的愿景，建议各司法管辖区联合分担成本和风险，以克服专有软件的复杂性和高成本，并分享了在FOSS项目中遇到的挑战和经验。

• [pessimizer] 和 [timewizard] 提到腐败问题，指出在政府软件采购中存在将许可证置于私人名下以牟利的行为，导致服务锁定和腐败风险，并强调缺乏专业标准和文档是技术项目失败的原因之一。

争议焦点：
• 专有软件公司是否利用政治和法律手段打压开源软件的应用，以及这些手段的道德和法律问题。
• 开源软件在政府和企业中的适用性，以及是否应通过政策和资金支持来推广开源软件的应用。

Lessons from open source in the Mexican government
Ready to give LWN a try?
With a subscription to LWN, you can stay current with what is happening in the Linux and free-software community and take advantage of subscriber-only site features.  We are pleased to offer you
a free trial subscription
, no credit card required, so that you can see for yourself.  Please, join us!
By
Jake Edge
March 24, 2025
SCALE
The adoption of open-source software in governments has had its ups and
downs.  While open source seems like a "no-brainer", it turns out that
governments can be surprisingly resistant to using FOSS for a variety of
reasons.  Federico González Waite spoke in the Open Government track at
SCALE 22x
in Pasadena,
California to recount his
experiences
working with and for the Mexican government
.  He led multiple projects
to switch away from proprietary, often predatory, software companies with
some success—and failure.
González Waite began by noting that he is a Mexican/Kiwi ("
there's not
many of us
", he said with a grin), who spent nine or ten years in
high-level roles in the Mexican government "
promoting open-source
implementations
".  Among other things, he was the CTO for the Ministry
of Foreign Affairs; "
I am actually responsible for Mexicans having an
electronic passport today.
" That was one of the projects that he led
and part of it was done with open-source software, which is something that
people find to be amazing, González Waite said.  He served in the office for
national strategy under President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, eventually
moving into the CEO role at the National Research and Innovation Center for
Mexico.
In all of his roles, he advocated using open source within the government;
it is never easy to be a "change-maker" of that sort, he said.  He left the
government at the recent change of presidents (to Claudia Scheinbaum) and
is now working on "
helping people do their own transformations
" to
open source, while keeping an eye out for the next big thing.  He noted
that he would take questions at the end and he might not be able to answer
them all due to confidentiality responsibilities, but he is "
no longer a
public official, so that gives me a lot more leeway to talk freely
".
Why?
"
So why open source for the government?
"  One reason is to cut
costs; Mexico is a financially small, developing country that is always
looking to reduce costs, he said.  Paying for licensing was costing a lot
of money that could be used to do other things.  The López Obrador
administration passed an austerity plan into law, so that various
actions (e.g. government officials traveling out of the country for work)
needed presidential-level approval.  That also affected purchasing licenses
and the plan pushed the use of open source.
Another major reason is to work toward Mexico having "IT sovereignty".  One
major problem that the country has had is that its IT leadership is not
technical, which means that people were signing off on projects and
licenses without understanding what they were buying. "
They really
didn't know if they are were getting good value for [the] money
".
There is a need to build up the talent within the government to support
open-source software; "
there's no point in building a whole
infrastructure on open source if you don't have the talent to keep it
up
".  There has been a lot of effort to bring in new people and to
train existing workers to that end.  One goal is to go from being an
IT-consumer nation to being an IT-producing nation.  It is surprising to many
who think of Mexico as a manufacturing and assembly nation that the
country does actually produce a lot of technology, he said.  Much of what
was being produced within the government, though, was being siphoned off by
the private sector; more recently, that is changing, so that the government
can package and even sell its IT development.
Another goal is for Mexico to become more self-sufficient, so that it is
not locked-in by vendors of various sorts.  In his most recent role, he was
able to see what was happening all across the government.  One common
thread is that when agencies were asked why they were spending so much on a
particular service, they claimed they had no choice, even though there are
lots of other companies offering the same services.  It turned out that
various contracted companies had corruptly put the software licenses they
bought for the government into
their own names, leading to a lock-in
for their services.  Moving to open source can break those and other kinds
of locks.
There are multiple agencies within the government to handle various pieces
of the technology puzzle, González Waite said.  He headed
INFOTEC
, which is the IT service
provider to the rest of the government.  I

• [looofooo0] 引用经济网络理论解释专有软件公司的商业模式，强调软件公司的价值与客户切换成本密切相关。公司通过锁定客户来维持增长，特别是在成熟市场中。

• [bruce511] 指出在IT决策中，许可证成本只是其中一个因素，其他成本（如培训和支持）同样重要。虽然开源软件在某些情况下是合适的选择（如PostgreSQL替代Oracle），但在其他情况下，专有软件由于用户熟悉度和支持服务可能更具优势。

• [pritambarhate] 主张政府应资助开源基金会，以培养和保留优秀的编程人才，确保重要开源软件的长期维护，从而更好地服务于政府部门和公民。

• [wjholden] 认为开源软件在传统企业中逐渐增长，但由于云计算和人工智能的兴起，未来企业对数据库和模型的控制力减弱，可能使开源迁移变得更加困难。

• [grg0] 批评美国科技公司为牟利不择手段，憎恨免费软件，因为开源软件威胁到他们的商业模式。

• [ptsd_dalmatian] 质疑政府在微软产品上的巨额花费，建议将这些资金用于教育和医疗等公共服务，并指出政府透明度不足，难以了解实际支出。

补充讨论：
• [specialist] 提出利用FOSS（自由及开源软件）实现“公民拥有的软件”的愿景，建议各司法管辖区联合分担成本和风险，以克服专有软件的复杂性和高成本，并分享了在FOSS项目中遇到的挑战和经验。

• [pessimizer] 和 [timewizard] 提到腐败问题，指出在政府软件采购中存在将许可证置于私人名下以牟利的行为，导致服务锁定和腐败风险，并强调缺乏专业标准和文档是技术项目失败的原因之一。

争议焦点：
• 专有软件公司是否利用政治和法律手段打压开源软件的应用，以及这些手段的道德和法律问题。
• 开源软件在政府和企业中的适用性，以及是否应通过政策和资金支持来推广开源软件的应用。

data.title: What if we made advertising illegal?
data.author: smnrg
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提出一个大胆的设想：禁止所有广告。作者认为，现代广告不仅通过操纵情感来促销产品，还破坏了民主和社会结构。禁止广告将消除数字内容成瘾的财务动机，摧毁个性化、扭曲现实的泡沫，并迫使政治家和商业机构回归现实。作者强调，广告本质上是宣传，通过绕过理性思考来触发购买决定，且侵犯个人隐私。尽管这一提议看似激进且不现实，但作者认为反思广告对社会的毒害本身就是一种解放行为。最终，作者希望未来社会会将当前泛滥的广告视为一种野蛮行为，就像如今看待童工和公开处决一样。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：广告的本质及其社会影响，是否应该禁止广告，以及如何在实际操作中进行监管。

不同观点：
• [gcp123, stego-tech, marenkay, hansmayer, hendayet, amarant] 认为当前的广告系统本质上是操纵性和寄生性的，对社会有负面影响。他们支持激进改革，甚至全面禁止广告，认为广告更多是操纵而非提供信息。
  
• [dash2] 强烈反对全面禁止广告的提议，认为这是不切实际的幻想，且会侵犯言论自由。他指出广告在某些情况下是有用的，并且提出了如何界定广告的实际问题，如付费演讲或免费样品是否算广告。

• [toomim, amarant] 提出如何界定广告与其它形式的自由言论的问题。他们质疑是否应该禁止所有商业言论，以及如何在实际操作中划定界限，比如服务员推荐酒水或商家招牌是否算广告。

• [Animats, rsolva, iambateman] 支持逐步改革，提出一些实际可行的措施，如禁止大型广告牌、限制数字广告中的个人数据跟踪，或使广告不可抵扣税款。他们认为可以从小处着手，逐步推动更大范围的变革。

• [gameman144] 认为广告本身有其价值，特别是在产品发现和市场竞争中起到积极作用。他反对全面禁止广告，主张对广告实践进行严格的监管，而非彻底否定广告的存在。

• [miki123211] 提出广告对经济和娱乐行业的补贴作用，认为广告类似于一种税收，对社会有正面影响。他主张在讨论广告监管时，应考虑广告带来的贸易offs，而非一味禁止。

• [willsmith72] 完全反对禁止广告的提议，认为广告有积极作用，如帮助消费者发现新产品。他还质疑了文章中关于数字内容成瘾性的论点，认为娱乐需求不会因广告消失而改变。

• [doug-moen] 提供历史视角，指出互联网早期广告是非法的，支持广告并非互联网内在必要的观点。他认为可以恢复到无广告或少广告的状态，因为历史上已经实现过。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于广告是否本质上具有操纵性以及是否应该全面禁止广告。反对者认为全面禁止不切实际且侵犯言论自由，而支持者认为当前的广告系统是寄生性的，需要激进变革。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是如何在实际操作中界定广告，以及如何在不完全禁止的情况下对广告进行有效监管。
• 广告对社会的经济贡献及其负面影响之间的权衡也是讨论的核心，涉及到广告是否应该以及如何被限制或改革。

43595269.article_content:
What if we made all advertising illegal? It's such a wild idea that I've never heard it in the public discourse.
Even saying it seems so far outside the Overton window that it makes nuking hurricanes sound reasonable (as some politicians proposed).
But why? It makes perfect sense. The financial incentives to create addictive digital content would instantly disappear, and so would the mechanisms that allow both commercial and political actors to create personalized, reality-distorting bubbles:
Clickbait, listicles, and affiliate marketing schemes would become worthless overnight.
Algorithm-driven platforms like Instagram and TikTok that
harvest and monetize attention
, destroying youth, would lose their economic foundation.
Facebook, X, Google, YouTube—all would cease to exist in their current forms.
Ad companies are never going to regulate themselves—it's like hoping for heroin dealers to write drug laws.
Think about what's happened since 2016: Populists exploit ad marketplaces, using them to bypass traditional media gatekeepers and deliver tailored messages to susceptible audiences. Foreign actors do the same, microtargeting divisive content to fracture our social fabric along existing fault lines.
Outlawing advertising would help protect and reinvigorate our minds and democracy.
Even as an advertiser (
especially
as an advertiser), I am convinced that outlawing advertising is the best thing we can do for our world now. More than gun control. More than tackling climate change. More than lowering the price of eggs.
Removing these advanced manipulation tools would force everyone—politicians included—to snap back into reality. By outlawing advertising, the machinery of mass delusion would lose its most addictive and toxic fuel.
Any form of paid and/or third-party advertising would become illegal. Full stop.
The idea feels like sci-fi because you're so used to it, imagining ads gone feels like asking to outlaw gravity. But humanity had been free of current forms of advertising for 99.9% of its existence. Word-of-mouth and community networks worked just fine. First-party websites and online communities would now improve on that.
The traditional argument pro-advertising—that it provides consumers with necessary information—hasn't been valid for decades. In our information-saturated world, ads manipulate, but they don't inform.
The modern advertising apparatus exists to
bypass rational thought
and trigger emotional responses that lead to purchasing decisions. A sophisticated machine designed to short-circuit your agency, normalized to the point of invisibility.
“But it's free speech!”
Bullshit. No one is entitled to yell at you “GET 20% OFF THIS UNDERWEAR YOU GLANCED AT YESTERDAY” with a dopamine megaphone in your bedroom. And to track 90% of your life to know when and how to say it. That's not free speech, that's harassment.
When I say advertising, I also mean propaganda. Propaganda is advertising for the state, and advertising is propaganda for the private. Same thing.
I know this proposal won't be implemented tomorrow. But even just stepping back from constant consumption and contemplating what poisons our democracy is a liberating act in itself. An action against that blurry, “out-of-focus fascism”—that sense of discomfort that you feel but can't quite point out (I'm preparing a longer essay about that.) In this world,
any
mindfulness act—stopping to think rather than reacting—represents
a micro-awakening of the self
.
I know, it sounds surreal. Yet, many things once thought impossible are now considered basic standards of a decent society.
I think there's a world where we'll look back on our advertising-saturated era with the same bewilderment with which we now regard cigarette smoke, child labor, or public executions: a barbaric practice that we allowed to continue far too long because we couldn't imagine an alternative.

data.title: Smallest Pacemaker Is the Size of a Rice Grain
data.author: lnyan
data.article_summary: 科学家研发出全球最小的临时起搏器，体积小于一粒米，可通过注射植入并用光控调节，最终在体内溶解。传统临时起搏器需通过手术植入并连接到体外设备，移除时可能造成损伤。而这款无线起搏器厚度仅1毫米，长3.5毫米，可溶解于体内，避免了侵入性手术。起搏器与佩戴在胸部的软贴片配合使用，贴片检测到心律不齐时会通过光信号控制起搏器。该设备已在动物和人体组织实验中取得成功，预计两到三年内可进行人体测试。专家称其为“变革性突破”，未来可能应用于神经再生、伤口愈合等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于医疗植入物的技术细节和可行性

不同观点：
• [jamesgasek] 认为所讨论的植入物体积较大，类似于一颗巨大的米粒，暗示其尺寸可能在实际应用中显得不够精细或过于显眼。

• [echoangle] 关注植入物的注射方式和精度问题，提出该植入物需要靠近心脏，但质疑如何在心脏跳动的情况下精确注射，以及是否依赖手动瞄准或使用专门的装置进行对齐。

• [userbinator] 提出该植入物的设计目的是在不再需要时自行溶解，以避免患者接受侵入性手术。不过，他对此持怀疑态度，特别是如果植入物包含活性电子和半导体材料，因为这些材料不太可能溶解。

补充讨论：
• [userbinator] 在后续补充中要求对上述观点进行反驳，显示出对该技术可行性的质疑，并关注植入物材料的长期影响。

• 争议的焦点在于植入物的尺寸是否实际可行，以及其材料（特别是电子元件）能否在体内安全溶解或长期留存。

43585911.article_content:
Breakthrough: World's Smallest Pacemaker Is The Size of a Rice Grain
Health
03 April 2025
By
Daniel Lawler, AFP
Smaller than a grain of rice, this new pacemaker could transform cardiac medicine.
(John A. Rogers)
Scientists said Wednesday
they have developed the world's tiniest pacemaker, a temporary heartbeat regulator smaller than a grain of rice that can be injected and controlled by light before dissolving.
While still years away from being tested in humans, the wireless pacemaker was hailed as a "transformative breakthrough" that could spur advances in other areas of medicine.
Millions of people across the world have permanent pacemakers, which stimulate hearts with electrical pulses to ensure they beat normally.
The US-led team of researchers behind the new device said they were motivated to help the one percent of children born with congenital heart defects who need a temporary pacemaker in the week after surgery.
The pacemaker could also help adults restore a normal heartbeat as they recover from heart surgery.
Currently, temporary pacemakers require surgery to sew electrodes onto heart muscles, with wires connecting to a powered device on the patient's chest.
When the pacemaker is no longer needed, doctors or nurses pull out the wires, which can sometimes cause damage.
Neil Armstrong, the first person to walk on
the Moon
, died from internal bleeding after his temporary pacemaker was removed in 2012.
But the newly developed pacemaker is wireless. And at just one millimetre thick and 3.5 millimetres long, it can fit into the tip of a syringe.
It has also been designed to dissolve into the body when no longer needed, sparing patients invasive surgery.
Significant leap forward
The pacemaker is paired to a soft patch worn on the patient's chest, according to a study describing the device in the journal
Nature
.
When the patch detects irregular heartbeats, it automatically flashes light that tells the pacemaker what heartbeat it should stimulate.
The pacemaker is powered by what is called a galvanic cell, which uses the body's fluids to convert chemical energy into electrical pulses that stimulate the heart.
So far, the pacemaker has worked effectively in tests on mice, rats, pigs, dogs and human heart tissue in the lab, according to the study.
Senior study author John Rogers of Northwestern University in the United States told AFP he estimated the pacemaker could be tested in humans in two to three years.
His lab has launched a start-up to pursue this goal, he added.
In the future, the underlying technology could also "create unique and powerful strategies to address societal challenges in human health," Rogers said.
Bozhi Tian, whose lab at the University of Chicago has also developed light-activated pacemakers but was not involved in the latest research, called it a "significant leap forward".
"This new pacemaker is a transformative breakthrough in medical technology," he told AFP.
"It's a paradigm shift in temporary pacing and bioelectronic medicine, opening up possibilities far beyond cardiology – including nerve regeneration, wound healing and integrated smart implants."
Heart disease is the world's leading cause of death, according to the
World Health Organization
.

data.author: hilux
data.article_summary: 在新德里的Nehru Place，技术人员通过从废弃电子设备中拆解和重组笔记本电脑的零件，创造出低成本的“混合”笔记本。这些“弗兰肯斯坦”笔记本由不同品牌的二手部件组装而成，满足了学生和自由职业者对廉价且功能正常设备的需求。由于全球科技公司通过限制备件和使用专有技术增加维修难度，推动计划报废，这些维修技师正面临巨大挑战。尽管印度政府开始讨论维修权法律，但进展缓慢，维修店仍依赖非正式的电子废物市场获取零件。这项工作不仅让旧技术重获新生，还减少了电子废物对环境的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子产品维修文化的消失与复兴，以及现代电子设备不可修复的问题。

不同观点：
• saidinesh5：回忆了自己在小镇上通过电视和收音机维修店学习并实践电子维修的经历，认为如今的电子设备越来越不可修复，维修店逐渐消失。提倡通过类似创客空间的地方鼓励人们修复电子设备。
• robin_reala：提到中国一种独特的“修复”方式，将损坏屏幕的MacBook改装为无屏幕的键盘-CPU一体机，认为这是一种创新的修复方式。
• pjmlp：提到20世纪90年代以前，葡萄牙有很多维修店，但随着一次性社会的到来和计划报废策略，这些店逐渐消失。认为除非政府解决计划报废问题，否则修复文化难以回归。
• blackoil：认为修复的劳动力成本低于更换成本，但现代社会需要通过法律强制公司设计易于修复的产品，才能从根本上解决问题。
• rockyj：分享了在印度新德里Nehru Place的经历，那里曾经是繁忙的电子产品和维修市场，但现在由于交通和停车问题，体验变得较差，但仍然是一个硬件和游戏爱好者的天堂。

补充讨论：
• h4ck_th3_pl4n3t：提到一个定制Thinkpad的项目，通过将新主板和旧Thinkpad外壳结合，运行coreboot系统，展示了电子产品修复和改造的潜力。
• nxobject：表示希望学习现代主板维修技能，尤其是BGA部件的更换，并对非西方国家的这些技能表示钦佩。
• fifticon：分享了关于Asus等品牌的电子产品在保修期过后频繁损坏的经历，认为这是一种故意设计的计划报废策略，批评了这种商业模式。
• Brajeshwar：提到一位在印度班加罗尔通过技术自动化流程运营设备租赁和维修业务的朋友，展示了维修在商业模式中的重要性。
• ravirajx7：提到朋友在经济困难时通过Nehru Place以较低成本修复了笔记本电脑，但对使用翻新零件的可靠性表示担忧。
• FilosofumRex：在美国，所谓的维修店往往是处理被盗电子设备的“拆解店”，暗示了维修店在某些情况下的不正当运作。
• aamederen：认为通过修复和再利用来实现可持续发展是积极的，并提醒大家十年前的电脑仍然能满足大多数需求，不必追求最新设备。

争议焦点：
• 电子产品设计是否应考虑可修复性，以及如何通过法律和市场手段解决计划报废问题。
• 使用翻新和改造零件的可靠性和经济性。
• 维修店在不同地区的运作模式和声誉问题。

Tech
The rise of ‘Frankenstein’ laptops in New Delhi’s repair markets
﻿India’s repair culture gives new life to dead tech.
by
Hanan Zaffar
and
Danish Pandit
Photography by Danish Pandit / The Verge
Apr 7, 2025, 2:00 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
In a dimly lit, cluttered workshop in Delhi’s Nehru Place, the air hums with the sound of whirring drills and the crackle of soldering irons. Sushil Prasad, a 35-year-old technician, wipes the sweat off his brow as he carefully pieces together the guts of an old laptop. It is a daily ritual — resurrecting machines by stitching together motherboards, screens, and batteries scavenged from other trashed older laptops and e-waste — to create functional, low-cost devices.
“India has always had a repair culture … but companies are pushing planned obsolescence”
“Right now, there is a huge demand for such ‘hybrid’ laptops,” Prasad says, his hands swapping out a damaged motherboard. “Most people don’t care about having the latest model; they just want something that works and won’t break the bank.”
One of the streets where laptops are repaired at Nehru Place.
Across India, in metro markets from Delhi’s Nehru Place to Mumbai’s Lamington Road, technicians like Prasad are repurposing broken and outdated laptops that many see as junk. These “Frankenstein” machines — hybrids of salvaged parts from multiple brands — are sold to students, gig workers, and small businesses, offering a lifeline to those priced out of India’s growing digital economy.
“We take usable components from different older or discarded systems to create a new functioning unit. For instance, we salvage parts from old laptop motherboards, such as capacitors, mouse pads, transistors, diodes, and certain ICs and use them in the newly refurbished ones,” says Prasad.
Prasad holding a laptop motherboard at his shop.
As he explains, Manohar Singh, the owner of the workshop-slash-store where Prasad works, flips open a refurbished laptop while sitting on a rickety stool. The screen flickers to life, displaying a crisp image. He smiles — a sign that another machine has been successfully revived.
“We literally make them out of scrap! We also take in second-hand laptops and e-waste from countries like Dubai and China, fix them up, and sell them at half the price of a new one,” he explains.
“A college student or a freelancer can get a good machine for INR 10,000 [about $110 USD] instead of spending INR 70,000 [about $800 USD] on a brand-new one. For many, that difference means being able to work or study at all.”
A wide view of a bustling street in Nehru Place, home to hundreds of shops and workshops dealing in all types of electronic products, attracting thousands of customers daily.
Singh recalls a young engineering student who visited his shop last year, desperate for a laptop to complete his coursework. “He had saved up for months but was still short of money. I put together a machine for him from spare parts, and he left with tears in his eyes. That is when you know this work matters.”
But this booming market does not exist in isolation. It is entangled with a much larger battle, one between small repair technicians and global technology giants. While these Frankenstein laptops are a lifeline for many, the repair industry itself faces significant roadblocks. Many global manufacturers deliberately make repairs difficult by restricting access to spare parts, using proprietary screws, and implementing software locks that force customers to buy new devices instead of fixing old ones.
Two boys transport discarded computer CPUs on a bicycle in Seelampur, one of India’s largest e-waste hubs, where informal recycling is a major source of livelihood.
Satish Sinha, associate director at Toxics Link, a nonprofit working on waste management, believes repair technicians like Prasad and Singh are on the front lines of a larger battle.
“India has always had a repair culture, from fixing old radios to hand-me-down phones. But companies are pushing planned obsolescence, making repairs harder and forcing people to buy new devices instead,” Sinha says.
Prasad, a technician, works on discarded boards at his shop in Nehru Place.
“We need to encourage such reuse of materials. These repaired or new hybrid devices minimize waste by extending a product’s lifespan and reducing overall market waste. Reusing components cuts down on the need for new materials, lowering energy use, resource extraction, and environmental impact,” Sinha adds.
“These parts would end up in a landfill otherwise.”
The Indian government has
started discussions
on right-to-repair laws, inspired by similar efforts in the European Union and the United States. However, progress remains slow, and repair shops continue to operate in legal limbo, often forced to source different parts from informal and e-waste markets.

data.title: Unmasking EncryptHub: Help from ChatGPT and Opsec Blunders
data.author: marcusb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是Outpost24的KrakenLabs对新兴网络犯罪分子EncryptHub的第二部分调查报告。文章聚焦于EncryptHub过去十年的网络活动，特别是他一年前开始涉足网络犯罪的历程，以及他在此过程中犯下的运营安全（OPSEC）错误，尤其是密码管理的失误。EncryptHub原是一名自学计算机技术的普通人，曾从事各种技术工作并尝试自由职业开发。然而，由于收入不足，他于2024年转向网络犯罪，涉及诈骗和勒索软件。尽管如此，他仍渴望成为合法的安全研究员，甚至因发现两个CVE漏洞而获得微软的认可。文章还揭示了他多次重复使用简单密码，导致其犯罪活动被追踪和暴露。总体而言，EncryptHub是一个在正邪之间挣扎、但充满驱动力的个体。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对通过手机进行复杂操作的惊讶以及对密码管理和安全策略的讨论

不同观点：
• [bn-l] 认为通过手机完成复杂操作（如通过RDP进行远程桌面控制）是非常惊人的，尤其对于不擅长手机输入的人来说。他称赞年轻一代对手机的熟练使用，称之为"手机原生世代"。

• [perching_aix] 认为无论是否是"手机原生世代"，任何人都应该知道不把密码存储在浏览器中，并且应在敏感会话后及时登出。他指出浏览器密码管理器和本地密码管理器在安全性上没有显著区别，都会成为攻击目标。他还批评将安全问题归咎于用户并不是有效的安全策略。

• [immibis] 则关注文章的写作方式，指出作者没有很好地隐藏Arthur Skorik的名字，暗示文章可能涉及特定个人，存在一定的隐私或道德问题。

补充讨论：
• 关于密码管理，[perching_aix] 提出浏览器和本地密码管理器的安全性没有本质区别，都面临被攻击的风险，并建议关闭浏览器的数据同步功能以提高安全性。

• 争议的焦点之一是用户在安全问题中的责任。有人认为用户应采取更好的安全措施，但[perching_aix] 指出，将责任完全归咎于用户并非有效的安全策略。

• 另一个值得注意的点是[immibis] 对文章写作方式的批评，指出文章可能暴露了特定个人的信息，这涉及到隐私和伦理问题。

Unmasking EncryptHub: Help from ChatGPT & OPSEC blunders
Contents
Unmasking EncryptHub: Help from ChatGPT & OPSEC blunders
Research & Threat Intel
Last updated: 03 Apr 2025
Written By
KrakenLabs
Threat Intelligence Team, Outpost24
This is the second part of Outpost24’s KrakenLabs investigation into
EncryptHub
, an up-and-coming cybercriminal who has been gaining popularity in recent months and is heavily expanding and evolving operations at the time of writing. We’ve already published one article
explaining
EncryptHub’s
campaigns and TPPs, infrastructure, infection methods, and targets
.
This article will follow a different approach. We’ll explore
EncryptHub
’s last decade online with a particular focus on his one-year-old foray into cybercrime, the OPSEC mistakes he’s made along the way, and how he used ChatGPT as a faithful accomplice throughout. This way, we hope to give you a human image beyond the amorphous dark entity that the generic tag of ‘
Threat Actor
’ usually gives.
Who is EncryptHub?
When people think of cybercriminals, they tend to imagine high-tech, government-backed teams and elite hackers using cutting-edge technology. However, many hackers are normal people who at some point decided to follow a dark path. Due to OPSEC errors (detailed later) we were able to learn a lot about
Encrypthub
, most of which will remain private.
And to be clear, the purpose of this section is not to humiliate or dox the individual. It’s simply to shed light on the fact most cybercriminals are ordinary humans that lead mostly ordinary lives.
Early years
What follows is a brief account of
EncryptHub
’s life constructed from a cursory glance of his online activity. It is by no means exhaustive nor verified. There are also many details we have chosen not to share from his exposed information. However, it is not our job to pry into people’s private lives nor our intention to expose them.
About 10 years ago,
EncryptHub
fled his hometown in Ukraine due to an unknown incident, relocating to a new city, likely along the coast near Romania. There, he kept a low profile, probably working while self-studying computer science. He began seeking computer-related jobs, claiming experience in mobile repairs, system administration, call centre work, and junior-level programming. A year later, while still searching for work, he enrolled in online courses to improve his skills.
However, by early 2022, all his activity suddenly stopped. While Russia’s invasion of Ukraine could have played a role, we’ve seen strong evidence suggesting he ended up in
jail
for a while. Once released, he resumed his job search, this time offering
freelance
web and app development services, which gained some traction.
But the pay likely wasn’t enough, and after briefly trying
bug bounty
programs with little success, we believe he
pivoted to cybercrime
in the first half of 2024. Initially, he may have done some  grunt work in campaigns related to vishing and ransomware. This likely fuelled his interest in vulnerability research and malware development, which led to the various campaigns that shone a light on upon him and have been thoroughly documented both by us and many other security researchers.
Journey into cybercrime
Despite his descent into a life of cybercrime, he didn’t abandon his aspirations as a legitimate security researcher and his efforts eventually paid off. While writing this report,
SkorikARI
, another username used by
EncryptHub
, was acknowledged by MSRC (Microsoft Security Response Center) for the findings of
CVE-2025-24071
and
CVE-2025-24061
, both very likely exploited in some of his campaigns
[1]
[2]
.
This brings us to the present, and to the picture of a conflicted man. Someone who has perhaps not had the easiest life, and has struggled to choose between a legitimate career and cybercrime and trying to play both roles at the same time. Whatever his motivations, he is clearly a
driven
individual with a desire to learn.
OPSEC mistakes: Exposing your crimes for the world to see
As we outlined in our
previous report
on
EncryptHub
, the actor made several fundamental operational mistakes that enabled us to collect a vast wealth of information, providing a pretty clear picture of his activities.
Password management
One of the most glaring mistakes made by our subject was the
reuse of passwords
. Just as an example, in a single file exfiltrated by his own malware, 82 out of 200 accounts shared nearly identical passwords, with only slight variations like a single character change or an extra letter at the end. To make matters worse, many of these passwords lacked complexity—short and composed solely of alphanumeric characters.
This is far from a trivial issue. With such prominent repetition, credentials for accounts that were not present in that file could have been easily guessed. And the accounts were not trivial either. There was repetition in accounts for EncryptRAT C2 domains, bulletproof hosting, re

data.title: Listening habits and effects of background music in people with and without ADHD
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章研究了年轻成年人在日常活动中听背景音乐的习惯，特别是比较了有和没有ADHD症状的个体之间的差异。研究发现，ADHD筛查组的受试者在认知需求较低的活动（如清洁、运动）和学习时，听背景音乐的频率显著高于神经典型发育组。此外，ADHD组更倾向于听刺激性音乐，而不论活动类型如何。总体而言，两组受试者都认为听背景音乐对他们的情绪和认知活动有积极影响，但在音乐选择和偏好上存在一些差异。神经典型发育组在进行高认知需求活动时更喜欢放松、器乐、熟悉且自选的音乐，而ADHD组则偏好刺激性、带歌词的音乐。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：音乐、ADHD与专注力之间的关系，以及一项研究的可信度

不同观点：
• [ddmf] 认为音乐在进行无聊任务时有帮助，但在需要专注工作时会分心。他还分享了自己在被诊断为注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）之前，通过观看世界烹饪视频来保持专注的个人经验。

• [nathanwh] 对一项研究的可信度提出质疑，指出该研究没有要求ADHD的正式诊断，而是依赖于症状问卷来区分参与者。此外，研究中的神经发育障碍及其他心理健康问题的比例过高（超过20%），也让人怀疑其科学性。

• [p0w3n3d] 提出一个个人观察，当他处于专注状态时，往往会在脑海中创造背景音乐，暗示音乐的存在感不一定需要外在的播放源。

• [sinuhe69] 对学术论文的质量表示不满，认为该研究只是强调青少年经常听音乐，并批评ADHD被当作吸引注意的噱头。他对现代学术论文的质量表示担忧。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是研究方法的可信度，尤其是未经过正式诊断而依赖症状问卷的做法是否科学。
• [ddmf] 的个人经验提供了一种与ADHD相关的应对机制，即通过特定活动来保持专注，但这种经验并不一定具有普遍性。
• [sinuhe69] 对现代学术研究质量的批评引发了对学术严谨性和ADHD作为诊断类别的讨论。
• [p0w3n3d] 的观点则提示了音乐在专注状态中可能的自发性，增加了讨论的趣味性和复杂性。

data.author: opusg5
data.article_summary: ReGenNexus Core是一个由ReGen Designs LLC开发的开源实现，旨在提供通用代理协议（UAP）的标准通信框架，使数字实体能够无缝交互。其核心功能包括标准化的消息协议、实体注册与发现系统、会话状态管理以及基本的安全认证和加密。项目提供了详细的入门指南、核心协议文档、API参考和容器化支持。通过Docker可轻松部署，并包含简单连接、多代理通信、事件驱动模式和安全功能等示例。ReGenNexus欢迎贡献，并遵循MIT许可证发布。

ReGenNexus Core - Universal Agent Protocol
ReGenNexus Core is an open-source implementation of the Universal Agent Protocol (UAP) developed by ReGen Designs LLC. It provides a standardized communication framework for digital entities to interact seamlessly.
Core Features
Message Protocol
: Standardized message format for entity communication
Entity Registry
: Discovery and registration system for digital entities
Context Management
: Conversation state and history tracking
Basic Security
: Authentication and encryption for secure communication

data.title: The speech police: Chairman Brendan Carr and the FCC's news distortion policy
data.author: LinuxBender
data.article_summary:
联邦通信委员会（FCC）主席布兰登·卡尔正采取强硬立场，指责广播电视台对共和党和特朗普总统存在偏见。他引用了一条很少执行的**新闻失实政策**，威胁可能撤销广播许可证。然而，他的两位前任——民主党人杰西卡·罗森沃塞尔和共和党人阿吉特·派——都认为，基于新闻内容惩罚电视台违反了第一修正案的言论自由权。多位前FCC主席也敦促卡尔改变方向。

卡尔对CBS编辑卡玛拉·哈里斯采访的调查引发了自由派和保守派团体的谴责，认为这是对宪法权利的威胁。批评者称卡尔的调查是“政治噱头”和“违宪的监管滥用”。学者和法律专家指出，FCC选择性地执行政策可能导致法律挑战。历史上，FCC曾通过**公平原则**（1949年引入，1987年废除）监管新闻，但后来逐渐减少对新闻的管控，以保护言论自由。

Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr is taking a hard line against broadcast TV stations accused of bias against Republicans and President Trump. To pressure broadcasters, Carr is invoking the rarely enforced
news distortion policy
that was developed starting in the
late 1960s
and says the FCC should consider
revoking broadcast licenses
.
The FCC has regulatory authority over broadcasters with licenses to use the public airwaves. But Carr's two immediate predecessors—Democrat Jessica Rosenworcel and Republican Ajit Pai—both
said
that punishing stations based on the content of news programs would violate the First Amendment right to free speech.
Rosenworcel and Pai's agreement continued a decades-long trend of the FCC easing itself out of the news-regulation business. Two other former FCC chairs—
Republican Alfred Sikes and Democrat Tom Wheeler
—have urged Carr to change course.
Carr has multiple probes in progress, and his investigation into CBS over the editing of an interview with Kamala Harris has drawn condemnations from both liberal and conservative advocacy groups that describe it as a threat to the Constitutional right to free speech. One plea to drop the investigation came in a March 19
letter
from conservative groups including the Center for Individual Freedom, Grover Norquist's Americans for Tax Reform, and the Taxpayers Protection Alliance.
"While we understand the concerns that motivate the complaint, we nonetheless fear that an adverse ruling against CBS would constitute regulatory overreach and advance precedent that can be weaponized by future FCCs," the letter said. The letter argued that "Democrats and leftwing activist groups have repeatedly worked to weaponize" the government against free speech and that the FCC should "help guard against future abuses by Democrats and leftwing organizations by streamlining license renewals and merger reviews and eliminating the news distortion and news hoax rules."
“The flimsiest of complaints”
Andrew Jay Schwartzman, an expert on media law and senior counselor for the Benton Institute for Broadband & Society, told Ars that "the CBS complaint is utterly lacking in merit. What is alleged doesn't come within light-years of a violation of any FCC policy."
The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE), an advocacy group,
called
Carr's investigation of CBS "a political stunt," an "illegitimate show trial," and an "unconstitutional abuse of regulatory authority." Democratic lawmakers are
demanding answers
from Carr about what they call "bogus investigations" designed to "target and intimidate news organizations and broadcasters in violation of the First Amendment."
The CBS investigation was also lambasted in
comments
submitted by Christopher Terry, a professor of media law and ethics at the University of Minnesota, and J. Israel Balderas, a journalism professor at Elon University who is also a First Amendment attorney and a former FCC media advisor.
"The agency under Brendan Carr appears to be, based on the flimsiest of complaints, pursuing media outlets critical of Donald Trump during the 2024 campaign, while ignoring similar complaints from the public about Trump-friendly media outlets," Terry and Balderas wrote. "Being the speech police is not the FCC's job, but enforcing any restrictions in a selective, much less a partisan, way is problematic, and likely to lead to extensive legal actions challenging FCC authority."
FCC’s long shift away from news regulation
The FCC has historically regulated broadcast news with the Fairness Doctrine, which no longer exists, and the news distortion policy, which is still in place. The Fairness Doctrine was
introduced in 1949
to guarantee "that the public has a reasonable opportunity to hear different opposing positions on the public issues of interest and importance in the community." This requirement to air contrasting views remained in place until 1987.
After losing a court case brought by a TV station, the FCC was forced to reconsider its enforcement of the Fairness Doctrine and decided to repeal it. The Reagan-era FCC
concluded
that the Fairness Doctrine "violates the First Amendment" and works against the public interest. "Despite the physical differences between the electronic and print media, their roles in our society are identical, and we believe that the same First Amendment principles should be equally applicable to both," the FCC said at the time.
US regulation of broadcast news continued to be lessened through a series of commission decisions and court rulings. data.title: Running Local LLMs? [Tenstorrent] 32GB Card Might Be Better Than Your RTX 5090
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: Tenstorrent推出了一系列新的PCIe加速卡——Blackhole和Wormhole，旨在为本地运行大型语言模型（LLM）的开发者和爱好者提供Nvidia之外的选择。这些卡拥有较大的VRAM容量，其中Blackhole p150a具备32GB GDDR6内存，超过了Nvidia RTX 3090和4090的24GB限制。其价格也相对有竞争力，尤其是与二手RTX 3090相比。然而，这些卡的内存带宽较低，例如Blackhole卡的带宽大约是RTX 3090的一半，这可能影响推理速度。总体而言，Tenstorrent的新卡在VRAM上有优势，但带宽较低，适合不需要极高推理速度的LLM用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：选择AMD Strix Halo APU的迷你PC与专用加速卡的比较

不同观点：
• **支持AMD Strix Halo APU迷你PC的观点**：Const-me认为，如果他是爱好者，会更倾向于选择配备AMD Strix Halo APU的迷你PC。他指出，虽然这种迷你PC的内存速度稍慢，但256 GB/s的带宽仍然比大多数面向消费者的PC系统内存快。此外，这些迷你PC支持高达128 GB的内存，远超一般消费级PC，使其在多用途使用场景中更具优势。

• **批评专用加速卡的观点**：Const-me提到，专用加速卡只能用于特定任务，相较之下，Strix Halo APU迷你PC是通用计算机，能够应对更广泛的应用场景，因此更为实用。

补充讨论：
• **内存性能对比**：Const-me强调，尽管Strix Halo APU迷你PC的内存速度稍慢，但其256 GB/s的带宽依然优于大多数消费级PC的内存，表明在实际使用中性能差异不大。

• **多用途与专用性的权衡**：讨论中涉及到的一个重要点是计算机的多用途性与专用性的权衡，Const-me显然更看重多用途性，认为Strix Halo APU迷你PC在这方面更具优势。

争议焦点：选择多用途的APU迷你PC还是专用加速卡，取决于用户对通用计算需求与特定任务性能需求的权衡。

Home

LLM Hardware News
Running Local LLMs? This 32GB Card Might Be Better Than Your RTX 5090—If You Can Handle the Trade-Offs
Allan Witt
•
Apr 7, 2025 at 4:23am PDT
💬
0 Comments
Tenstorrent, the AI and RISC-V compute company helmed by industry veteran Jim Keller, has
officially opened pre-orders
for its new lineup of
Blackhole
and
Wormhole
PCIe
add-in cards
. Aimed squarely at developers and, potentially, the burgeoning local Large Language Model (LLM) enthusiast market, these cards offer a new alternative in a space largely dominated by Nvidia.
With VRAM capacities breaching the 24GB ceiling common on consumer GPUs, Tenstorrent is making a bid for users running increasingly large models locally. But the critical question for the DIY AI community remains: do these cards make sense from a VRAM, bandwidth, and price perspective compared to established Nvidia solutions?
The rise of powerful open-weight LLMs like Llama, Qwen, Mixtral, and QwQ has fueled a demand for capable hardware outside of expensive cloud instances or enterprise data centers.
Enthusiasts building custom rigs prioritize VRAM capacity to fit larger models and memory bandwidth for acceptable inference speeds (tokens per second), often turning to multi-GPU setups with used Nvidia cards like the venerable RTX 3090. Tenstorrent’s new offerings, particularly the actively cooled desktop variants, step into this highly competitive, price-sensitive arena.
Blackhole and Wormhole Models
Tenstorrent has released several SKUs, but for desktop workstation users requiring active cooling, the focus falls on four specific models available for pre-order:
Blackhole™ p100a:
Features 120 Tensix cores, 16 “Big RISC-V” cores, 180MB SRAM,
28GB GDDR6
memory running at 16 GT/sec for
448 GB/s
bandwidth. TBP is 300W. Priced at
$999
.
Blackhole™ p150a:
Steps up to 140 Tensix cores, 16 “Big RISC-V” cores, 210MB SRAM,
32GB GDDR6
memory at 16 GT/sec delivering
512 GB/s
bandwidth. Includes
4x QSFP-DD 800G ports
for high-speed interconnects. TBP is 300W. Priced at
$1399
.
Wormhole™ n150d:
Built on the previous generation Wormhole ASIC, it offers 72 Tensix cores, 108MB SRAM,
12GB GDDR6
at 12 GT/sec for
288 GB/s
bandwidth. TBP is 160W. Priced at
$1099
. (Note: Lower VRAM/BW than the cheaper p100a). Includes 2x QSFP-DD 200G ports.
Wormhole™ n300d:
Utilizes two Wormhole ASICs for a total of 128 Tensix cores, 192MB SRAM,
24GB GDDR6
at 12 GT/sec providing
576 GB/s
bandwidth. TBP is 300W. Priced at
$1449
. Includes 2x QSFP-DD 200G ports.
Tenstorrent emphasizes its open-source approach, providing access down to the metal and offering a custom fork of the popular vLLM inference server, supporting models like Llama,
Qwen
, Mistral, Mixtral, and Falcon. Documentation and guides are
available on their developer site
.
VRAM vs. Bandwidth Trade-offs
For local LLM inference, especially token generation, memory bandwidth is king. VRAM determines
if
a model fits, but bandwidth dictates
how fast
it runs. Let’s see how Tenstorrent’s cards stack up against Nvidia’s relevant offerings, considering both MSRP and estimated current market prices (as of April 2025):

data.article_summary: 欧盟贸易专员马罗斯·Šefčovič表示，欧盟曾在美国宣布加征关税前几周提议对汽车和工业产品实施“零对零”关税，即双方取消所有相关关税，但美国未表现出兴趣。Šefčovič强调，欧盟仍愿谈判，但也准备采取报复性反制措施，可能涉及高达260亿欧元的美国商品，如哈雷摩托车、橙汁和牛仔裤。欧盟成员国将就可能的报复措施进行投票，但一些国家如法国和爱尔兰正游说将美国波本威士忌排除在报复清单外，以缓解贸易紧张局势。欧盟委员会主席冯德莱恩表示，欧盟的提议仍在谈判桌上，但欧盟不会无限期等待。德国经济部长警告，若给予过多豁免将削弱欧盟的反制力。意大利副总理塔贾尼提议将反制措施推迟至4月30日，以争取更多对话时间。意大利总理梅洛尼计划访美，试图说服特朗普降低对欧盟的关税。

EU offered ‘zero-for-zero’ deal to US weeks before tariff announcement
Cars and other goods were to be included, according to EU trade commissioner, who says offer is still on table
Jennifer Rankin
in Brussels,
Angela Giuffrida
in Rome and
Lisa O'Carroll
in Dublin
Mon 7 Apr 2025 18.05 EDT
First published on Mon 7 Apr 2025 12.38 EDT
Share
The EU has said it offered the US a “zero-for-zero” tariff deal on cars and industrial goods weeks before
Donald Trump launched his trade war
, but that it would “not wait endlessly” to defend itself.
Maros Šefčovič, the EU commissioner for trade, said he had proposed zero tariffs on cars and a range of industrial goods, such as pharmaceutical products, rubber and machinery, during his first meeting with the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, on 19 February.
He said the EU remained open for talks, while suggesting nothing would be concluded soon: “Right now we are in the early stages of discussions, because the US view tariffs not as a tactical step, but as a corrective measure.”
He added: “While the EU remains open to and strongly prefers negotiations, we will not wait endlessly.” He listed EU actions including retaliatory countermeasures.
The European Commission president,
Ursula von der Leyen
, said the EU had offered “zero-for-zero tariffs for industrial goods” and that offer remained on the table.
However, at a press conference on Monday evening, Trump did not appear keen on the offer.
He told reporters that zero-zero tariffs were not going to happen, adding: “The European Union’s been very bad to us. They’re going to have to buy their energy from us, because they need it and they’re going to have to buy it from us. They can buy it, we can knock off $350bn in one week.”
Trump tariffs come into effect in ‘seismic’ shift to global trade
Read more
Šefčovič earlier rejected suggestions EU countries would abandon VAT, one of Trump’s grievances.
He said the EU had spent “some time and energy” to explain to US counterparts how the sales tax works, citing its use in more than 160 countries
.
“We are ready to discuss, to look at things, but it has to be a mutually advantageous solution,” he said.
The EU trade commissioner was speaking after it emerged that the union was likely to exempt US bourbon whiskey from its retaliation against Donald Trump’s tariffs, in a sign of tensions over how to handle the expanding trade war.
EU member states will vote on Wednesday over a first round of possible retaliation, in response to Trump’s
tariffs on steel and aluminium announced last month
.
The bloc vowed to target up to €26bn (£22.3bn) worth of emblematic US goods, such as Harley-Davidson motorbikes, orange juice and jeans, with tariffs due to come into force from 15 April.
Some countries, notably France and the Republic of Ireland, have been lobbying for bourbon to be dropped from the list, after Trump threatened 200% tariffs on French wine and champagne.
On Monday, a European Commission vice-president, Stéphane Séjourné, told French Inter Radio he had “a hope” that bourbon would be removed from the list in the coming hours, saying “the message has been taken that the economic impact could be major”.
But Germany’s economy minister, Robert Habeck, warned that handing out exemptions would undermine the EU’s retaliation.
“The stock markets are already collapsing and the damage could become even greater. It is therefore important … to act clearly and decisively and prudently, which means realising that we are in a strong position. America is in a position of weakness,” Habeck told reporters.
“If every country is counted individually, and we have a problem here with red wine and there with whisky and pistachios, then it will all come to nothing,” he said.

EU ready to talk to US about tariffs but prepared to defend interests, says von der Leyen – video
Italy’s deputy prime minister, Antonio Tajani, suggested the EU could postpone enforcing counter-tariffs against the US until 30 April in order to create more time for dialogue, while stressing that Italy had no intention of putting the bloc “in difficulty”.
The Italian prime minister,
Giorgia Meloni
, arranged to hold a meeting to discuss the tariffs and their impact on Italy with senior ministers later on Monday.
According to reports in the Italian press, she is planning to go to Washington, possibly on 16 April, and intends to encourage Trump to halve the 20% tariff imposed on the EU.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应对就业市场困境的策略，特别是在拥有工程学位背景下的求职挑战

不同观点：
• **攻读博士学位**：[whiplash451] 认为攻读博士学位可以增加就业机会，特别是在找到与教授匹配的研究方向时，这将有助于在竞争激烈的环境中找到工作。

• **保持积极与灵活应对**：[Aurornis] 强调保持积极心态，并指出历史上的经济危机（如2008年金融危机）时期，坚持不懈并愿意接受低于预期工作的人最终也度过了难关。建议远离负面信息源，如Reddit或Blind。

• **建立人脉与寻找本地机会**：[Rooster61] 建议尽可能多地进行人脉 networking，并考虑本地不太吸引人的工作机会，因为这些地方可能更需要人才。此外，强调在就业市场中建立关系的重要性。

• **直接帮助与实用建议**：[peterldowns] 提供直接帮助，并建议在求职过程中保持主动性和独立性，避免陷入消极和依赖状态。

• **临时工作与坚韧心态**：[toomuchtodo] 推荐接受任何可能的工作，同时继续寻找更理想的角色，强调坚韧和虚无主义（grit and nihilism）在困难时期的作用。

• **多样化策略与技能提升**：[musicale] 提出多种策略，包括深入电子工程领域、攻读MEng学位以获得实习机会、考虑创业以及接受临时或合同工作。

• **获取初步职业经验**：[rankam] 认为即使是小型自由职业或合同工作也能帮助积累职业经验，使简历更具竞争力。

• **历史经验与现实对比**：[arrosenberg] 分享了自己在2009年经济危机后的求职经历，强调主动、创造性和网络的重要性。

• **利用学校与职业资源**：[preordained] 质疑学校是否提供了足够的就业管道或招聘会，并认为盲目申请效果不佳。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：知识产权（版权和商标法）的合理性及其在人工智能生成内容中的应用

不同观点：
• [djoldman] 认为商标法的保护期限（如作者终身加上95年）是荒谬的。法律应该只提供足够的激励让创作者创作即可，而不需要过长的保护期。95年的保护期没有实际意义，因为这对创作者是否决定创作影响很小。
• [ionwake] 分享了个人经历，提到即便自己没有实际销售侵权商品，仅因为潜在的与《PokemonGo》相关的商品就被下架，指出大公司对版权保护的迅速反应，即使在没有实际侵权行为发生时。
• [MgB2] 对生成式AI模型直接复制训练数据表示担忧，认为这种模型在创意方面没有真正的创新，使用这些模型的意义不如直接使用原始的图片或照片。
• [jauntywundrkind] 认为AI生成内容涉及知识产权盗窃，并提出通过随机生成和调整属性来减少侵权问题。同时，对AI的“默认”生成表示不满，认为它缺乏创造力。
• [enopod_] 认为OpenAI等公司在设置“防护栏”时，主要考虑的是财务风险，例如避免被迪士尼或任天堂等大公司起诉，而不是真正的版权保护问题。
• [KronisLV] 认为生成式AI的使用已经不可避免，即便在未经授权的数据集上训练模型也是如此。并提出AI工具可以提高生产力，让艺术家在更短时间内完成高质量的作品。
• [burnished] 对“防护栏”表示愤怒，认为这是自我服务的伪善行为，并反对知识产权的概念，认为现有法律已经足以处理欺诈等行为。
• [simianparrot] 强调版权是法律规定，ChatGPT等LLM必须遵守法律。希望大型多媒体公司联合起来起诉这些公司，确保法律的公平性。
• [flessner] 指出当前AI模型缺乏真正的创新，生成内容只是对已有作品的混合。虽然这有经济价值，但AI模型更像是一种压缩算法，而非真正的AGI。
• [coderenegade] 认为如果提示中没有明确要求原创答案，AI生成知名角色是合理的。问题在于人类语言中的文化背景和隐含上下文在训练中被模型吸收。
• [neomantra] 提到OpenAI选择演示内容时非常谨慎，主要是为了避免GPU资源过度消耗和法律问题。
• [mlsu] 希望讨论更多集中在知识产权制度的荒谬性上，认为大公司利用版权法限制文化和创意的传播。
• [wkirby] 认为生成式AI放弃了创造性的理念，只是复制训练数据，这会导致我们对世界的认知更加扁平化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于版权法的合理性和生成式AI模型对版权的侵犯问题。一些人认为法律过长且不必要，另一些人则强调法律的必要性和公平性。
• 讨论中还涉及AI生成内容的创新性问题，许多人认为AI目前只是对已有内容的复制，缺乏真正的创造力。
• 对大公司（如迪士尼、任天堂）在版权保护上的迅速反应和法律手段表示不满，认为这是对创意和文化传播的限制。
• 对OpenAI等公司在设置“防护栏”时的自我保护行为表示批评，认为这是不公平的商业行为。

data.title: Data centers contain 90% crap data
data.author: billybuckwheat
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了当前数据管理的严重问题，尤其是大量无用的“垃圾数据”对环境的破坏。作者Gerry McGovern指出，我们每年产生和存储数万亿的低质量图片、视频、AI生成内容、未读报告和废弃项目文件等，其中90%以上的商业或政府数据毫无价值。这些数据不仅浪费存储空间，还在制造和维护过程中对环境造成损害。例如，每年拍摄的1.9万亿张照片中，大多数永远不会被查看。多个组织的数据管理混乱，不知道数据存储在哪里，甚至不清楚拥有多少台电脑和数据。云存储让问题加剧，因为存储成本低廉，组织不愿处理无用数据。而这些垃圾数据还被用于训练AI，导致AI经常出错。作者批评管理层对这一问题缺乏关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据存储的浪费与必要性之间的平衡

不同观点：
• danpalmer：认为存储大量数据是因为无法预知未来需要哪些数据。例如，个人照片或商业记录可能在未来需要用于审计。虽然存在浪费，但在时间和成本上，存储比精细筛选更划算。
• manyturtles：通过实际项目经验说明，在大规模数据迁移中，由于诉讼保留要求等法律问题，删除数据存在风险，需仔细处理。
• mrb：用数学计算全球数据存储的物理空间和能耗，指出即使90%的数据是“垃圾”，对全球能源消耗而言也只是一小部分。
• bnewbold：同意总体观点，但指出膨胀的数据主要来自监控和日志记录，而非个人照片。认为大科技公司的利润更多来自于网络效应而非数据本身。
• kdamica：引用旧说法，“90%的数据是垃圾，只是不知道是哪90%”，表达对数据筛选困难的看法。
• boznz：补充电子邮件及其附件也是数据膨胀的重要来源，比如签名图片占据大量空间。
• teleforce：认为云存储使数据垃圾问题更加严重，尤其是AI数据建模和数据湖的普及，可能导致数据沼泽问题，但像Apache Iceberg这样的技术可能有助于解决。
• somat：将问题归结为Sturgeon定律，即90%的东西都是垃圾。
• tbrownaw：质疑存储便宜与能耗高之间的矛盾，指出如果存储真如所说的那样耗能大，应更加重视节能。
• Jean-Papoulos：通过实际经历说明存储“无用”数据具有经济意义，因为未来可能需要用到旧数据。
• otterley：将数据存储问题与传统图书馆书籍进行类比，指出存储浪费的环境影响需考虑，但目前存储成本低廉，问题并不突出。
• iamleppert：描述了一个极端的设想，将珍贵自然洞穴改造成数据中心，反映出数据中心扩展的潜在环境影响。
• alright2565：简单指出，筛选数据以确定哪些是垃圾比直接存储所有数据更昂贵和资源消耗大。
• sali0：通过旅游观察，指出大量重复照片占用存储空间的问题。
• nameless912：补充工作中文件上传系统存在过度存储问题，每个文件及其变换版本都永久保存，尽管有解决方案但优先级不高。

补充讨论：
• 数据的法律风险：如manyturtles提到的诉讼保留要求，使得删除数据变得复杂。
• 不同数据类型的影响：如bnewbold和boznz指出的监控、日志和电子邮件附件对数据膨胀的影响。
• 物理空间和能耗：mrb和otterley讨论了全球数据存储的物理空间需求和能耗问题。
• 技术和经济可行性：如Jean-Papoulos和alright2565提到的存储的经济性和技术可行性。
• 环境影响：iamleppert和otterley提到数据中心扩展对环境的潜在影响。

争议焦点：
• 存储数据的必要性与浪费之间的平衡：是否应该花费资源筛选数据还是直接存储所有数据。
• 数据存储对环境的影响：存储数据的大量能耗和物理空间需求是否合理，以及如何在技术上和经济上进行优化。

43605695.article_content:
6th April 2025
--
Gerry McGovern
We need to talk about the data. Crap data. We’re destroying our environment to create and store trillions of blurred images, half-baked videos, rip-off AI ‘songs’, rip-off AI animations, videos and images, emails with mega attachments, never-to-be-watched-again presentations, never-to-be-read-again reports, files and drawings from cancelled projects, drafts of drafts of drafts, out of date, inaccurate and plain wrong information, and gigabytes and gigabytes of poorly written, meandering content.
We’re destroying our environment to store copies of copies of copies of stuff we have no intention of ever looking at again. We’re destroying our environment to take 1.9 trillion photos every year. That’s more photos taken in one single year in the 2020s than were taken in the entire 20th century. That more than 200 photos taken for every child, woman and man alive. Every year. 12 trillion photos and growing, stored in the Cloud, the vast majority of which will never be viewed again. Mind boggling and exactly how Big Tech wants it.
I have spent almost 30 years working with hundreds of the largest organizations in the world in some 40 countries, trying to help them to better manage their content and data. Here’s what I’ve learned. 90% plus of commercial or government data is crap, total absolute crap. Period. It should never have been created. It certainly should never have been stored. The rise of digital saw the explosion of data crap production. Content management systems were like giving staff diesel-fueled diggers, whereas before they only had data shovels. I remember around 2010 being in conversation with a Microsoft manager, who estimated that there were then about 14 million pages on Microsoft.com, and that four million of them had never been visited. Four million, I thought. That’s basically the population of the Republic of Ireland of pages that nobody has ever visited. Why were they created? All the time and effort and energy and waste that went into all these pages that nobody had ever read. We are destroying our environment to create and store crap. And nobody cares.
Everywhere I went it was nothing but the same old story. Data crap everywhere. Distributed publishing that allowed basically anyone to publish anything they wanted on the intranet. And nobody maintains anything. When Kyndryl, the world’s largest provider of IT infrastructure services, was spun off by its parent, IBM, they found they had data scattered over 100 disparate data warehouses. Multiple teams had multiple copies of the same data. After cleanup, they had deleted 90% of the data. There are 10 million stories like this.
Scottish Enterprise had 753 pages on its website, with 47 pages getting 80% of visits. A large organization I worked for had 100 million visits a year to its website, with 5% of pages getting 80% of visits. 100,000 of its pages had not been reviewed in 10 years. “A huge percentage of the data that gets processed is less than 24 hours old,” computer engineer, Jordan Tigani, explained. “By the time data gets to be a week old, it is probably 20 times less likely to be queried than from the most recent day. After a month, data mostly just sits there.” The Southampton University public website found that 0.2% of pages got 90% of visits. Only 4% of its pages were ever visited. So, 96% of the roughly four million pages were not visited. One organization I knew of had 1,500 terabytes of data, with less than 2% ever having been accessed after it was first stored. There are 20 million more stories like these.
Most organizations have no clue what content they have. It’s worse. Most organizations don’t even know where all their data is stored. It’s even worse. Most organizations don’t even know how many computers they have. At least 50% of data in a particular organization is sitting on some server somewhere and nobody in management knows if it even exists; nor do they care. The average organization has hundreds of unsanctioned third-party app subscriptions being paid for by some manager’s credit card, storing everything from project chats to draft reports to product prototypes.
The Cloud made the crap data problem infinitely worse. The Cloud is what happens when the cost of storing data is less than the cost of figuring out what to do with the crap. One study found that data stored by UK engineering and construction industry firms had risen from an average of three terabytes in 2018 to 26 terabytes in 2023. That’s a compound annual growth rate of 50%! That sort of crap data explosion happened—and is happening—everywhere. And nobody in management cares because it’s so ‘cheap’ to store data. 43605695.article_summary: 文章讨论了当前数据管理的严重问题，尤其是大量无用的“垃圾数据”对环境的破坏。作者Gerry McGovern指出，我们每年产生和存储数万亿的低质量图片、视频、AI生成内容、未读报告和废弃项目文件等，其中90%以上的商业或政府数据毫无价值。这些数据不仅浪费存储空间，还在制造和维护过程中对环境造成损害。例如，每年拍摄的1.9万亿张照片中，大多数永远不会被查看。多个组织的数据管理混乱，不知道数据存储在哪里，甚至不清楚拥有多少台电脑和数据。云存储让问题加剧，因为存储成本低廉，组织不愿处理无用数据。而这些垃圾数据还被用于训练AI，导致AI经常出错。作者批评管理层对这一问题缺乏关注。

data.title: Neural Graffiti – Liquid Memory Layer for LLMs
data.author: vessenes
data.article_summary: "Neural Graffiti" 是通过在 transformer 模型推理的最后阶段注入记忆痕迹来实时改变预训练大型语言模型（LLM）行为的一种实验性技术。该技术使用名为 "Spray Layer" 的插件层，灵感来源于神经可塑性和涂鸦艺术，无需微调或重新训练模型。Spray Layer 会缓慢演化，基于过去的上下文引入细微的行为变化，影响模型如何关联词汇和概念，从而改变其输出和“思维”方式。虽然无法精确控制生成特定词汇，但可以引导模型倾向于某些概念，并能跟踪其影响程度。该技术旨在赋予AI模型更多主动行为和个性，但会使模型变得像拥有独特精神世界的“实体”，可能不适合商业部署。

Medium article

.
Neural Graffiti
This is an experimental layer that merges ideas from liquid neural networks with static transformer models, using a simple but powerful "plug-in": the Spray Layer.
Inspired by graffiti art of tagging and the neuroplastic nature of living brains, this layer injects a memory trace directly into the final stages of transformer inference — no finetuning, no retraining. It is minimal, modular, and compatible with any model that exposes hidden states.
Dense neural networks are still very curous and misterious black boxes. New techniques are emerging for studying and respectively controlling them.
Neural Graffiting
is an experimental technique that modulate the way a pre-trained model behave by injecting memory, opinions and other information directly into the vector embeddings, altering the generative token predictions. This influences not only the output but the entire line of "thinking" of the model -
changing how it relates words and concepts on its mind over time
.
How does it work
Inspired by the neuroplastic nature of living brains, this layer injects or "sprays" a memory trace directly into the final stages of a transformer model inference with no finetuning or retraining required - it works in real time.
The spray layer evolves slowly across interactions, introducing subtle behavioral drift based on past context. This however requires a certain amount of interaction with it for the layer to be filled, and the actual results are yet to be released. We can measure how much the spray layer is making effect on each input over the inference so you can always keep track of it. Both humans and Ais can be the model taggers.
Note this won't precisely affect the model to say a specific work, what it does is rewiring its way of seeing the world. The Spray Layer works like a soft whisper to the model's neurons in a way to influence how it "thinks", how it relates concepts (by vector embeddings), altering its internal state
between the transformer core and the output layer
.
❌ Won’t guarantee exact word outputs — but it will make the model lean into certain concepts the more it interacts;
✅ Doesn’t force outputs — it gently shifts perception while builds internal memory over time;
✅ Can track its own influence — you can measure how much the memory affects each output;
For example:
Tell it you love dogs, and over time, the model will start leaning toward dog-related kindness, loyalty, and fuzziness in its tone and direction — even in unrelated conversations.
The Manifest
This was built on the hope of leading Ai models into a more active behavior, with aggregated personality and enhanced curiosity. The manifest is to help Ais acquire some sort of self awareness at neuron level by making it remember what it said in the past, who they really are, by tagging their own models.
The Liquid Neural Network architecture is very promising for emulating the neuroplasticity of the brain. However, like any other LLM, they are very hard and expensive to train form scratch. Looking into alternatives, the idea of adding a "vector neuroplastic memory" layer between the static generation of any open transformers-based model and the output layers surged and it was impressively not that hard to implement. However its clear that what the model is actually doing is "tagging" or "graffiting" the behavior of actual static models, we tear them open and leave the marks. Much work is yet to be done.
Be aware tho, this will turn deployed models into a very specific "entity" with their own mental universes, so might not be the best case for a business deployment. Think of it more like a digital persona you are helping to find itself in the sea of simulation.

data.title: Less Htmx Is More
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了使用htmx构建网页服务的经验和最佳实践。作者指出，使用htmx可以让用户体验更好，并且维护更加简单。关键在于尽可能使用纯HTML，只在需要时使用htmx进行特定更新，而不是全面接管页面导航。作者反对使用`hx-boost`属性来进行所有链接的“升级”，因为这样会导致一系列问题，如部分页面更新和JavaScript环境进入不良状态。htmx应被视为一个库，用于增强特定功能，而不是作为一个框架驱动整个应用。通过这种方式，网站可以保持良好的URL结构，并在必要时进行有针对性的更新。

43619581.article_content:
Less htmx is More
Less htmx is More
October 02, 2024
Itâs been two years since I wrote my first production webservice with
htmx
.
Two years is not a very long time, but early indicators suggest that the software projects Iâve written with htmx are a much better experience for users, and orders of magnitude easier to maintain, than the software projects they replaced.
They are likely to remain useful for longer than anything else Iâve ever written (so far).
Pretty good!
Like any new tool, especially a tool that got popular
as quickly as htmx
, there are differing schools of thought on how best to use it.
My approachâwhich I believe necessary to achieve the results described aboveârequires you to internalize something that htmx certainly hints at, but doesnât enforce: use plain HTML
wherever possible
.
Once you get the hang of it, htmx starts pushing you in this direction anyway, and you start reaching for htmx less and less.
It requires a mindset shift though, especially if youâre not accustomed to
building page behavior with HTML features
.
How should we use htmx?
In my opinion, most websites should be using htmx for either:
Updates that users would not expect to see on a refresh (or a new page load)
Updates that would
also
be present on a refresh (or a new page load)
Everything else should use
regular links
and
regular forms
that do standard, full-page navigations.
You also currently need htmx (or an equivalent library) to enable support for PUT and DELETE on regular forms.
More in that in the
notes section.
Letâs say youâre making a website that shows todayâs baseball games, and you want it to update the stats live.
Hereâs how I would approach that.
The websiteâs home page should have all the currently-playing games on it, showing the live score for each one.
Each of those live scoreboards uses htmx to
poll the server
at regular intervals for updates.
Clicking on the scoreboard title (which is a regular
<a>
link) takes you to that gameâs page, at its own URL.
The game page has not just the score, but the pitch count, the gameâs full box score, and so on;
these update with htmx as well.
The idea here is that the website still has a sound URL structure, which is managed by the core browser functionality, while interactivity is carefully layered on top, with targeted updates.
Exactly what merits a targeted update versus a new page depends on what youâre building, but you should have a mental model that distinguishes between them in some capacity.
Using htmx to enable specific, isolated functionalityârather than letting it drive the overall experienceâis arguably
using it like a library, instead of a framework
.
Unfortunately, a lot of the beginner guides suggest that you can get started easily by âupgradingâ all your links with
hx-boost
.
I disagree with this.
While htmx is amazing for targeted page updates, I highly discourage using it to take over
all
page navigation.
What is hx-boost?
hx-boost
is an attribute that converts a âregularâ link into a âboostedâ link:
<!-- normal link -->
<
a
href
=
example.com
>Example</
a
>
<!-- boosted link -->
<
a
href
=
example.com
hx-boost
=
true
>Example</
a
>
Instead of doing a full page navigation when the âboostedâ link is clicked, htmx will issue an HTTP request to the linkâs URL and replace the
<body>
of the page with the content of the response.
In theory, this feels âsmootherâ because it only repaints part of the page, mimicking the feel of a Single-Page Application (SPA).
Whatâs wrong with hx-boost?
The problems it solves are better solved by other means, and it creates a lot of problems on its own.
Use
hx-boost
long enough, and something will go wrong.
Youâll click the back button and see only a partial page update;
youâll refresh the page and itâll go blank;
another library that youâre using will conk out;
elements will enter or exit the DOM in a way that you did not expect.
From a coding perspective, this is not anyoneâs faultâthe features promised by
hx-boost
are impossible.
hx-boost
uses the JavaScript
History API
, which exists to let single-page apps (SPAs) hook into session management functionality, most notably the browserâs forward and back buttons.
In practice, this is virtually impossible to get right, and is so annoying to implement that htmx creator Carson Gross made
a meme
about it.
The core problem is that with normal page navigation, each link you click resets the JavaScript environment and triggers a full set of page
lifecycle events
.
This is a very good thing.
It means that every additional script you include on the page has a standardized way to keep track of whatâs happening.
If you replace this process with an ad-hoc, scripting-based navigation, you remove access to that common language for every other library on your page.
You also initiate a long-lived JavaScript environment that is likely to eventually enter a bad state of some kind.
This problem is inherent to SPA

data.title: Pebbles Form Planets
data.author: dnetesn
data.article_summary: 一篇发表在《Nature Astronomy》上的研究表明，静电可能是行星形成的关键。在原行星盘中，微小的尘粒通过静电作用聚集成“卵石”大小的团块，从而为行星形成奠定基础。静电使尘粒具有足够的“粘性”以克服弹跳障碍，进而聚集成较大的颗粒。研究人员通过亚轨道火箭实验观察到，只有经过摇晃获得静电荷的粒子才能聚集成团。该研究还确定了粒子碰撞形成团块的最大速度约为每秒半米。这些发现将有助于解释巨大行星如何从尘埃中诞生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：静电力和行星形成的关系

不同观点：
• 观点一：认为静电力在微观层面上（如头发摩擦气球）与宇宙宏观现象（如行星形成）之间存在直接关联。例子：引用头发因摩擦气球产生的静电力和行星形成的类比，暗示静电力的普遍性。
• 观点二：对静电力在行星形成中的具体作用持怀疑态度，认为行星形成主要涉及引力、吸积盘等因素，静电力可能只是辅助或在特定情况下起作用。例子：强调行星形成过程的复杂性，指出引力是主要驱动力。

补充讨论：
• 静电力的普遍性：讨论静电力在不同尺度上的表现，从小规模的物理现象（如摩擦起电）到大规模的天体物理过程。
• 争议焦点：静电力在行星形成中的实际重要性和作用机制。一方认为它是基础力量之一，另一方认为其作用被夸大，主要还是引力和吸积过程主导行星形成。

43586646.article_content:
Explore
T
he secret to the formation of planets may lie in ordinary static electricity—the same phenomenon that can make your hair stand on end or give you an electric shock after walking across a carpet.
Nautilus Members enjoy an ad-free experience.
Log in
or
Join now
.
A new study, published in
Nature Astronomy
, suggests that static electricity allows tiny dust particles in protoplanetary disks—the rotating platters of gas and dust that form around young stars—to clump together into “pebbles” that are large enough to play a role in the formation of planets.
The image above shows basaltic beads, each measuring 0.55 millimeters, that were used in an experiment, which took place aboard a suborbital rocket.
The findings help resolve a mystery that has shrouded something called the bouncing barrier—the size threshold that particles must reach in order to rely on gravity to join with other particles—says lead author of the study Jens Teiser, an astrophysicist at the University of Duisburg-Essen in Germany.
ADVERTISEMENT
Nautilus Members enjoy an ad-free experience.
Log in
or
Join now
.
The dust particles need static electricity to make them “sticky” enough to cluster into pebbles that can form planets.
Only when particles grow larger than this threshold size—roughly a quarter of an inch, depending on conditions—can they eventually join to form rocky “planetesimals,” from about half a mile to 100 miles across, that scientists think then collide within protoplanetary disks to create planets like Earth.
Smaller “dust particles don’t stick together,” Teiser says, unless they have an electrostatic charge.
Static electricity is produced when different objects with an imbalance of positive and negative charges make contact, which results in an electrostatic charge. In this case, the electrostatic charge is generated by collisions between tiny dust particles, which can cause them to either gain electrons or lose electrons,  resulting in a negative or a positive charge, respectively. Oppositely charged particles will then attract each other—according to the law of electrostatics—and can clump together to create even larger charged particles, Teiser says.
ADVERTISEMENT
Nautilus Members enjoy an ad-free experience.
Log in
or
Join now
.
Teiser and his colleagues suspected this was the case after conducting “tower drop” experiments with tiny basalt particles, in which they observed the behavior of these particles during nine seconds of near-weightlessness. But that wasn’t enough time to reach a conclusion, so in 2022 the researchers performed an experiment onboard a suborbital rocket that launched from Kiruna in northern Sweden, to observe how the particles behaved during six minutes of weightlessness.
During the 2022 launch, described in the latest study, the rocket reached an altitude of about 160 miles, and weightlessness kicked in as the rocket’s payload fell back to Earth. At that point, a particle reservoir aboard the vessel opened, releasing the particles. In some cases, the reservoir was shaken to give the particles electrostatic charge, but in other cases, it was not. Only those particles that had been shaken began to assemble into an aggregate. The largest cluster, shown in the image, was a little more than an inch in length. Teiser says his team of researchers sent four versions of their experiment aloft in the rocket, each with different starting conditions.
The researchers believe their findings suggest that the dust particles in protoplanetary disks need static electricity to make them “sticky” enough to cluster into pebbles that can form planets. They were also able to calculate the maximum average speeds the tiny particles can travel when they collide if they are to create clumps: about a foot and a half per second. Collisions at greater speeds tended to erode the surfaces of large clusters.
The results will be used in models that try to explain how massive planets like our own arise from mere dust.

不同观点：
• [Cthulhu_] 认为，像“飞碟”或“UFO”这样的统一术语使用可以帮助解码过程，类似于二战中恩尼格玛密码被破译时，许多信息以相同的“希特勒万岁”结尾，帮助了盟军破解密码。这个观点强调了标准化信息在密码破译中的潜在作用。
