Cloudflare acquires Outerbase to expand database and agent developer experience capabilities
2025-04-07
Brandon Strittmatter
Matt Silverlock
5 min read
Iâm thrilled to share that Cloudflare has acquired
Outerbase
. This is such an amazing opportunity for us, and I want to explain how we got here, what weâve built so far, and why we are so excited about becoming part of the Cloudflare team.
Databases are key to building almost any production application: you need to persist state for your users (or agents), be able to query it from a number of different clients, and you want it to be fast. But databases arenât always easy to use: designing a good schema, writing performant queries, creating indexes, and optimizing your access patterns tends to require a lot of experience. Add that to exposing your data through easy-to-grok APIs that make the ârightâ way to do things obvious, a great developer experience (from dashboard to CLI), and wellâ¦ thereâs a lot of work involved.
The Outerbase team is already getting to work on some big changes to how databases (and your data) are viewed, edited, and visualized from within
Workers
, and weâre excited to give you a few sneak peeks into what weâll be landing as we get to work.
Database DX
When we first started Outerbase, we saw how complicated databases could be. Even experienced developers struggled with writing queries, indexing data, and locking down their data. Meanwhile, non-developers often felt locked out and that they couldnât access the data they needed. We believed there had to be a better way. From day one, our goal was to make data accessible to everyone, no matter their skill level. While it started out by simply building a better database interface, it quickly evolved into something much more special.
Outerbase became a platform that helps you manage data in a way that feels natural. You can browse tables, edit rows, and run queries without having to deal with memorizing SQL structure. Even if you do know SQL, you can use Outerbase to dive in deeper and share your knowledge with your team. We also added visualization features so entire teams, both technical and not, could see whatâs happening with their data at a glance. Then, with the growth of AI, we realized we could use it to handle many of the more complicated tasks.
One of our more exciting offerings is Starbase, a SQLite-compatible database built on top of Cloudflareâs
Durable Objects
. Our goal was never to simply wrap a legacy system in a shiny interface; we wanted to make it so easy to get started from day one with nothing, and Cloudflareâs Durable Objects gave us a way to easily manage and spin up databases for anyone who needed one. On top of them, we provided automatic REST APIs, row-level security, WebSocket support for streaming queries, and much more.
1 + 1 = 3
Our collaboration with Cloudflare first started last year, when we introduced a way for developers to import and manage their
D1
databases inside Outerbase. We were impressed with how powerful Cloudflareâs tools are for deploying and scaling applications. As we worked together, we quickly saw how well our missions aligned. Cloudflare was building the infrastructure we wished weâd had when we first started, and we were building the data experience that many Cloudflare developers were asking for. This eventually led to the seemingly obvious decision of Outerbase joining Cloudflare â it just made so much sense.
Going forward, weâll integrate Outerbaseâs core features into Cloudflareâs platform. If youâre a developer using D1 or Durable Objects, youâll start seeing features from Outerbase show up in the Cloudflare dashboard. Expect to see our data explorer for browsing and editing tables, new REST APIs, query editor with type-ahead functionality, real-time data capture, and more of the other tooling weâve been refining over the last couple of years show up inside the Cloudflare dashboard.
As part of this transition, the hosted Outerbase cloud will shut down on October 15, 2025, whichÂ is about six months from now. We know some of you rely on Outerbase as it stands today, so weâre leaving the open-source repositories as they are.
You will still be able to self-host Outerbase if you prefer, and weâll provide guidance on how to do that within your own Cloudflare account. Our main goal will be to ensure that the best parts of Outerbase become part of the Cloudflare developer experience, so you no longer have to make a choice (itâll be obvious!).
Sneak peek
Weâve already done a lot of thinking about how weâre going to bring the best parts of Outerbase into D1, Durable Objects, Workflows, and Agents, and weâre going to a share a little about what will be landing over the course of Q2 2025 as the Outerbase team gets to work.
Specifically, weâll be heads-down focusing on:
Adapting the powerful table viewer and query runner experiences to D1 and Durable Objects (amongst many other things!)

data.author: davidkuennen

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：搜索引擎与AI工具在信息检索中的使用对比

不同观点：
• **支持AI工具（如ChatGPT、Claude）**：
  - [mooreds]：在处理开放性问题时更倾向于使用AI工具，而在明确知道文档存在的情况下使用搜索引擎。
  - [DavidaGinter]：默认使用ChatGPT或Perplexity进行研究，只有在需要快速检查特定公司细节时使用Google。
  - [mohi-kalantari]：认为AI工具更准确且直接，预测Google搜索可能很快会过时。
  - [guillaume8375]：越来越少使用传统搜索引擎，更多使用ChatGPT和Claude，并用Kagi来验证结果或特定搜索。
  - [InfiniteLoup]：几乎所有搜索都通过ChatGPT或Claude完成，仅在搜索Reddit时使用Google。

• **支持搜索引擎（如Google、DDG）**：
  - [lelanthran]：认为在快速扫描关键词时，搜索引擎更快。
  - [austin-cheney]：虽然使用AI工具，但仍主要依赖搜索引擎，特别是在需要长篇解释时。

• **混合使用**：
  - [muzani]：同时使用Google和ChatGPT，Google用于获取多样化结果（如视频、论坛），ChatGPT用于获取简明的步骤指导。
  - [bigomega]：与 peers 一起使用ChatGPT探索新主题，但现在更倾向于在Google中使用Gemini，结合SEO结果和AI摘要。

补充讨论：
• **AI工具的局限性**：
  - [austin-cheney]：AI工具在处理超级边缘案例时表现不佳，甚至与人类一样挣扎。
  - [maxehmookau]：不信任AI工具，因为它们可能编造信息（“幻觉”），且无法完全避免。

• **用户体验和技术趋势**：
  - [bigomega]：提到新设计范式正在出现，内容结果与对话答案正在融合，混合模型正在兴起。
  - [guillaume8375]：指出Google用户基础广泛，改变搜索方式对老用户影响巨大。

争议焦点：
• **AI工具的准确性和可信度**：
  - [maxehmookau]对AI工具的不信任与[DavidaGinter]和[mohi-kalantari]对其的信任形成对比。
  - [muzani]通过实例展示Google搜索结果中的不准确信息，而ChatGPT提供了更实用的指导。

总体来看，讨论围绕搜索引擎与AI工具在不同情境下的优劣，以及未来可能的搜索方式变革。

主要讨论点：BluOS系统的软件更新和硬件兼容性问题

不同观点：
• 支持观点1：更新对系统性能有提升  
   支持者认为，BluOS的软件更新通常会带来性能提升和新功能。例如，有用户提到更新后系统变得更加稳定，并且增加了对新音频格式的支持，提升了整体使用体验。

• 反对观点1：更新导致旧设备不兼容  
   反对者指出，软件更新有时会导致旧设备的不兼容问题。有用户提到他们的旧款Node设备在更新后无法正常使用，表现为无法连接到网络或者出现播放中断的问题。

• 支持观点2：厂商提供良好的客户服务  
   有用户认为，BluOS的开发团队在更新后提供了及时的客户支持，帮助解决了更新引发的问题。例如，有用户提到通过客服获得了替代方案或硬件升级建议。

• 反对观点2：更新过于频繁且缺乏测试  
   有用户批评更新频率过高，并且怀疑更新前是否进行了充分的测试。他们担心每次更新都可能带来新的问题，而不是解决问题。有用户举例说某次更新后音频同步出现问题，影响了观影体验。

• 中立观点1：更新需谨慎，根据需求选择  
   这部分用户持中立态度，建议其他用户根据自身需求决定是否更新。他们认为更新可能对新设备有益，但对旧设备可能存在风险。建议在更新前查看更新日志和用户反馈。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于更新带来的新功能和性能提升是否值得冒兼容性风险。支持者看重创新和提升，反对者则担心旧设备的稳定性和使用寿命。
• 用户普遍希望厂商能够在更新前进行更充分的测试，并提供更详细的更新日志和兼容性说明，以便用户做出明智的选择。
• 有用户建议厂商为旧设备提供长期支持计划，以平衡新功能引入和老用户的使用体验。

   有用户批评更新频率过高，并且怀疑更新前是否进行了充分的测试。他们担心每次更新都可能带来新的问题，而不是解决问题。有用户举例说某次更新后音频同步出现问题，影响了观影体验。

• 中立观点1：更新需谨慎，根据需求选择  
   这部分用户持中立态度，建议其他用户根据自身需求决定是否更新。他们认为更新可能对新设备有益，但对旧设备可能存在风险。建议在更新前查看更新日志和用户反馈。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于更新带来的新功能和性能提升是否值得冒兼容性风险。支持者看重创新和提升，反对者则担心旧设备的稳定性和使用寿命。

The Taliban Hands Over Bagram Air Base to the United States
Zark Shabab
·
Follow

In a surprising development with significant geopolitical implications, the Afghan Taliban has reportedly handed over control of
Bagram Air Base
to the
United States
. Sources on the ground confirm that
U.S. C-17 Globemaster aircraft
have landed at the base, carrying military vehicles, equipment, and reportedly,
senior intelligence personnel
.
According to unverified reports, one of the aircraft is believed to have transported the
Deputy Chief of the CIA
, underscoring the potential intelligence and strategic importance of this renewed presence at Bagram.
A Historic Base with Global Attention
Bagram Air Base, once the largest U.S. military installation in Afghanistan, played a central role in America’s 20-year presence in the country. Following the U.S. military’s withdrawal in August 2021 and the subsequent Taliban takeover, the base remained under Taliban control — symbolizing a sharp turn in the region’s power dynamics.
This recent handover, if confirmed, marks an unprecedented shift in Taliban-U.S. engagement. It raises questions about
behind-the-scenes diplomacy
, potential
counter-terrorism coordination
, and
regional security strategies
.
Strategic or Tactical?
Analysts are divided over the implications of this move:
Strategic Realignment?
Some view this as a potential starting point for
intelligence-sharing
and
counterterrorism cooperation
, especially amid growing concerns over ISIS-K and other extremist elements reemerging in Afghanistan.
Tactical Leverage?
Others interpret the handover as a calculated move by the Taliban to gain
international legitimacy
, unfreeze Afghan assets, or ease
sanctions and restrictions
.
What Comes Next?
The presence of CIA leadership signals that the U.S. is potentially
re-establishing intelligence footholds
in the region. However, official confirmations from Washington or Kabul have yet to be issued, and the
motives, scope, and duration
of this renewed military presence remain unclear.
This development is likely to generate swift reactions from regional powers such as
Russia, China, Iran, and Pakistan
, all of whom closely monitor U.S. activities in Central and South Asia.
The reported return of the U.S. to Bagram Air Base — now seemingly with the cooperation of the Taliban — marks a new and unexpected chapter in Afghan geopolitics. Whether this is a prelude to long-term cooperation or a temporary strategic maneuver, it is bound to reshape narratives around the
U.S.-Taliban dynamic
, global intelligence operations, and the evolving balance of power in the region.

data.title: An underwater volcano just released a million giant eggs–scientists stunned
data.author: jerNils
data.article_summary: 科学家在太平洋温哥华岛附近的海底死火山发现了一个惊人的秘密：一座看似休眠的火山实际上是一个巨大的生物孵化场，成千上万、甚至可能超过一百万的巨型蛋正借助火山热量孵化。这些蛋属于白斑鳐魟，它们利用火山提供的温暖环境加速胚胎发育，这在深海寒冷的环境中极为罕见。该发现不仅揭示了深海生物的适应策略，还强调了保护深海生态系统的重要性。这一罕见的地质与生物交汇点为研究极端环境中的生命提供了独特机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在海底火山发现巨型卵的讨论

不同观点：
• Miraltar认为这些巨型卵来自已知的鳐鱼物种，但强调了卵的尺寸巨大，长达50厘米，暗示这一发现不同寻常，可能具有特殊意义。

• jerNils则描述了这一发现的背景，指出这些卵是在太平洋海底的一座休眠火山附近发现的，并强调了其数量巨大，可能超过一百万，且这些卵依靠火山热量进行孵化。jerNils还提到这个发现让科学家们既兴奋又困惑，暗示这一发现具有重要的科学研究价值。

补充讨论：
• 发现的地点和环境：jerNils指出这些卵是在海底火山附近发现的，这表明特殊的地理和地质条件可能对卵的孵化和物种的生存起到了关键作用。

• 科学意义：jerNils提到科学家对此发现感到兴奋和困惑，暗示这一发现可能挑战现有对海洋生物繁殖和栖息地的理解，可能需要进一步研究来揭示这些巨型卵的真正来源和其背后的生物学机制。

• 尺寸和数量的争议：Miraltar特别强调了卵的尺寸巨大，这可能引发关于这些卵是否真的来自已知物种的讨论，或者是否可能涉及新的或未被发现的物种。

争议焦点：这些巨型卵究竟来自哪种生物，以及它们如何在如此特殊的环境下生存和繁殖，是讨论的主要争议点。这涉及到对海洋生物多样性和生态系统的深入理解。

Far beneath the Pacific Ocean, off the coast of Vancouver Island, a seemingly dormant underwater volcano has revealed a breathtaking secret—one that has left scientists both thrilled and puzzled. What began as a geological survey quickly turned into a remarkable biological discovery: a hidden nursery where thousands—possibly over a million—giant eggs are incubating in the warm embrace of volcanic heat.
A Volcano That Refused to Die
Subscribe to the Glass Almanac YouTube channel
Back in 2019, researchers from Fisheries and Oceans Canada launched a deep-sea mission to explore a 2,000-square-kilometer seamount that rises more than
1,100 meters above the seafloor
. Initially believed to be extinct, the volcano surprised the team by
venting mineral-rich hot water
, a clear sign of ongoing geological activity. This natural heat source has created a rare haven for marine life, especially deep-sea
corals and sponges
.
But the true marvel came when the scientists spotted
white skate rays (Bathyraja spinosissima)
laying eggs in droves across the summit of the volcano—
1.5 kilometers below the surface
.
Subscribe to the Glass Almanac YouTube channel
An Unprecedented Egg Deposit
An underwater volcano just released a million giant eggs—scientists stunned
While deep-sea rays aren’t new to marine biologists, what stunned the team was the
sheer scale
of this reproductive gathering. Based on initial counts and image surveys, experts believe the site could be home to
hundreds of thousands, possibly over a million eggs
—a number that has never before been documented for this species.
What’s even more astounding is the
size of the eggs themselves
. These rays produce egg cases nearly
50 centimeters in length
, resembling soft, curved pillows or even ravioli in shape. That’s massive by marine standards. Producing such
energy-intensive eggs
is a strategy that ensures each embryo has ample nutrients to survive the harsh conditions of the deep sea.
See also
The Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses have just been upgraded: explore three new AI-powered features
Volcanic Warmth: Nature’s Incubator
White skate rays typically dwell between
800 and 2,900 meters deep
, making them difficult to study. But scientists now believe these females may be
strategically using hydrothermal warmth
to speed up embryonic development—a biological shortcut in a cold and slow world. According to marine biologist
Cherisse Du Preez
, incubation in this harsh environment can take up to
four years
, but the residual heat from the volcano may
significantly reduce
that time.
And it’s not just about warmth. The volcano’s summit offers
shallower, more protected terrain
, where vulnerable hatchlings can grow before venturing into deeper, more dangerous waters.
A Living Laboratory for Marine Evolution
This rare convergence of geology and biology offers researchers a one-of-a-kind opportunity to study how
extreme environments influence life
. Just like the vents discovered near the Galápagos years ago, this site proves that even the harshest locations can nurture complex life.
The
adaptive strategy of these rays
—laying large eggs in volcanically active zones—shows an
evolutionary brilliance
that has likely gone undetected for centuries. And while we may never know exactly what other species share this hidden volcano habitat, it’s a strong reminder of how much there still is to explore below the surface.
A Call for Conservation and Curiosity
As the mystery of the million eggs unfolds, it brings with it a renewed urgency to
protect deep-sea ecosystems
. These volcanic oases are fragile, and with deep-sea mining and climate change threatening marine habitats globally, discoveries like this underscore the need for
responsible exploration
and
global cooperation
in preserving what we’ve only just begun to understand.
See also
For an Affordable Yet Powerful CPU/Processor, Go With… (Closed)
This isn’t just a story about a
volcano
or even about a rare marine species. It’s a reminder that the
deep ocean holds secrets
more profound than we can imagine—secrets that challenge our understanding of life and force us to look again at how interconnected our planet truly is.

DNA nanorobots that can alter artificial cells offer a new tool for synthetic biology
by Jutta Witte,
University of Stuttgart
Reconfigurable DNA nanorobots that are working on the surface of synthetic cells. Credit: 2nd Physics Institute, University of Stuttgart
The shape and morphology of a cell play a key role in the biological function. This corresponds to the principle of "form follows function," which is common in modern fields of design and architecture. The transfer of this principle to artificial cells is a challenge in synthetic biology. Advances in DNA nanotechnology now offer promising solutions. They allow the creation of novel transport channels that are large enough to facilitate the passage of therapeutic proteins across cell membranes.
In this emerging field, Prof. Laura Na Liu, Director of the 2nd Physics Institute at the University of Stuttgart and Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research (MPI-FKF), has developed an innovative tool for controlling the shape and permeability of lipid membranes in synthetic cells. These membranes are made up of
lipid bilayers
that enclose an aqueous compartment and serve as simplified models of biological membranes. They are useful for studying membrane dynamics, protein interactions, and lipid behavior.
The work is
published
in
Nature Materials
.
A milestone in the application of DNA nanotechnology
This new tool may pave the way for the creation of functional synthetic cells. The work of Laura Na Liu aims to significantly influence the research and development of new therapies. Liu and her team have succeeded in using signal-dependent DNA nanorobots to enable programmable interactions with synthetic cells.
"This work is a milestone in the application of DNA nanotechnology to regulate cell behavior," Liu says.
The team works with giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs), which are simple, cell-sized structures that mimic living cells. Using DNA nanorobots, the researchers were able to influence the shape and functionality of these synthetic cells.
GUV deformations induced by the conformation change from the s-DRs to e-DRs after adding unlocking DNA strands. b, Control experiment by adding randomly-sequenced DNA strands. Credit:
Nature Materials
(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41563-024-02075-9
New transport channels for proteins and enzymes
DNA nanotechnology is one of Laura Na Liu's main research areas. She is an expert in DNA origami structures—DNA strands that are folded by means of specifically designed shorter DNA sequences, so-called staples. The team of Liu used DNA origami structures as reconfigurable nanorobots that can reversibly change their shape and thereby influence their immediate environment in the micrometer range.
The researchers found that the transformation of these DNA nanorobots can be coupled with the deformation of the GUVs and the formation of synthetic channels in the model GUV membranes. These channels allowed large molecules to pass through the membrane and can be resealed if necessary.
Fully artificial DNA structures for biological environments
"This means that we can use DNA nanorobots to design the shape and configuration of GUVs to enable the formation of transport channels in the membrane," says Prof. Stephan Nussberger, who is a co-author of this work.
"It is extremely exciting that the functional mechanism of the DNA nanorobots on GUVs has no direct biological equivalent in living cells."
The new work raises new questions: Could synthetic platforms—such as DNA nanorobots—be designed with less complexity than their biological counterparts, which would nevertheless function in a biological environment?
Reconfigurable DNA rafts working on lipid membranes. Credit:
Nature Materials
, DOI: 10.1038/s41563-024-02075-9

Understanding disease mechanisms and improving therapies
The new study is an important step in this direction. The system of cross-membrane channels, created by DNA nanorobots, allows efficient passage of certain molecules and substances into the cells. Most importantly, these channels are large and can be programmed to close when needed.
When applied to living cells, this system can facilitate the transportation of therapeutic proteins or enzymes to their targets in the cell. It thus offers new possibilities for the administration of drugs and other therapeutic interventions.

• oersted认为，20世纪中叶之前的地图制作更像是一项工程技术活动，而非单纯的艺术。他指出，精确的海图和陆地地图在航海时代和军事、国家财政中起到了关键作用，且制作和使用这些地图需要高度的技术和资金支持。他不认同将地图制作视为纯粹的艺术，并认为忽视这一历史背景对地图制作理论的讨论是不妥的。
• superfist引用了信息理论中的观点，指出20世纪70年代中期以后，地图学模型变得越来越复杂和流行，导致一些评论者感到被“淹没在科学术语的海洋中”。他强调了地图学理论中跨学科借鉴的现象。
• gryn对2001年的文章表示质疑，认为文章中讨论的内容在现代已经非常普遍，尤其是在GIS相关工具（如QGIS、D3、Mapbox等）广泛应用的情况下，没有提供新的见解。
• chippadoodle同样对2001年的文章表示不感兴趣，提到自那时以来GIS和可视化领域已经有了丰富的发展，并建议关注Wild Bill Bunge的更为激进的工作。

补充讨论：
• 地图制作在历史上的技术性和科学性是讨论的焦点之一，oersted强调了其工程和技术背景，而其他评论者则更关注现代技术工具的应用和理论发展。
• 对于2001年文章的相关性，gryn和chippadoodle都认为该文章没有提供新的或特别有价值的内容，反映了不同时代对地图学理论的不同关注点。
• superfist提到的信息理论跨学科借鉴现象，丰富了关于地图学理论发展和多样性的讨论。

争议焦点：
• 地图制作在历史上的定位：是艺术还是科学/工程。
• 2001年文章的现代相关性和价值，特别是与当前GIS工具和技术相比。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gaussian blur效果的技术实现及其效率比较

不同观点：
• tobr认为文章在技术细节深入之前转向了市场宣传，希望有后续深入技术分析的 follow-up。
• rikroots 提出了使用无限冲激响应（IIR）实现高斯模糊效果的具体方法，引用了IBM的研究和GitHub上的相关代码实现。
• ajb 对文中提到的矢量羽化方法持怀疑态度，认为这种方法可能在计算上并不比滤镜更高效，并指出滤镜计算虽然多但可以通过并行化和卷积定理来优化。
• cjbgkagh 补充说明2D高斯模糊可以通过分离成两次1D卷积来提高速度，从而减轻性能问题。
• zokier 对是否可以通过简单的渐变加偏移实现相同效果表示困惑。
• B1FF_PSUVM 以幽默的方式误解了文中的技术讨论，将其联想到维多利亚时代的历史片段。

补充讨论：
• 关于高斯模糊效果实现的技术细节存在多种方法的讨论，包括IIR、矢量羽化、以及卷积分离等方法。
• 争议焦点在于不同方法的计算效率和实际应用中的性能表现。
• 部分评论者对技术讨论的深度不满意，希望有更详细的技术分析。
• 存在幽默和误解的元素，使得讨论氛围较为轻松。
